title: Mid-stream SSE event interleaving and duplicated tokens when requests route through CDN connection-pooling
body:
Mid-stream SSE event interleaving and duplicated tokens when requests route through CDN connection-pooling

Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running SSE streams intermittently return interleaved token fragments on reconnect when requests are routed through their CDN (FastFront). The client observes duplicated partial tokens and occasional mix of the tail of the previous session with the head of the resumed session, producing corrupt text output.

Impact:
- Several production end-users of Vertex Health experienced corrupted completion text during follow-up prompts in their chat product.
- Customer reports a 3-5% failure rate on streams longer than ~12k tokens, causing manual retries and degraded UX.

Environment:
- Customer: Dedicated account on us-west region; traffic fronted by FastFront CDN with connection pooling and response buffering enabled.
- Redwood serving: rw-inference-13b-quant pinned variant, streaming SSE endpoint (/v1/generate/stream).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Open SSE connection to /v1/generate/stream through FastFront edge in us-west-2.
2) Send prompt that triggers generation > 8k tokens.
3) Simulate mid-stream temporary connectivity hiccup: FastFront probes or a short network blip.
4) Client reconnects and attempts SSE resume using last-event-id header.
5) Observe interleaved and duplicated token fragments in resumed stream.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should continue seamlessly from last emitted token; fragments should not be duplicated or interleaved.

Actual behavior:
- Final few dozen bytes from the pre-disconnect session sometimes reappear prefixed to the resumed session, and in some cases fragments from two sessions arrive interleaved (A-B-A pattern). The client cannot deterministically stitch choices back together.

Immediate customer-provided logs/trace snippets:
- FastFront request logs show backend keepalive probes and upstream connection reuse between sessions.
- Customer captured a sample: "...senti|ment analysis...

... analysis of the input shows" where "analysis" appears split and duplicated across fragments.

Notes:
- Customer is on a dedicated pool and requires low-latency streaming; they cannot disable CDN for production without a staged mitigation plan.
Initial triage by Support (Alyssa): collected request traces, SSE event IDs, and FastFront logs. Observed correlation between occurrence and FastFront keepalive/health probes that close idle upstream connections and immediately reuse the same upstream socket for resumed client connections.

Engineering hypothesis (Marco/Edge team): FastFront's connection-pooling + response buffering is coalescing backend TCP segments during reconnects. When client reconnects and sends resume token (last-event-id), the edge may forward the tail of the prior chunk plus buffered bytes from a reused connection before forwarding new bytes, leading to event boundary overlap. Additionally, gzip-on-the-fly at edge may split SSE boundaries unpredictably when combined with TCP-level reassembly.

Evidence gathered:
- tcpdump from a customer side shows chunk A end + chunk B start arriving in single upstream write after connection reuse.
- Redwood edge-proxy access logs show identical upstream connection id used for two sequential sessions.
- No server-side duplicate write was observed inside the serving runtime: tokenization and write logs show single emission per token.

Temporary reproducer (internal):
- Simulated FastFront config with proxy_buffering=on and keepalive 20s; reproduced interleaving locally with nginx leveling.

Next steps planned:
- Short term: advise customer CDN config changes (see Workaround) and provide a patch to edge-proxy to add explicit SSE flush markers/sequence numbers.
- Medium term: internal change to edge-proxy to disable response buffering for SSE routes and ensure per-session connection affinity or explicit chunk boundary markers to make resume idempotent.
- Track remediation in internal ticket INT-4512 (edge-proxy streaming fixes).

Customer accepted and will test canary this afternoon.

Workaround provided: customer disabled response buffering/proxy buffering for streaming endpoints and adjusted FastFront upstream keepalive to avoid immediate socket reuse. This reduced the failure rate to near-zero in their canary.

Permanent fix plan: edge-proxy change to explicitly tag SSE event boundaries with sequence numbers and to opt-out SSE endpoints from response buffering by default. INT-4512 tracks implementation; PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/789 contains the initial flush-marker prototype.

- Engineering to schedule rollout of streaming boundary markers in next minor release (target 2026-04-02).
- Support to perform a follow-up with Vertex Health after 10% canary completes (owner: Alyssa Chen).

title: Intermittent gRPC channel drops due to edge proxy idle-close causing serving node KV-cache coherence and high tail latency
body:
Intermittent gRPC channel drops due to edge proxy idle-close causing serving node KV-cache coherence and high tail latency

Customer reports intermittent 5xxs and long tail latency for streaming responses from their Private deployment. Errors correlate with long-lived sessions; behavior started after a corporate edge proxy change on the customer side. Initial hypothesis is that the corporate edge/proxy closes idle TCP connections (60s) which causes gRPC streams to drop and the serving runtime to re-establish sessions in a way that temporarily breaks KV cache coherence, producing downstream cache cold-starts and 5xx errors.
1) Deploy private stack with the customer's edge proxy enabled in path (proxy configured with default idle timeout ~60s).
2) Start a long-lived streaming chat session to the hosted model and leave it idle for ~70s,
3) Resume the stream and observe either a client-side gRPC error (CANCELLED/UNAVAILABLE) or higher tail latency on the resumed request,
4) Observe serving node logs for stream reconnect and KV cache eviction/rehydration events.
tcpdump sample: repeated FIN packets from customer-proxy at ~60s idle; gRPC client sees UNAVAILABLE then reconnect. Serving-runtime logs show 'session closed: EOF' followed by 'kv-cache-miss: prefetch-trigger' and a spike in token generation latency. Examples attached in Confluence runbook link.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Support triaged with customer; customer provided tcpdumps and proxy config showing idle-timeout=60s.
2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE reproduced on staging by inserting an HTTP edge that closes idle TCP at 60s; observed identical client disconnect and streaming reinit sequence.
Network capture: client TCP FIN initiated by proxy, server sends FIN-ACK; gRPC connection is not transitioning cleanly to keepalive-based probe - re-establish causes serving-runtime to spin up a new session and reload KV cache state for that model shard.
Serving runtime metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate drops from 98% to 12% on reconnect; token_latency_p95 jumps from 120ms to 1.8s for first few requests after reconnect.
Hypothesis: edge idle-close prevents gRPC keepalive probes from keeping connection alive. The runtime assumes long-lived channels and uses in-memory KV cache warm state tied to a connection lifecycle; abrupt close causes a short window where prefetch/replica warmup hasn't completed, leading to request timeouts and transient 503/504s.
Validated that customer ALB/proxy change coincided with incident start time (change approved 2026-03-09).
SRE reproduced workaround by setting keepalive and lowering KV prefetch dependency; successful mitigation observed.

Benji Morales (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging using a proxy that enforces 60s idle-close. Confirming impact on kv-cache warmup. Working on short-term mitigation and long-term fix.
Customer (Pinebrook Health) 2026-03-10: We rolled a proxy policy last week; happy to revert but need guidance on safe values for production.
Benji Morales 2026-03-11: Short-term mitigation tested: 1) Increase customer proxy idle timeout to >=300s OR enable TCP keepalive/HTTP/2 ping support; 2) Runtime patch to tolerate GOAWAY/FIN and trigger faster warmup with reduced tail latency (PR linked).
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12: Customer applied idle-timeout=360s in staging; errors stopped. Customer agreed to a staged production change after a maintenance window.

Workaround validated and applied: customer increased edge-proxy idle timeout to 360s and enabled gRPC keepalive. This eliminated the immediate disconnects and restored normal kv_cache hit rates. Engineering merged a serving-runtime patch to make KV-cache rehydration asynchronous and resilient to short reconnects (see PR). Planned follow-up: runtime release 0.43.2 with improved warmup + docs for recommended proxy settings for Private deployments.
Create a KB article for customer-run proxy tuning (idle-timeout >= 300s or gRPC ping/keepalive enabled); add a config flag in private-deploy that validates edge/proxy settings on bootstrap; schedule runtime patch rollout in 0.43.2.

title: Conditional Access policy loop prevents admin console unlock after Okta session refresh
body:
Conditional Access policy loop prevents admin console unlock after Okta session refresh

Issue summary:
After Okta session refresh triggered by our short-lived SSO cookie policy, admins attempting to unlock the Redwood Console get redirected into a conditional access evaluation loop and ultimately receive a generic 403 / Access Denied in the console UI.

Impact:
- ~8 administrators across multiple teams unable to access the Console for ~45 minutes during maintenance window.
- Unable to escalate or change role bindings while console access is blocked; delayed incident responses.

Environment:
- Affected environment: prod - us-east
- Identities: corporate Okta org (redwood.okta.com) using device-trust + conditional access policy set (MFA + network restrictions)
- Affected services: Console (web), Okta session refresh hook, Auth proxy (oauth2-proxy variant)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Admin with existing Console session sits idle until Okta short-lived cookie rotation (~30m) triggers session refresh.
2) Console redirects to Okta for re-auth; Okta evaluates conditional access policies that include device trust + recently-rotated endpoint tag.
3) Okta returns a redirect to our auth callback with a state token.
4) Our auth proxy attempts to exchange the state token but receives a 401 from Okta introspection due to a race where the device-trust assertion has not propagated to the session.
5) Proxy triggers another redirect to Okta; Okta starts a new evaluation and repeats step 4, creating a loop.

Observed logs / traces:
- auth-proxy (us-east-1, pod auth-proxy-62): repeated lines: "Failed token introspection: 401 - Device assertion pending" timestamped every 5s.
- Okta logs (audit link):  multiple auth evaluations for user a.patel@redwood.ai with status "MFA_REQUIRED" then "DENIED" then "CHALLENGE" in quick succession.
- Browser console: final error page shows HTTP 403 from console API: "Access Denied - missing session".

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Conditional Access policy coupled with very short cookie rotation creates transient state where device-trust assertion hasn't propagated between Okta's eval path and token introspection endpoints.
- Hypothesis 2: Our auth-proxy does not honor the Okta state token retry TTL and immediately attempts introspection leading to a predictable 401.
- Reproduced consistently in staging with identical Okta policy (see test user test.admin@redwood.ai).
- Correlated with a recent roll (2026-03-09) of the auth-proxy container which introduced a change in how query params are forwarded to Okta (PR referenced above).

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Increased the proxy's Okta introspection retry delay to 10s in runtime with a manual config override — reduced loop frequency but did not fully prevent denial on first refresh for some users.
- Temporarily relaxed the conditional access tag requirement for our admin group in Okta and confirmed normal re-login flow for test users (manual change reverted after validation).

Next steps / action items:
- [Assigned] Liam Chen: Revert the query-param forwarding change from PR 1147 and redeploy auth-proxy canary (ETA: 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC).
- [Assigned] Oncall IAM (Rhea Kapoor): Coordinate with Okta support to confirm that device-trust assertion propagation time is within expected bounds and request workaround flags if available (ETA: 2026-03-13 EOD).
- [Assigned] Aisha Patel: Create a short-term console-level guard to surface a clearer error message and a self-service unlock link for affected admins (ETA: 2026-03-14).

Resolution notes (provisional):
- Reverted auth-proxy change in canary; canary passed smoke tests and no loop observed for 30m in staging.
- Okta confirmed the propagation delay is normal during a high-fanout policy evaluation and suggested adding a 5-10s introspection backoff.

Follow-up / Postmortem items:
- Produce a short postmortem documenting root cause and timeline, include runbook additions to handle short-lived session rotations (owner: SRE).
- Consider extending Okta introspection backoff in default auth-proxy config (owner: platform infra).
- Add a monitoring alert for repeated auth-proxy 401 introspection failures to detect loops earlier.

title: Intermittent graceful fallback after canary weight increase due to slow pin handshake
body:
Intermittent graceful fallback after canary weight increase due to slow pin handshake

Issue summary:
BrightWrite reports intermittent routing to a degraded fallback model immediately after a canary weight increase for a tenant-pinned variant. Impact is visible for a subset of streaming requests (approx 2-4% of requests during bursts) where responses are truncated or have reduced quality.

Impact:
- Customer-visible reduced generation quality and shorter responses for some streaming sessions.
- Occurs shortly after canary weight adjustments or prewarm churn.
- Requests show a short-lived diversion to a fallback model which is explicitly configured as a safety variant.

Timeline / Observed behavior (customer report):
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Customer increased canary weight from 5% to 25% for route /v1/generate with model redwood-open-13b-v2 and pinned sessions.
- 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC: ~2-4% of streaming sessions returned responses that matched fallback quality signature (shorter completions, truncated tokens).
- 2026-03-10 09:18 UTC: Customer opened support chat referencing request IDs and a short snippet of logs.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Tenant with active pinned sessions to redwood-open-13b-v2.
2) Increase canary weight rapidly (e.g., 5% -> 25%) or trigger prewarm across a shard.
3) Drive sustained concurrent streaming requests (50-200 concurrent streams) with persistent connections/keepalives.
4) Observe ~2-4% of sessions routed to redwood-open-13b-compat-fallback for the first few seconds after the weight change.

Logs & Traces collected:
- Edge request IDs: bw-req-20260310-1123xx (sample set provided by customer).
- Edge logs show handshake timeout events: "pin-handshake: timeout=120ms elapsed=201ms", followed by routing decision "route: fallback-variant chosen by graceful-fallback-policy".
- Orchestrator traces show slow commit latency when writing cohort snapshot to control-plane (commit latency spikes 120-300ms during the window).
- No 5xx from serving runtime; explicit intentional fallback chosen by routing logic.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Roll weight back to prior level (5%) and perform a slower ramp (5% -> 10% -> 15% -> 25% with 2–5 min stabilization).
- If immediate relief required, pin the tenant explicitly to the stable variant on the control plane to avoid canary handshake during traffic.

Initial hypothesis:
- The pin handshake timeout is too aggressive relative to control-plane commit latency under a prewarm/autoscale wave. Sessions that do not receive a timely pin confirmation are routed to the safe fallback. A rapid canary weight change combined with prewarm operations causes transient control-plane commit latency that exceeds handshake window.

Next steps (investigation):
- Correlate orchestrator snapshot commit spikes with edge handshake timeouts (SRE).
- Validate whether handshake timeout values are globally configured or per-route.
- Run a controlled repro in staging mimicking canary weight ramp + concurrent streaming.
- Evaluate increasing handshake window or adding short-lived grace period for pinned sessions during weight ramping.

title: Runner secret-cache livelock during bulk key rewrap blocks release cutover
body:
Runner secret-cache livelock during bulk key rewrap blocks release cutover

Issue summary:
During a scheduled bulk KMS rewrap for ephemeral runner credentials, a subset of runners entered a secret-cache livelock where vault-sync repeatedly refreshed secrets but the runner-provisioner refused to mark nodes healthy. This prevented the release cutover job from acquiring the required pool of labeled runners and blocked the production deploy window.

Impact:
- Release cutover delayed for two release pipelines (nightly + hotfix).
- ~18% of ephemeral runner fleet in us-west-2 and 12% in eu-central-1 continuously flapped between REGISTERED and UNHEALTHY, failing job assignment.
- Some long-running jobs were evicted and re-queued, creating billing churn.

Environment:
- prod account (redwood-prod) running 2026-03-10 KMS rewrap job initiated from operations-rotate-key pipeline.
- Runner image v2026.02.1, runner-provisioner v1.14.0, vault-sync v0.9.3.
- Autoscaler policy: conservative-surge with max-unavailable 10%.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Triggered bulk KMS rewrap for ephemeral runner service account keys across regions.
2) vault-sync pushed new wrapped secrets and incremented secret-version labels on k8s Secret objects.
3) Runner pods attempted to fetch new secret; cache layer (runner-provisioner cache) attempted a soft-refresh but observed nonce mismatch with authz-cache table.
4) Provisioner flagged pod as unhealthy and restarted the token renewal flow. vault-sync simultaneously rewrapped again due to perceived failure, renewing secret-version and causing the runner to see a new version mid-refresh.
5) Loop repeated until operator intervention.

Logs / Observations:
- Vault-sync logs (us-west-2): many 2026-03-10T22:14:xx entries "secret rewrap: success version=222->223" followed quickly by retries for same pod IDs.
- Runner-provisioner logs: repeated "cache nonce mismatch, dropping token refresh" followed by "marking runner UNHEALTHY: token-refresh-failed" for same container IDs.
- Authz-cache (redis) had transient high CPU and eviction spikes coincident with the rewrap window.
- Scheduler metrics showed job-assign latency spike to 4.1s (baseline 0.6s) and pending-job queue growth.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: concurrent rewraps + eventual consistency of authz-cache caused the provisioner to observe mixed secret-versions across components and treat that as compromise, triggering aggressive eviction.
- Vault-sync retry/backoff is too eager when secrets appear outdated; it will rewrap again for a pod perceived as failed, which escalates version churn.
- The provisioner cache validates both secret-version and nonce; if versions do not align within a short window, it refuses to accept the token and evicts. The short acceptance window is too tight for our multi-region rewrap choreography.
- Related: similar pattern to INT-30542 (runner deregistered during credentials rotation) but here it manifests as livelock due to compounded rewrap retries across components.

Temporary workaround implemented:
- Paused the rolling rewrap in eu-central-1 and set vault-sync to single-threaded mode for us-west-2.
- Increased provisioner token acceptance window (config toggle) from 5s to 45s as an emergency mitigation to allow reconciliation.
- Manually reconciled ~120 affected pods by forcing a single rewrap and restarting runner-provisioner for the affected node pool.

Resolution plan (short-term):
- Stabilize by rolling a hotfix to vault-sync to add optimistic backoff and a per-pod rewrap gate so we don't rewrap the same pod while a previous refresh is in-flight. Target: vault-sync v0.9.4.
- Roll hotfix to runner-provisioner to make cache-version acceptance window configurable and to add a one-time idempotency token check to tolerate brief version skew. Target: v1.14.1.
- Increase authz-cache resource requests and add Redis persistence tuning to avoid eviction during rotation windows.
- Re-run controlled rotation with feature flags enabling single-region stagger and observability hooks.

Follow-ups and postmortem items:
- Postmortem to be authored once stable with timeline, blame-free root cause, and remediation owner assignments.
- Add automated test that simulates concurrent rewrap + cache skew to CI test harness.
- Update the Release Cutover Checklist to include a secret-rotation readiness gate.
- Consider orchestration change: central coordinator that stages rewraps per runner label instead of region-wide parallel rewraps.

title: Routing heuristics weight skew causing incorrect SLA attribution in daily ops reports
body:
Routing heuristics weight skew causing incorrect SLA attribution in daily ops reports

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 morning, the daily internal SLA attribution report (generated by reporting-pipeline) shows an unexpected 1.8-2.6% shift of P1/P2 tickets from 'on-time' to 'missed' compared to historical baselines. Impact: Internal SLA dashboards and routing summaries used by SRE and Support Ops are reporting skewed attribution; downstream automation that triggers reminders and escalations has sent spurious follow-ups. Environment: prod | us-east; routing-engine v3.4.1; template-indexer v1.9.4; reporting-pipeline v2.7. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run routing simulation against the last 7 days of ticket traffic using current template weights from template-indexer; 2) Compare SLA attribution results against simulation with re-normalized weights; 3) Query template-indexer API /v1/templates?include_weights=true and inspect weight sums. Observed behavior / logs: - template-indexer API returns template weight lists whose sums are not normalized to 1.0 for ~12% of templates. - routing-engine logs show 'applied_weight' values > 1.0 for some routing decisions (examples at /var/log/routing/2026-03-11.log lines 4821-4860). - reporting-pipeline job rp-job-2026-03-11 produced an aggregation warning: "weight_sum_deviation: true" and emitted a note to the metrics index. Suspected recent change: template-indexer v1.9.4 included a config toggle normalize_weights (default expected true) which appears to have been set to false in the production config bundle.

title: Scheduled digest emails: tracehook query param sanitized to trace_hook, causing 404s and missing trace context
body: Scheduled digest emails: tracehook query param sanitized to trace_hook, causing 404s and missing trace context Issue summary: Customers receive scheduled digest emails for dashboard alerts, but the deep links back to the console lose trace context. The tracehook query parameter is being changed from 'tracehook' to 'trace_hook' by the email templating pipeline, and the console rejects the modified parameter, returning a 404 and therefore dropping trace linkage for all triggered alerts in the digest. Impact: - ClarityHealth reports missed trace links on scheduled alert digests for 18 dashboards across two orgs. - Customers cannot jump from an alert email to the associated console view, slowing investigation (support/CS escalation). - Loss of trace context causes SLO/alert correlation gaps for affected routes. Environment: - Prod (us-east) scheduled digest worker: alert-formatter v2.11.4, emailer v1.6.0, console v3.2.1 - Affected orgs: clarity-prod and clarity-staging (org merge history exists) Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a dashboard with an alert that includes a tracehook link (console -> scheduled alert config). 2) Add a high-cardinality route filter (route param in query string) to the scheduled alert. 3) Wait for scheduled digest run (or trigger via POST /api/v1/scheduled-runs). 4) Inspect email HTML body and the alert deep-link URL. Observed behavior: - Link in email HTML: https://console.redwood.dev/org/clarity-prod/dash/123?trace_hook=eyJ... (note underscore) - Clicking link returns console 404 and no tracehook context is attached to the session. Expected behavior: - Link should be: https://console.redwood.dev/org/clarity-prod/dash/123?tracehook=eyJ... and open console with trace context resolved. Preliminary investigation notes: - The email HTML is generated by alert-formatter service which calls the templating helper in emailer. The helper runs a sanitize pass to prevent XSS explosions in customer-supplied strings. - Trace: alert-formatter:v2.11.4 -> emailer:v1.6.0 -> sanitizer:mustache-sanitize@0.9.3 (internal fork). The sanitizer has a normalization rule that converts consecutive alphanumeric segments separated by non-alphanumeric chars into snake_case. In the sanitization step the parameter key 'tracehook' is seen in an interpolated fragment and the sanitizer rewrites it to 'trace_hook'. - Nginx edge and console validate the exact 'tracehook' parameter name; trace_hook is treated as unknown and rejected by the dashboard link handler (403 -> 404 surface). - The behavior was introduced after the sanitizer bump on 2026-02-28 during a templating dependency update. No change to console input validation was done concurrently. Next steps planned: - Short term mitigation: add an edge rewrite rule to map trace_hook -> tracehook for scheduled-digest endpoints in prod/us-east. (Workaround applied 2026-03-11 21:10 UTC for clarity-prod, verified links restored). - Medium term fix: remove the aggressive key-normalization from the sanitizer pipeline for alert URLs and add a whitelist exception for known tracehook keys. Create internal PR to revert or patch sanitizer behavior. - Long term: add automated unit test to alert-formatter/emailer that asserts no query-key rewrite for tracehook and add integration test covering scheduled digest email deep-linking. Related artifacts: - Sample broken email HTML (snippet): View dashboard - Sample expected URL: https://console.redwood.dev/org/clarity-prod/dash/123?tracehook=eyJhbGci... 2026-03-10 09:22 - Hannah Park (Support): Customer reported scheduled digest links 404ing; provided sample email HTML and dashboard IDs. 2026-03-10 11:05 - Ethan Rivera (SRE): Reproduced in prod/us-east by triggering scheduled run. Confirmed parameter name rewrite in email body. Collected emailer and alert-formatter logs (attached to ticket). 2026-03-11 02:40 - Maya Chen (Platform Eng): Verified sanitizer upgrade on 2026-02-28. Locally reproduced sanitizer rule that normalizes 'tracehook' -> 'trace_hook' when parameter is generated via template interpolation. 2026-03-11 20:55 - Ethan Rivera (SRE): Rolled out temporary CDN rewrite mapping trace_hook -> tracehook for scheduled-digest domain on prod/us-east. Customer confirmed links now land on console and trace context restores. 2026-03-12 08:15 - Product (Aisha Patel): Logged follow-up INT ticket to remove normalization rule and add tests. Prioritizing for next minor release. Sanitizer normalizes interpolated keys. Reproducible on local branch of sanitizer. No evidence of console-side change; console correctly enforces expected param name. CDN rewrite is a safe short-term mitigation but brittle for other keys. Need whitelist and tests. Temporary CDN/edge rewrite mapping trace_hook -> tracehook applied in prod/us-east for scheduled-digest host. Customer notified. For customers in other regions, open support ticket to apply region-specific rule if impacted. Mitigation applied (CDN rewrite) and verified on 2026-03-11. Code fix in progress: PR created to patch sanitizer (github.com/redwood/alert-service/pull/7342). INT-9012 tracks removal of aggressive key-normalization and test additions. Change will ship in alert-formatter v2.11.5. - Ensure migration plan in INT-9012 includes a canary and monitoring for scheduled-digest link failures. - Add post-deploy synthetic that triggers a scheduled digest and validates returned email link contains 'tracehook' param exactly. - Communicate to CS and customer once v2.11.5 is released with remediation steps.

title: Heterogeneous GPU mix in dedicated pool causing unfair slot throttling and transient p50 throughput loss
body:
Heterogeneous GPU mix in dedicated pool causing unfair slot throttling and transient p50 throughput loss

Issue summary: BrightCart reported intermittent p50 throughput regressions (20-35% increase) on their dedicated pool during off-peak hours starting 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes for batched generation endpoints, elevated queue depth and fallback routing to lower-tier instances. Environment: BrightCart dedicated pool (heterogeneous GPU mix: some older A10G and newer A100s were present after a recent node re-provision).

Observed behaviour:
- Sudden p50 increase from 120ms -> 160-180ms for batched routes (batch size ~8).
- Autoscaler did not add new nodes for 7-9 minutes despite queue depth crossing the burst threshold.
- Single tenant (BrightCart) saw sustained throughput drop while other tenants on the same pool maintained normal throughput.
- GPU utilization graphs show apparent imbalance: older A10G nodes at 95% with growing NVLink wait spikes; A100 nodes showing lower sustained utilization but higher per-inference latency variance.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Send sustained batched traffic (batch=8, seq_len avg=512) to BrightCart dedicated route for 10 minutes.
2. Observe queue depth and p50/p95 on Redwood Console per-route dashboard.
3. Note autoscaler activity and slot allocation logs in the dedicated cluster.

Logs & links: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/brightcart/dedicated-pool-642981
Slack thread: #support (BrightCart) link t=thread-CLY2345
Instance logs: s3://redwood-logs/brightcart/2026-03-01/throughput/
Relevant tickets: SUP-33489 (slot fragmentation), INT-4123 (scheduler fairness experiment).

Immediate customer impact: Degraded user experience during intermittent windows; BrightCart flagged potential SLA breach and requested mitigation and RCA.
Node inventory check: Maintenance on 2026-02-28 added three A10G nodes into the dedicated pool for capacity; node tagging inconsistency present (missing 'generation' tag on two nodes).
Scheduler logs: affinity_score calculation returned higher packing preference for older nodes for specific tenant CPU/memory footprint. Suspect integer overflow in weight adjustment when GPU_generation tag absent.
Autoscaler behavior: scale decision uses moving average of queue depth over 5 minutes — short burst did not exceed the high-water threshold long enough for immediate scale-out. Consider reducing window or adding spike-detection for dedicated pools.
Serving-runtime traces: on A10G nodes KV cache miss penalty slightly higher for long context; combined with higher tensor core divergence, effective per-batch GPU time increased leading to queue buildup.
Reproduction in lab: mixing a 30% subset of older nodes with batch-heavy tenant traffic reproduced 20-30% p50 regressions in 3/5 runs.
Related code areas: scheduler/packing.go, autoscaler/scale_policy.go, runtime/kernel_selector.cpp (PRs filed).
2026-03-03: Customer applied temporary route pinning to A100-only subset per support instructions — immediate p50 improvement observed.
2026-03-04: Deployed emergency scheduler change to prefer GPUs with 'generation' tag parity with tenant preference; this prevents cross-generation packing for routes with steady batch patterns.
2026-03-04: Short-term autoscaler adjustment applied: enable spike detector that triggers scale-out if queue depth > threshold for two consecutive 30s windows.
2026-03-04: Ops scheduled a tag-cleanup run for the pool to ensure generation metadata is present on all nodes to prevent affinity fallthrough.
Customer confirmation: BrightCart validated restored performance and reopened if regressions recur.
Combination of mixed GPU generations in the dedicated pool and missing node metadata caused the scheduler affinity logic to preferentially pack a batch-heavy tenant onto older GPUs. Older GPUs had higher per-batch execution variance and NVLink wait spikes; autoscaler did not react quickly to the short-lived queue bursts because of a long averaging window. Together these produced transient p50 throughput loss for the tenant.

title: LDAP connector started returning encoded group attribute values; RBAC bindings fail in private deployment
body:
LDAP connector started returning encoded group attribute values; RBAC bindings fail in private deployment

Issue summary: After a vendor upgrade to the LDAP connector, SCIM provisioning began transmitting the group/memberOf attribute values Base64-encoded instead of plain Distinguished Names (DNs). The identity stack's normalization path did not decode the values, so role-to-group mappings in RBAC failed to match, producing widespread 403s for admin users and service accounts.

Impact: Several FinSight admin users and automation service accounts lost administrative access to the private control plane (console and admin API). Customer reports inability to perform tenant admin tasks and manage model rollouts. Incidence started after vendor connector rollout at ~2026-03-01T02:00 UTC.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC) running control-plane v1.8.2, identity-proxy v2.4.5, scim-provisioner v0.14.0. Customer region: us-east-1. Affected tenants: fin_sight_prod.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Authenticate via corporate SSO (LDAP-backed) as a user known to have admin roles.
2) Access /console or call admin API endpoints (e.g., /v1/admin/models).
3) Observe 403 Forbidden for previously-authorized principals.
4) Inspect assertion headers forwarded by identity-proxy (X-User-Groups / X-Assertion-memberOf) and SCIM payloads; values appear Base64-encoded (e.g., "YmFzZV9ncnVwPQ==").

Logs / Observations:
- identity-proxy logs show incoming header X-Assertion-memberOf: "YmFzZV9kbi1vYmplY3Q9RmluU2lnaCxlbnY9ZW50cHA="
- RBAC service chaîne: "no matching role mapping for group 'YmFzZV9kbi1vYmplY3Q='"
- Grafana: spike in 403s from admin endpoints beginning 2026-03-01T02:10 UTC; error trace IDs: trc-4a8b2f, trc-4a8b3c.

Customer-provided artifacts: sample assertion header, SCIM member JSON, and screenshots attached in ticket (customer_claims.json, scim_payload.json).

2026-03-01 13:40 - FinSight (Customer): Vendor indicates they shipped connector v3.2 which intentionally Base64-encodes group strings for transport safety. They can toggle legacy mode on request.
2026-03-02 02:20 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Implemented a temporary RBAC mapping to accept encoded DNs for fin_sight_prod tenant to restore admin access. Verified console access returned for affected admins.
2026-03-03 15:55 - POO (Engineering): Ran a canary of identity-proxy v2.4.6 that includes decode step for memberOf prior to normalization; no regressions observed on canary hosts.
2026-03-04 08:30 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer confirmed functionality restored and performing validation of automation jobs.
Confirmed timeline correlates with vendor connector release at 2026-03-01T02:00 UTC (vendor ticket VEND-4887).
Identity-proxy was not decoding group/memberOf values prior to SCIM normalization or RBAC lookup; code path assumed plain text DN values. See trace in logs and unit test gaps.
Reproduced locally by injecting encoded group header into a staging gateway; RBAC lookup fails because mapping table keys are plain DNs.
Grafana dashboard (dashboards/redwood-auth/403-admin-rate) shows 120x increase in admin 403s at spike time.
Applied short-term mitigation: inserted tenant-scoped mapping to map encoded group tokens to existing role bindings for fin_sight_prod. Restored access without requiring connector rollback.
Longer-term fix implemented in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/789 that decodes Base64 group attributes and normalizes DN values before SCIM mapping. Unit and e2e tests added for encoded group flows.
Runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/IDP-data-normalization-runbook includes steps for toggling allowlist mappings and verifying assertion normalization.
Workaround and permanent fix applied. Short-term: Support created tenant-scoped allowlist mappings for encoded group values and restored admin access for FinSight on 2026-03-02. Permanent: rolled identity-proxy v2.4.6 to customer private control plane on 2026-03-03 (canary then full rollout) which decodes Base64 group attributes and normalizes DNs before RBAC matching. Verified with customer and monitored Grafana for 48h with no recurrence. Follow-up actions: request vendor to add backward-compatible mode in connector, add integration tests, update onboarding docs for private SSO connector expectations, and schedule a postmortem with FinSight.

title: Runner metrics-exporter cert rotation misroutes runner heartbeats causing job stalls
body:
Runner metrics-exporter cert rotation misroutes runner heartbeats causing job stalls

Issue summary: After a scheduled rotation of the metrics-exporter TLS certs (2026-03-09 03:00 UTC), a subset of self-hosted CI runners started to stop reporting heartbeats to the runner-manager and were subsequently evicted from job assignment pools. Impact: Several nightly release and canary builds observed elongated queue times (median queue increase ~4x) and 12% of in-flight ephemeral jobs showed 'runner unreachable' errors. No data exfiltration suspected; operational availability degraded for release windows.

Environment: Production (us-west cluster of self-hosted runners). Metrics exporter sits in front of runner heartbeats to feed autoscaling and health checks. Rotation was performed via automated rotation job (release-eng kubejob) that updated cert secret and restarted metrics-exporter pods.

Observed behavior: After rotation, metrics-exporter started responding with 503 on /heartbeat-proxy for ~30% of runners. The runner-manager incorrectly routed heartbeat traffic to the old cert-bound proxy endpoint due to an in-memory mapping TTL mismatch, causing TLS handshake failures and eventual runner eviction.

Expected behavior: Rotation should update both cert secrets and the in-memory proxy mapping atomically or with a short synchronization window so active runners keep streaming heartbeats uninterrupted.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Deploy rotation job that updates secret "metrics-exporter-cert". 2) Restart metrics-exporter deployment. 3) Observe runner-manager logs for TLS handshake errors and runner disconnects while jobs are active. (Repro rate observed ~30% under steady-state job load).
Trigger automated cert rotation for metrics-exporter secret in prod (simulate via canary namespace).
Restart metrics-exporter pods while 200+ runners are active in the pool.
Observe runner-manager and proxy logs for TLS handshake and routing mismatch errors.
2026-03-09T03:12:41Z runner-manager ERROR tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate (peer=runner-az1-004)
2026-03-09T03:12:43Z metrics-exporter WARN proxymap: stale-mapping-detected key=runner-az1-004 last_update=2026-03-09T02:59:10Z
curl -v https://metrics-proxy.internal/heartbeat-proxy --tlsv1.2 -> SSL: certificate subject mismatch (expected new cert)
Initial hypothesis: cert rotation updated Kubernetes secret and restarted pods but did not flush in-memory proxy mapping used by runner-manager. Evidence: proxymap logs show stale entries with TTL 15m; rotation job updated secret but mapping clean job is a separate cron (30m). Reproduce locally by forcing rotation and checking mapping TTL expiration; confirmed that mappings referencing old endpoint remained for ~18 minutes, during which runner heartbeats failed when leader routing switched to new pods. Secondary hypothesis: load-balancer sticky routing kept some heartbeats pinned to an old pod with rotated cert; however cloud LB logs show round-robin after restart, reducing likelihood.

Related artifacts: linked INT-70123 (ci-runner-permission-lockout-during-credential-rollforward) -- similar timing pattern during bulk rotates; relevant PRs: github.com/redwood/release-tools/pull/412 (rotation job change), github.com/redwood/runner-manager/pull/988 (proxy mapping TTL change proposed). Confluence runbook: "Release cert rotation checklist" updated to note proxymap flush step.
1) Manually trigger proxymap flush job post-rotation: kubectl -n release-eng apply -f proxymap-flush-job.yaml. 2) Temporarily increase proxymap TTL to 1m (reduces window) via deployment env var PROXYMAP_TTL_SECONDS. 3) For immediate recovery, curl each affected metrics-exporter pod to force TLS negotiation and then scale runners by +10% to absorb evicted jobs.

Customer-facing impact: Internal only (no external customers affected), but release pipelines delayed ~30-90 minutes for some teams.

title: Tenant-induced pipeline IO spill causing autoscaler latency and p99 throughput degradation in reserved pool
body:
Tenant-induced pipeline IO spill causing autoscaler latency and p99 throughput degradation in reserved pool

Issue summary: Multiple LexiHealth tenants on reserved capacity experienced sudden p99 throughput regressions and elevated tail latency beginning 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC. Symptoms include stalled batch queues, autoscaler taking 30-90s to react, and error bursts of 502/504 on long streaming requests. Impact: LexiHealth reported degraded user-facing response times for inference flows tied to clinical note summarization, causing timeouts and retries in their app. Timeline: 14:12 UTC spike in IO wait and NVMe device queue depth observed; autoscaler attempted scale-up but new allocations delayed due to slot fragmentation; 14:27 UTC temporary mitigation applied (tenant soft-rate-limit). Hypothesis: A noisy tenant generated high small-request fanout (many short streams) that induced storage-io pressure on the node local NVMe, which cascaded into serving runtime stalls and autoscaler misjudging available capacity leading to delayed allocations and p99 throughput loss. Next steps: continue root-cause data collection (iostat, container-level io stats), validate autoscaler sampling windows, and evaluate a short-term tenant-level soft cap plus scheduler affinity tweak.
Customer production traffic experiencing p99 latency increases from ~1.1s to ~7-12s on long-context streaming endpoints and increased 5xx rate (~4% of requests). Business impact: customer-facing app timeouts and retries affecting clinical workflows for a subset of users.
1) Route sustained small (<=128 token) streaming requests from many concurrent clients (1000+ short streams) to a single reserved pool with mixed tenant placement.
2) Observe NVMe device queue depth and host-level i/o util increase in affected nodes.
3) Watch batcher queues grow and p99 token latency climb; autoscaler logs show scale decision but allocation delayed due to fragmented GPU slot availability.
4) Reproduce with isolated synthetic load in staging by replaying LexiHealth request trace (attached).
2026-03-10T14:12:34Z node-az1-03 iostat: avg-cpu: %iowait=34.6, util=92
2026-03-10T14:13:01Z serving-runtime[pid:8421]: batcher: enqueue_wait_ms=1200, current_batch_size=2
2026-03-10T14:13:07Z scheduler: allocation_delay=45s, reason=slot-fragmentation
2026-03-10T14:14:10Z autoscaler: decision=scale_up, requested_gpus=2, allocated=0 (pending)
Checked node metrics: affected hosts show NVMe write queue saturated and high iowait correlated with request spikes.
Correlation found between many short streaming sessions from a single tenant and NVMe random I/O spike (small writes for logging/checkpointing in sidecars).
Autoscaler sampling window (30s) + allocation TPS limits caused scale decisions to be queued; combined with GPU slot fragmentation, allocations were delayed 30-90s.
No kernel panic or driver OOM; memory usage normal. Evidence of a background sidecar on tenant containers performing frequent small fsyncs during request processing.
Heatmap from 2026-03-10 14:00-14:30 UTC attached in Confluence (see link).
Ava Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported p99 jump at 14:15 UTC. Escalating to SRE and Dedicated infra on-call.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Observed NVMe queue spike on nodes hosting LexiHealth shards. Kicking off node-level io captures and sampling container io stats.
Maya Patel (Infra Eng) 2026-03-11: Identified a LexiHealth sidecar that writes frequent small checkpoints. Requesting customer to temporarily disable sidecar while we test scheduler affinity change.

Mitigation applied: (1) Tenant soft-rate-limit deployed for LexiHealth at 2026-03-11 15:02 UTC, (2) temporary +1 GPU reservation added to affected pool, (3) customer disabled sidecar during mitigation window. Result: p99 latency reduced from ~10s to ~1.4s and 5xx dropped below 0.5%. Permanent fix path: implement scheduler placement preference to avoid collocating high-small-io tenants, add per-tenant burst IO throttling at node-local level, and adjust autoscaler to consider IO wait metrics when deciding scaling. title: Affinity-token TTL expiry causes pinned session to fall back during weight rebalance
body:
Affinity-token TTL expiry causes pinned session to fall back during weight rebalance

Issue summary: During a controlled canary weight adjustment for redwood/gpt-4s-8k in us-east we observed a subset of customer LumenAI sessions that were pinned to a specific model version drop affinity and route to a fallback model. Impact: customer-facing inference latencies increased and a small percentage of responses returned from fallback model variant (quantized), causing quality degradation for 2% of requests for a 35-minute window. Environment: prod-us-east, serving clusters behind router-3 and cache-tier A.

Observed behavior: When the canary weight rebalance job applied incremental weight changes, sessions with pinned-version affinity tokens that were near TTL expiry had their routing affinity evaluated mid-update. Affinity token refresh failed for those sessions due to race with router reconfiguration; the routing decision fell through to fallback routing and the requests were served by the quantized fallback model.

Expected behavior: Pinned sessions should preserve model binding through atomic weight updates or refresh their affinity tokens before re-routing to avoid transient fallback.

Impact statement: Affected customer LumenAI (dedicated) reported increased errors in production monitors and downgraded quality for a critical ranking flow. No data leak; only routing/quality impact.
1) Create a dedicated session pinned to redwood/gpt-4s-8k with affinity token TTL set to default (30s).
2) Start steady traffic from the session (50 qps) routed through router-3 in us-east.
3) Trigger a canary weight rebalance job that updates weights in multiple small increments over 2 minutes.
4) Observe session-level routing decisions in router logs; note tokens that expire mid-rebalance and fallback routing entries.
Initial hypothesis: affinity token TTL too short relative to weight rebalance window and router reconfiguration touches token refresh path. We reproduced locally by shortening TTL to 5s and running a multi-step weight update; observed identical behavior. Root cause: router applies weight updates by streaming route diffs which can race with the affinity refresh path; small-ttl tokens that are validated during the reconfiguration were treated as expired and not refreshed due to a lock contention bug in router-3. A secondary factor: the fallback routing path does not re-check for immediate rebind once token refresh completes (non-idempotent path). Traces and heap profiles attached in PR.
2026-03-10T14:22:03Z router-3 INFO routing decision session=abcd1234 pin=redwood/gpt-4s-8k token_ttl=3s -> token-expired -> fallback-route=redwood/gpt-4s-8k-quant
2026-03-10T14:22:05Z cache-A WARN affinity-refresh session=abcd1234 attempt=1 err=timeout
2026-03-10T14:47:12Z autoscaler INFO canary-rebalance start weights {stable:0.9, canary:0.1} -> {stable:0.85, canary:0.15} steps=5
2026-03-10T15:03:11Z - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reported ~2% of requests routed to quantized fallback during canary update window. Collected request IDs, logs, and session tokens. Escalating to infra/SRE.
2026-03-10T16:05:42Z - SRE (Diego Martinez): Reproduced in staging by shrinking affinity TTL to 5s. Router-3 shows lock wait spikes when applying weight diffs. Suspect reconfiguration ordering + token refresh race.
2026-03-10T18:12:00Z - Runtime (Priya Nair): Confirmed fallback path does not rebind the session once token refresh resolves. Preparing a minimal patch to make token refresh take precedence and to make weight updates apply atomically per-session where pinned.
2026-03-11T09:22:30Z - Support (Maya Chen): Communicated temporary mitigation to customer: avoid rolling weight changes during peak windows and increase session token TTL via API (recommended 5m) until fix is deployed.
2026-03-12T02:47:05Z - Deploy (Diego Martinez): Patch merged (infra PR #8321, runtime PR #1290). Deployed router hotfix to prod-us-east with canary at 10% then 100%. Monitoring shows no further pin-drop events in the 6h observation window.
Fix deployed: (1) Router weight reconfiguration now acquires a lightweight session-affinity guard to avoid racing with token refresh; (2) Fallback path updated to re-evaluate token refresh completion before finalizing routing decision; (3) Default affinity-token TTL increased from 30s to 5m for dedicated sessions by safe-config rollout. Customer mitigation: recommended TTL bump for critical sessions while we rolled the fix. Post-deploy verification: 6h of traffic with LumenAI showed zero recurrence. Follow-up: add unit/integration tests for atomic weight update behavior (ticket INT-21042) and a monitoring alert for sudden rise in fallback ratio during rollouts.
1) Add automated integration test covering affinity refresh vs weight reconfiguration.
2) Instrument router to emit metrics on token-refresh vs routing-finalize latency.
3) Update runbook: require a pre-check for token-liveness before multi-step weight updates for dedicated customers.
4) Notify platform customers via changelog about affinity TTL increase and guidance for custom TTL settings.

title: Buildkite CI unable to impersonate GCP Workload Identity for prod bucket reads during nightly migration
body:
Buildkite CI unable to impersonate GCP Workload Identity for prod bucket reads during nightly migration

Issue summary:
Buildkite CI jobs running in prod are failing to access GCS bucket gs://redwood-prod-model-checkpoints during the nightly model migration. The failure started after we tightened org-level IAM policies last week (policy rollout noted in infra PR #2187).

Impact:
- Nightly migration jobs failing ~100% blocking model checkpoint copy and delaying deployments.
- Downstream inference stacks that rely on fresh checkpoints risk stale models if migration isn't complete.
- Security team flagged this as needing an SR for audit evidence (potential policy regression).

Environment:
- Project: redwood-prod (GCP org: redwood-ai)
- Region: us-central1
- CI: Buildkite (self-hosted runners in GKE prod pool)
- Affected bucket: gs://redwood-prod-model-checkpoints

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger nightly migration pipeline (pipeline: model-migration-nightly).
2) Observe Buildkite job that runs `gsutil cp` to the prod bucket.
3) Job fails with 403 when runner attempts to impersonate service account via Workload Identity.

Expected behavior:
- Runner should successfully exchange Kubernetes service account token for GCP service account credentials (Workload Identity) and read/write to bucket.

Actual behavior / Error excerpts:
- Buildkite job logs show: "StorageException: 403 Forbidden" followed by "Request had insufficient authentication scopes" and an error from IAM: "caller does not have iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken permission".
- Example log snippet (sanitized):
  2026-03-09T23:02:13Z ERROR: StorageException: 403 Forbidden
  2026-03-09T23:02:13Z DEBUG: Token exchange failure: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied for serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Business impact / urgency:
- Nightly migration is critical for test/validation; if not resolved before Monday release window, release may be delayed. Security requires documented remediation steps.

Initial hypothesis:
- Org policy or newly applied IAM Conditions removed or restricted iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken for the impersonation principal (KSA->GSA mapping).
- Possible mismatch in KSA annotation (workload identity) after cluster upgrade or CI runner config drift.

Found recently applied constraint 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' restricting members to 'redwood-ai.com' only; Workload Identity member format serviceAccount:redwood-prod.svc.id.goog[...] is not a domain-bound member and may be implicitly blocked by a restrictive condition on the binding.
- Concluded the org-level constraint added in PR #2187 could be too restrictive for Workload Identity members.
Reproduced locally: Using a k8s token and calling iamcredentials.generateAccessToken via gcloud returned PERMISSION_DENIED unless executed by infra-admin account. Suggests a deny at org level or a conditional binding requiring a particular tag/attribute.
Planned remediation (in collaboration with Security):
1) Narrow rollback of the org-level constraint applied in infra PR #2187 to exempt Workload Identity member format (serviceAccount:<project>.svc.id.goog[...]) OR add an explicit allow binding for the specific KSA->GSA mapping.
2) Implement a temporary, auditable exception for the model-migration-nightly pipeline: grant roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on ci-runner@redwood-prod to the CI KSA via an explicitly-scoped binding valid for 48 hours.
3) After migration completes, replace the temporary binding with a least-privilege condition that restricts impersonation to the runner pod identity + time window.
4) Update Confluence runbook with checklist for Workload Identity changes and include an automated policy test in CI that validates token exchange.
Owners: Diego (SRE) to implement above steps; Maya (Security) to approve exceptions and verify audit events.

Infra team: schedule a short retro to discuss org policy rollout checklist to avoid future accidental blocks.

title: Relocation mid-probation: hardware handback vs local issuance, KMS rekey and SSO group changes for APAC transfer
body:
Relocation mid-probation: hardware handback vs local issuance, KMS rekey and SSO group changes for APAC transfer

Issue summary: Senior Data Engineer (internal headcount) has requested permanent relocation from US to APAC office mid-probation (start date 2026-02-02). HR needs guidance on whether to require return of company laptop (MacBook Pro M1) shipped to US or allow device to remain with employee and provision a new APAC-managed device. Request also asks for KMS/HSM key custody plan and SSO/SCIM group mapping changes so that user appears in APAC org unit without duplicate accounts.

Impact: Decisions will affect compliance (local import/export/tax reporting), KMS key material residency, license seat accounting, and security posture if device remains outside original region. Employee is handling customer data classified as Confidential; we must ensure no residual US-only secrets remain accessible.

Background: HR and hiring manager prefer minimal disruption and would like to avoid international courier return if policy allows. Security & Compliance flagged need to rotate encrypted volumes, service account tokens, and re-enroll device in regional MDM. Current SCIM sync shows duplicate person record during test move (observed 2026-03-09).

title: Client certificate chain ordering accepted by edge proxy but yields wrong subject -> service account impersonation fails in private VPC
body:
Client certificate chain ordering accepted by edge proxy but yields wrong subject -> service account impersonation fails in private VPC

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after rotating a service account client certificate in their private VPC, scheduled workers and admin impersonation calls started failing with 403s. The certificate upload process accepted the provided chain (end-entity cert + intermediate) but Redwood's identity proxy appears to map the request to the wrong service principal during mTLS subject extraction.

Impact:
- Multiple scheduled jobs (service-account impersonation) failing to call Redwood admin API in production (DataForge tenant).
- Customer-facing automation degraded: hourly ingestion jobs missing for ~6 hours.
- No token exchange logs for the expected principal; access denied responses returned.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in us-east; customer-managed edge proxy sits in front of Redwood private ingress.
- Identity proxy version: 1.14.3 (private image), OpenSSL 1.1.1k on proxy host.
- Customer rotated certificate via their internal CA and uploaded a concatenated certificate file (leaf followed by intermediate).

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Upload client certificate bundle with end-entity cert first followed by intermediate cert to their on-prem SSO gateway (same bundle they use for mTLS).
2) Trigger admin impersonation endpoint (POST /v1/admin/impersonate) using mutual TLS client auth.
3) Observe 403 response from Redwood with no token issued to expected service account.

Observed behavior:
- Edge proxy TLS logs show a successful mTLS handshake but identity-proxy logs the client subject as "CN=old-service-account,OU=other,O=example" instead of the expected "CN=dataforge-svc-ingest,OU=svcaccounts,O=dataforge".
- Handshake excerpts include the peer certificates in transmitted order (leaf, intermediate).
- Identity proxy chooses the first certificate present in the chain for subject extraction when chain order is non-canonical.

Expected behavior:
- Identity proxy should canonicalize and validate the full chain, then extract the correct subject corresponding to the leaf certificate for impersonation mapping.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- identity-proxy: "mtls: peer certs count=2; using cert index=0 subject=CN=old-service-account,..."
- auth-proxy: "impersonation: mapping lookup failed for subject=CN=old-service-account -> mapping not found"
- customer-provided tcpdump/pcap shows TLS ClientHello and Certificate messages where certificates are concatenated leaf->intermediate.

Additional notes:
- Customer says their previous cert bundle uploads (with intermediate first) worked fine; their CA tooling appears to emit varying chain orders depending on packaging.
- Customer provided the exact PEM bundle and a PKI toolchain trace via secure share.
2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Ava Ramirez): Opened ticket after customer provided failure traces and their PEM bundle. Customer reports ~6 hours of job failures and attached pcap and cert files.
2026-03-10 11:03 - Support (Ava Ramirez): Confirmed production impact; set priority to P1 and paged SRE on-call (Liam Chen). Requested exact identity-proxy logs and docker image digest.
2026-03-10 12:20 - SRE (Liam Chen): Retrieved logs from private instance (identity-proxy 1.14.3). Observed subject mismatch and that proxy selected cert index 0 from chain. Attached log excerpt to ticket.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Customer (DataForge admin): Provided original CA packaging steps; said their packaging tool sometimes emits leaf-first bundles after rotation. Shared link to secure artifact store.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Eng (Nora Patel): Reproduced locally with OpenSSL 1.1.1k + haproxy; confirmed that when presented leaf-first chain, the proxy library returned certs in transmitted order and our code was extracting subject from index 0 without verifying canonicalization.
2026-03-11 13:30 - Support (Liam Chen): Provided temporary workaround to customer: re-upload bundle with canonical order (intermediate then leaf) and restart their edge proxy process. Customer applied workaround and reported scheduled jobs resumed.
2026-03-12 10:15 - Eng (Nora Patel): Created PR to normalize chain order in identity-proxy and to fallback to verified leaf cert when mapping fails (see PR 2045). Marked as hotfix candidate for next private patch release.
2026-03-12 15:50 - Support (Ava Ramirez): Confirmed with customer that workaround is effective and asked for permission to schedule validation run during low-traffic window for patch rollout. Customer agreed.
Initial hypothesis: rotation created a new subject that wasn't mapped. Reproduced failure without mapping issue — mapping existed but subject extracted differed.
Reproduction: local test with haproxy + identity-proxy shows OpenSSL hands certs to userland in the order transmitted by client; code assumed canonical order and used cert[0] as leaf.
Root cause: identity-proxy extracted the subject from the first certificate in the presented chain without canonicalizing/validating which cert is the end-entity. Some CA tooling emits end-entity first which flips the order and leads to extracting an intermediate or previous cert when multiple certs are concatenated incorrectly.
Risk assessment: High for private deployments where customers control the edge packaging process. Can cause broad impersonation failures for scheduled workers and automation that rely on client cert identity.
Short-term mitigation: instruct customers to provide a canonical bundle (leaf last / intermediate first) and restart edge process. Documented in runbook linked above.
Long-term fix: normalize chain order inside identity-proxy, validate chain, and prefer the verified leaf cert for subject extraction. PR created and targeted for next patch release (hotfix path available for severely impacted customers).
Related internal work: INT-4012 created to track rollout automation for private tenants and to add test vectors for different chain orders in CI.
Workaround applied: DataForge re-uploaded the certificate bundle with canonical order (intermediates first, leaf last) and restarted their edge proxy; scheduled jobs resumed. Engineering implemented a normalization and verification patch (PR 2045) to ensure identity-proxy derives the subject from the verified leaf even when clients present chains in arbitrary order. Patch queued for private hotfix release 1.14.4. Follow-up: schedule validation window with customer and add chain-order tests to CI.

title: SSE session: CORS preflight teardown leads to silent final-fragment split and incomplete terminal output
body:
SSE session: CORS preflight teardown leads to silent final-fragment split and incomplete terminal output

Customer reports intermittent loss of final text and abrupt SSE session termination when their browser issues a CORS preflight OPTIONS request concurrently with an active server-sent events stream. Symptoms: the stream ends without the final JSON metadata block and the last sentence is truncated. This appears correlated with CDN/edge preflight probes that reuse/tear down the underlying HTTP/2 connection mid-flight.
Some production users of DocuStream's editor see incomplete paragraphs or missing final bullets in streamed completions. Affects ~0.3% of long-streaming requests for the customer; they are enterprise-tier and rely on deterministic document completion for legal drafting flows.
1) From a browser behind a corporate CDN and strict CORS policy, open a long SSE generation session to /v1/streams with a prompt that generates multi-paragraph output.
2) Trigger a concurrent OPTIONS preflight for the same origin (simulate with a periodic metrics probe or set up an external CDN that fires preflight probes).
3) Observe that the SSE connection receives several final data chunks but the terminal 'end' JSON metadata is missing and the final sentence is cut mid-word.
4) Reproduce rate increases if preflight interval overlaps with streaming windows (0.5–2s probes).
Edge proxy access logs (edge/prod/us-east/2026-03-09-14:23:xx): shows OPTIONS 200 followed by TCP FIN on h2 connection id 0x7f2ab
API gateway trace: request_id=rs-98a1cdf streaming duration 18.4s, saw http2 RST_STREAM from upstream immediately after preflight probe at t+16.9s
Serving runtime debug: session_id=svc-3421, last_kv_seq=8423, no explicit session end recorded; worker observed partial choice state and evicted connection
Client capture (customer): browser console network log and raw SSE frames excerpt (trimmed)
Initial hypothesis: CORS preflight OPTIONS triggered by the CDN/enterprise WAF reuses the same HTTP/2 connection and causes a half-close or stream reset. The server runtime relies on implicit connection close to emit final metadata; when the connection is torn down by an upstream preflight, the final JSON envelope doesn't flush. Reproduced in our staging environment by adding an OPTIONS probe against the same connection: observed identical mid-stream RST_STREAM and missing terminal metadata.
1) Customer can disable aggressive preflight probes on their CDN/enterprise WAF for streaming endpoints as a stopgap.
2) Recommend using WebSocket fallback for long-running streams from behind strict CDNs.
3) As a client-side mitigation, buffer partial stream client-side until a short inactivity timer (e.g., 400ms) elapses before treating stream as finalized. Not ideal for real-time UX but reduces visible truncation.

title: Stream snap-gap produces half-formed JSON blocks and idle tail when client reattaches behind corp proxy
body:
Stream snap-gap produces half-formed JSON blocks and idle tail when client reattaches behind corp proxy

Issue summary:
Customer (Orbis Analytics) reports repeats of short-lived connection drops (~400-800ms) when users on a specific corporate network (behind an enterprise WAF/proxy) interact with our streaming endpoint. After the client reattaches the stream, the payload occasionally contains half-formed JSON objects (truncated mid-object) followed by an idle tail: no further events are delivered even though the model is still producing tokens.

Impact:
- Several customers reported partial outputs in final responses (missing closing braces/arrays) which prevents downstream JSON parsing in their ingestion pipeline, causing job failures and retries.
- Affects ~3% of streaming sessions originating from Orbis's corp network during peak hours. Customer is enterprise and using dedicated-plan traffic routing.

Environment:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/stream/chat (SSE) and ws://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/chat (websocket fallback)
- Region: prod us-west-2
- Customer network: corporate WAF + transparent proxy that injects keepalive and performs TLS termination (device: Akamai WAF in front of customer edge).
- Client SDK: Orbis internal JS wrapper v2.4.1 (they reported no client-side parsing errors before network flap).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer and validated locally):
1. From Orbis corp network, initiate an SSE stream with a long-running completion (expected > 90s of token stream).
2. Introduce a short network micro-drop (simulate by briefly blocking outbound on client for ~600ms) or allow the WAF to probe and reestablish the connection.
3. Client reconnects and resumes using the same session token/stream id.
4. Observe the first resumed chunks: occasionally a chunk ends mid-JSON-object. After that, no final 'end' event is observed and the stream remains silent while the server-side model continues to generate (confirmed via internal tracing).

Observed behavior:
- Partial JSON chunk delivered (e.g., ends in '"content":"..."' or ""choices": [ { "index": 0, "delta": {"content": "incomp" } ] ) where trailing brace/closing array is missing.
- Client-side parser throws a SyntaxError and usually falls back to retry logic; some Orbis jobs treat this as irrecoverable and mark records as failed.
- Server traces (trace IDs below) indicate the model completed and server-side terminal metadata was emitted, but the terminal event did not arrive at the client path due to an intermediate stream fragment being dropped or not closed by the proxy handshake.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- Example trace IDs: trace-usw-20260312-8642, trace-usw-20260312-8721.
- Raw SSE chunk capture (s3): s3://support-artifacts/Orbis/2026-03-12/partial-chunk-8642.txt
- Customer pcap (provided): orbis_pcap_20260312.pcap (contains the short TCP close/fin seen from the WAF at time of snapshot).

Initial triage notes (Support):
- Reproduced locally using a simple local reverse proxy that performs a mid-chunk RST: when the proxy cuts the stream mid-chunk and allows client to reconnect quickly, client-side JSON is left incomplete and our resume logic delivers prefix replays that do not include a closing terminal event.
- Hypothesis 1: Transparent proxy performs buffering and re-chunking that splits our JSON token boundaries; on reconnection our resume handshake's last-ack alignment does not map to the proxy's buffered stream, causing the proxy to drop remaining terminal bytes.
- Hypothesis 2: When connection is re-established, our streaming mux assigns a new worker; the worker's reattach code path merges cached prefix with fresh tail but drops finalizer metadata when earlier fragment flagged as 'in-flight' is not fully flushed.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Advise client to enable SSE chunk reassembly on the ingesting side where feasible (lenient JSON streaming parser) and to retry on SyntaxError rather than abandoning the record.
- Recommend Orbis route traffic through a plain TCP passthrough (bypass WAF) to validate whether the WAF/proxy is a contributing factor.

Next steps (owned by assigned eng):
- SRE to run edge-proxy capture during a scheduled test from Orbis to reproduce with full server-side captures (ticketed).
- Engineering to audit resume/reattach code path: ensure terminal 'end' event is always enqueued and that partial final chunks are retried or reconstituted from KV cache when resume alignment mismatches.
- If proxy re-chunking is confirmed, add defensive framing: wrap streaming JSON choices in a length-prefixed envelope (opt-in) or emit explicit sequence numbers for chunks so clients/proxies can reconcile boundaries.

Customer communication plan:
- Notify Orbis that we are treating this as Sev1 and will provide hourly updates until a mitigation or fix is deployed.
- Ask Orbis to schedule a 1:1 test window where support and SRE will run controlled reconnect tests behind their corporate WAF.

Resume offset mismatch and proxy buffer non-idempotence are primary suspects. Engineering to add sequence numbers and additional logging to verify boundary alignment across reconnects.

title: Accept-queue buildup from ephemeral prewarm handshake triggering sustained 5xx wave
body:
Accept-queue buildup from ephemeral prewarm handshake triggering sustained 5xx wave

Issue summary:

Starting 2026-03-12 23:12 UTC, Acme Retail (dedicated tenant) reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for streaming/chat routes. Error pattern shows a stair-stepped increase in API gateway 502/503 responses lasting several hours with intermittent short recoveries. Customer impact: their storefront assistant fell back to degraded behavior (timeouts and truncated responses) across peak shopping hours.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx rate (~12% of requests to streaming chat routes at peak).
- Increased tail latency for successful responses (+400ms p95).
- Customer-visible partial message truncation and reconnect loops.

Environment:
- prod:us-east (Dedicated capacity pool assigned to Acme Retail)
- Models: redwood-open-7B for chat, acme-embedder-v2 for on-the-fly embeddings

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High concurrency burst from Acme's client at ~23:10 UTC with many long-lived streaming connections + a simultaneous bulk embedding upload job.
2) Ephemeral runtime prewarm subsystem begins spawning warmup workers and performing TLS handshakes to the proxy/acceptor.
3) API gateway accept queue depth rises, new connections see delayed accept or early RST.
4) Proxy returns 502/503 where gateway reports upstream unavailable.

Observed logs & traces (examples):
- api-gateway logs: repeated accept() latency spikes, backlog exceeded, upstream reset when handing to ephemeral-proxy.
- ephemeral-proxy logs: repeated TLS renegotiation failures "handshake timeout" for short-lived prewarm connections; many half-open sockets.
- serving-runtime logs: series of evictions/oom warnings shortly after prewarm wave; KV cache writes spiked and NVMe write latency increased (iowait).
- kernel metrics: netstat shows SYN_RECV/SYN_SENT queue growth and increased orphan sockets.
- kernel backlog: somaxconn / net.core.somaxconn counts reached limit on several nodes.

Initial hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: API gateway threadpool starvation from large-sidecar healthchecks. (ruled out after thread pool metrics remained within normal ranges)
- Hypothesis B: Autoscaler activity removed warmed workers mid-prewarm causing handshake storms and connection churn. (partial evidence: scale-in events correlate with start of 5xx staircase)
- Hypothesis C: Local NVMe IO saturation due to ephemeral runtime KV-cache snapshotting created backpressure, causing worker OOMs and upstream restarts. (strong evidence: correlated nvme latency spikes and increase in runtime evictions)

Investigation notes:
- Correlated timeline across systems indicates the initial trigger is a coordinated arrival of long-lived streaming connections + a bulk embedding job from the tenant. The prewarm subsystem responds by launching warmers that perform multiple short TLS handshakes to the proxy layer. When autoscaler concurrently scales in to save costs (based on memory-util thresholds), there is a window where warmers are being torn down while new warmers spin up — increasing handshake churn and SYN backpressure at the acceptor.
- NVMe write amplification was observed at the time of the spike: frequent small writes from the runtime's KV-cache checkpointing increased iowait which in turn delayed worker threads, increasing connection hold time and accept queue growth.
- Kernel backlog tuning (somaxconn) on affected nodes was at default; raising backlog would temporarily reduce accept failures but not address root cause.

Temporary mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-12 23:40 UTC: Routed Acme tenant traffic to a reserved warm pool (fallback pool) to reduce prewarm pressure; immediate 5xx reduction to ~1.5%.
- 2026-03-12 23:55 UTC: Reduced prewarm concurrency for Acme's tenant from 8 -> 2 per node and disabled aggressive KV-cache snapshotting for the affected runtime group.
- 2026-03-13 01:10 UTC: Increased somaxconn on edge acceptor nodes as short-term relief.

Permanent remediation plan (work items):
1) Autoscaler policy change (ENG-998): modify scale-in thresholds to avoid concurrent scale-in during active prewarm phases for dedicated tenants (canary patch in staging).
2) Prewarm handshake backoff (RUNTIME-1421): implement exponential backoff and connection reuse for prewarm workers to reduce SYN bursts.
3) KV-cache snapshot batching (RUNTIME-1422): reduce small-file NVMe write amplification by batching checkpoints and using async fsync.
4) Kernel/infra tuning (OPS-776): formally increase accept backlog and tune net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog on acceptor tiers for dedicated pools.
5) Observability: add an alert rule that correlates prewarm spawn rate, NVMe iowait and accept queue depth to catch emergent patterns early (MON-312).

Resolution notes / current status:
- Customer traffic was stabilized by routing to reserved warm pool and adjusting prewarm concurrency. No data loss observed.
- Engineering owners assigned for remediation items 1-4. Estimated ETA for full rollout of fixes: 2 weeks after code review and staging validation.

Follow-up actions for CS/Support:
- Schedule a joint postmortem session with Acme on 2026-03-18 to review mitigations and planned changes.
- Offer temporary traffic smoothing guidance and safe concurrency knobs to the customer until permanent fixes land.

References & cross-links:
- Live dashboards: /dashboards/tenant/Acme-Retail/accept-queue-backpressure
- Kernel backlog notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/accept-queue-backpressure-runbook
- Related internal ticket: INT-3301 (autoscaler scale-in timeline investigation)

title: Client header-based version lock lost during canary health-probe wave causing unexpected fallback to degraded variant
body:
Client header-based version lock lost during canary health-probe wave causing unexpected fallback to degraded variant

Issue summary: Customer reports that tenant-scoped 'X-Model-Pin' header set by their client is inconsistently honoured during a staged canary window. Instead of routing to the pinned model variant, traffic intermittently falls back to the degraded fallback variant during a health-probe surge from internal canary probes. Impact: Several production requests returned degraded-model outputs for short bursts (~30-60s), causing downstream NovaHealth inference scoring to drop and one downstream job to fail validation checks. Environment: prod-us-east, tenant: novahealth-prod, model route: /v1/generate (pinned via header). Occurrence: first observed 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC; recurring during canary health sweep at ~09:12–09:17 and again at 13:45. Hypothesis: Edge smoothing / circuit-shedding combined with asynchronous commit of header-based pin creates a window where the orchestrator's staged-commit path bypasses the pin and applies fallback policies when probe-induced prewarm/drain events cause ephemeral re-routing.

Operational ask: Confirm root cause and provide mitigation (hotfix or recommended client-side change) and a short-term workaround for NovaHealth to avoid production impact while fix is deployed.
1) Customer sets X-Model-Pin: gpt-large-v2-quantized in request header when calling /v1/generate
2) Trigger a staged canary by incrementing canary weight to 10% in us-east for the canonical route
3) Run a health-probe wave (internal) configured to prewarm and then probe 50 edge nodes in quick succession
4) Observe routing logs: some requests from the pinned tenant are routed to fallback variant instead of pinned model for ~30-60s windows
5) Repeat with lower probe concurrency and observe that issue frequency decreases

stack-trace-snippet: orchestrator commit step failed at route-epoch-sync: timeout waiting for prewarm ack (500ms threshold)
