Reproduced locally in staging by simulating 40 concurrent health probes hitting edge-proxy + orchestrator; when prewarm ack latency >300ms commit-path sometimes chooses fallback route due to slot-marking logic.
Edge-proxy sticky lookup occurs before orchestrator epoch merge. If orchestrator snapshot update completes after edge sticky read but before commit ack, header-based pin state can be lost for in-flight requests.
Observed related condition: sidecar backpressure and circuit-shedding triggers 'slot-unavailable' which immediately applies fallback variant without re-evaluating header pins for pending requests.
Log correlation: request-ids abc124 and abc128 show identical timing where orchestrator logged 'slot-unavailable' within 8–12ms after edge read.
Workaround provided: customer to include explicit model field in request body and temporarily increase client retry/backoff to avoid hitting the probe window. Engineering proposed patch: change orchestrator commit flow to mark header-based pin as 'sticky-until-ack' so in-flight requests keep the pin even if snapshot merge occurs; also add a short (500ms) debounce for health-probe bursts to avoid back-to-back prewarm-induced drain. Patch PR opened and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/842. Estimated deployment to canary next 48 hours pending review. Follow-ups: - add automated test for header-pin retention across snapshot merges - update canary health probe config to include smoothing defaults

title: Intermittent long-tail timeouts when output_as_json returns large arrays
body:
Intermittent long-tail timeouts when output_as_json returns large arrays

Issue summary:
Customer BrightLedger reports ~2-5% of inference requests using output_as_json (array-heavy responses) end with 504/timeout or very long tail latencies (>10s). Impact: production traffic hitting enterprise plan, visible in us-east and occasionally in eu-west.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints see intermittent user-perceived timeouts.
- Elevated error rates correlate with requests that serialize arrays with >1000 elements.

Environment:
- prod - us-east primary; also reproducible in eu-west staging less frequently.
- Model in use: redwood-instruct-3b, token length ~150–900, streaming response enabled, output_as_json flag set to true.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a generation request to the /v1/generate endpoint with output_as_json:true and a prompt that instructs the model to enumerate ~1500 items (example prompt attached).
2) Enable streaming.
3) Observe client socket remains open while server completes generation; in some cases, finalization step stalls and client receives a 504.

Observed behavior:
- Long CPU spike (~70–90% on the postprocess thread) when serializer flattens and validates large arrays.
- Streaming chunk delivery continues, but finalization (closing JSON structure and validation) can take multiple seconds and sometimes exceeds gateway timeout, returning 504.
- SRE dashboard shows elevated GC events on the front-end proxy pod during these requests.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming responses with output_as_json should keep tail latency bounded and not timeout in normal load. Finalization should be O(n) without sudden CPU/GC spikes.

Logs / artifacts:
- Trace: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/72a1f4b3
- Kibana query: kbn://prod-logs/app/kibana#/discover?_g=()&query=service:%22json-postprocess%22%20AND%20http.status_code:504
- Attached sample request payload and client SDK log snippet (customer provided).
Use output_as_json:true and request generation of >1000 list elements
Enable streaming in SDK
Observe request duration and gateway timeout
Final JSON close/validation takes multiple seconds
Intermittent 504s at gateway despite tokens delivered over stream
Postprocess worker CPU spikes and GC activity
Finalization completes quickly and keeps request under SLA
Streaming clients receive a clean JSON stream without server timeouts
Heap/CPU profiles point to json-postprocess worker doing bulk validation using ajv-like validator in a single pass at the end of the stream.
Proxy gateway (nginx) timeout default of 30s triggered on worst-case finalization, client saw 504 despite streaming chunks arriving earlier.
Reproducible with both redwood-instruct-3b and openchat-4x-lite; severity higher on models that emit many small tokens per element.
Hypothesis: full-document schema validation at the end creates an O(n^2) behavior due to repeated canonicalization; switching to incremental validation should be O(n).
Customer can disable output_as_json and stream newline-delimited JSON manually from tokens.
Instruct model to emit fewer items per call or paginate results to keep arrays <800 elements.
Increase gateway timeout for customer-specific route as a short-term mitigation (requires security review).
Implement incremental/streaming JSON schema validation during streaming and avoid full canonicalization at finalization. Backfill with a fast-path for large arrays that skips expensive checks when schema is simple.
Merge runtime PR #987 and rollout canary to prod during maintenance window (assigned to Eng/runtime)
Monitor tail latency and 504 rate for BrightLedger routes for 72 hours post-rollout
Add a dashboard alert for json-postprocess finalization time >2s and automatic rollback signal

title: SSE resume hangs when proxy path splits; partial metadata and stalled epilogue on reconnect
body:
SSE resume hangs when proxy path splits; partial metadata and stalled epilogue on reconnect

Issue summary: Customer reports that after an intermittent network disruption their SSE streaming response resumes but then stalls: the client receives heartbeat frames and a partial metadata envelope (session_id/seq mismatch) and never receives the final 'end' envelope that marks completion. Impact: NovaDocs users see partial outputs or indefinite streaming hangs for long-running generations (document summarization flows). Roughly 8% of resumed sessions in the last 24h for the customer's dedicated pool show this symptom.
1) Start a long-running generation (approx 800-1200 token expected) via SSE against the customer's dedicated endpoint in us-west
2) Force a short connection interruption (simulate NAT timeout / client network swap) during token stream (around 60-120 seconds in),
3) Allow client to reconnect and send the SSE resume token (client uses resume_token header with last_offset),
4) Observe that the resumed stream emits several heartbeat-only chunks, then a metadata envelope with session_id that does not match the pre-drop session, and the final 'end' envelope is not delivered — client parser stays waiting for termination.
2026-03-10T18:42:03Z [edge-proxy] connid=abcd1234 path=/v1/streams/resume route=origin-region-2 -> rebind worker=worker-3b
2026-03-10T18:42:04Z [serving-runtime] resume_token check: incoming.ts=1679869324, root_snapshot.ts=1679869323, token_delta=1
2026-03-10T18:42:05Z [serving-runtime] INFO emitted heartbeat chunk (len=2) for stream_id=stream-7782
2026-03-10T18:42:08Z [serving-runtime] WARN metadata envelope session_id mismatch (expected=session-77 got=session-77-rebind) for stream-7782
2026-03-10T18:42:20Z [edge-proxy] keepalive-trim triggered by CDN (Fastly) semi-close: early-crlf-trim=true
2026-03-10T18:42:30Z [serving-runtime] stream flusher: no terminal envelope sent; client connection still open; flusher retry-count=4

2026-03-10 19:20 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): I pulled edge logs for the customer's pool. I see ConnRebinds to worker-3b and an early CRLF trim from the CDN; sending to runtime to correlate. Assigning to serving-runtime on-call.
2026-03-11 03:05 - Arjun Patel (runtime on-call): Observed that when resume is handled by a different worker the session_id suffix is appended by sidecar rebind code. Parser on client side treats it as mismatched session and drops incoming terminal envelope. Hypothesis: sticky-session not honored for some rebinds under autoscaling.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Provided additional client capture and indicated customer is on Dedicated with autoscaling enabled. Customer requests workaround within 24h to avoid user-facing failures.
2026-03-12 11:43 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied: pinned sticky session policy for NovaDocs dedicated pool for us-west. Also asked them to enable websocket fallback in their client as a short-term change. Monitoring for reduction in failures.
2026-03-13 08:00 - Arjun Patel (runtime): Reproducer added to CI and a fix (avoid appending rebind suffix to session_id) landed in PR #5881. Coordinating rollout; planned canary in us-west on 2026-03-14.
2026-03-13 08:30 - NovaDocs (Customer): Confirmed that after sticky pin was applied new resumed sessions appear to complete end-to-end. They will keep websocket fallback active while we roll out fix.
Edge logs show frequent conn rebinds in same second window as resume attempts; rebind often sends to a worker instance with '-rebind' suffix in session_id assignment.
Fastly/edge performed an aggressive keepalive trim (early-crlf-trim) which appears to cause the connection to be semi-closed before the runtime flusher finalizes the terminal envelope.
Client parser behavior: the client treats any session_id mismatch as a hard desync and will ignore subsequent 'end' envelopes coming with unexpected session_id namespace.
Autoscaling path: when Dedicated pool scales up during high concurrency we observe ephemeral sidecars using different session namespace which is not transparently compatible with resume semantics.
Hypothesis chain: CDN semi-close -> edge rebind -> worker sidecar appends rebind suffix -> runtime emits terminal envelope with new session_id -> client discards terminal envelope because session_id mismatches -> client waits indefinitely.
1) Pinned sticky sessions for NovaDocs dedicated pool in us-west (applied 2026-03-12) — this reduced observed failures in our short window of monitoring.
2) Recommended customer enable websocket fallback for critical flows (client-side change). Websocket fallbacks completed full sessions consistently in our tests.
3) If using a CDN with keepalive trimming, increase origin keepalive timeout or disable early CRLF trimming for the affected route.
Fix in progress: runtime change to preserve canonical session_id across rebinds (do not append ad-hoc suffixes). PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5881 submitted and passing unit+integration tests. Plan: canary rollout in us-west 2026-03-14, monitor 24h, then global rollout if stable.
Canary rollout to 10% of us-west traffic on 2026-03-14 by deploying PR #5881
Monitor resumed stream failure rate vs baseline for 24 hours (target: <0.5% of resumes failing)
Coordinate with NovaDocs to revert sticky-pin once canary is green
Add additional telemetry to resume flow: emit resume_token_origin_worker and resume_token_matched boolean to traces

title: Connection-pool token-window drift causing soft 429s on multiplexed multipart uploads
body:
Connection-pool token-window drift causing soft 429s on multiplexed multipart uploads

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 responses during parallel multipart embedding uploads using a pool of long-lived HTTP/2 connections via their dedicated pool. The pattern is tied to short bursts of parallel PUTs where connections are reused from a keep-alive pool and the tenant token-window shows drift compared to console metrics.

Impact: BrightLayer ingestion jobs (batch of ~2k files per run) are failing intermittently with 429s during peak-of-run. Failures cause retries that stretch job run time from ~3m to >15m and trigger downstream timeouts in their orchestrator. Estimated ~12% of batches in last 24h experienced partial failure.

Environment: BrightLayer on Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-us-east-12). Production. API client uses HTTP/2 multiplexing with 8 concurrent streams per connection and reuses 16 pooled connections.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a multiprocess uploader with 48 workers (concurrency 48) that opens 16 persistent HTTP/2 connections and multiplexes requests across them.
2) Each worker uploads multi-part files (small ~16KB payloads) to /v1/embeddings in parallel.
3) Observe ~10-20s into the run intermittent 429 responses returned for some requests, then a wave of retries.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses return with X-RateLimit-* headers indicating token_bucket_remaining near zero for the tenant, but console quota graphs show a slightly higher remaining tokens (apparent skew).
- Throttles cluster around moments where a single connection's streams spike (connection affinity), then recover as connections age or are recreated.

Expected behavior: Client-side connection reuse should not cause token accounting drift. Throttles should be evenly applied across tenant requests and exposed token headers should match console quota state within short reconciliation window.

Temporary mitigation applied by Support: Instructed customer to reduce per-connection stream concurrency to 4 and stagger uploader start by jittering worker launches. This reduced 429s in their next run but is not acceptable long-term.

Logs / dashboards / pointers:
- Customer provided request IDs: r-ff12a3c4, r-ff12a3d6, r-ff12a3e2 (sample wave 2026-03-12T09:22:xxZ).
- Console tenant quota graph: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/brightlayer/usage?window=24h (customer-shared view).
- Edge proxy logs: edge-proxy-us-east-12: /var/log/edge/conn-reuse-2026-03-12.log (SRE link: https://logs.redwood.ai/q/edge-proxy/conn-reuse-03-12).
- Rate limiter dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/dashboards/rate-limiter/tenant/brightlayer (shows short-window refill spikes).

Next steps proposed:
1) Reproduce in lab using a dedicated-pool replica with identical connection pooling (8 streams x 16 connections) and BrightLayer's upload pattern.
2) Validate whether per-connection token accounting (edge shard) can momentarily deplete and not immediately reconcile with central refill due to health-check increments or connection affinity.
3) If reproduced, scope fix: either change refill reconciliation frequency for short windows or add a fast-path that spreads refill credits across active connections when burst detected.
4) Provide permanent guidance to customers for safe defaults (recommended max streams per connection, recommended jittering).

Customer asked for a timeline and whether this will count as reserved-capacity ticket for SLA. Support to coordinate with Dedicated PM for priority handling.

2026-03-12 11:40 - BrightLayer (Customer): Provided request IDs, client config, and confirmed they use persistent HTTP/2 connections with keepalive. Noted pattern started after enabling a custom uploader that multiplexes aggressively.

2026-03-13 14:22 - Diego Ramirez (SRE): Added temporary alert to rate-limiter to capture connection-affinity spikes and token-window deltas between edge shard and central ledger. Shared trace links in ticket.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Product (PM - Aisha Patel): Flagged as candidate for short-window refill smoothing. Requested impact numbers and whether behavior affects other dedicated customers. Asked to attach repro harness and metrics.
2026-03-14 12:50 - Support (Sofia Nguyen): Shared mitigation steps with customer and scheduled a follow-up call to validate next week's rollout of a rate-limiter config change in staging.
Lab repro succeeded with narrow parameters: high stream multiplexing and high connection reuse produced transient token starvation on certain edge shards.
Hypothesis: Edge shard token buckets track per-connection counts; when multiple streams on same connection fire simultaneously, local accounting heads to zero before central refill distributes credits, causing 429s surfaced to client with token-headers reflecting local depletion.
Observed correlation between health-check bursts from edge (heartbeat writer) and small refill timing misalignments that exacerbate short-window depletion.
Customer workload uses many small payloads which increases tokens-per-request accounting churn compared to fewer large requests; batching behavior differs from typical embed workflows.
Potential fix vectors: a) increase refill frequency for short windows b) add cross-connection credit redistribution c) update client guidance to limit per-connection streams (recommended <=4) until fix ships.
Priority: high for Dedicated customers running high-concurrency multiplexers; medium for self-serve customers who typically have lower concurrent connections.
Temporary mitigation documented and shared; SRE implemented short-term monitoring and a staging config that smooths short-window refills. Product requested impact analysis for permanent fix. Plan: schedule a canary rollout of refill-smoothing in staging next week and monitor 429 rate delta; if good, schedule production rollout with migration notes and recommended client limits. Customer happy to test staging build.

title: Dashboard snapshot filter state resets when support impersonation toggled during snapshot generation
body:
Dashboard snapshot filter state resets when support impersonation toggled during snapshot generation

Issue summary:
When Support toggles the impersonation view while a dashboard snapshot job is running (scheduled or ad-hoc 'Save snapshot' flow), the resulting snapshot file retains the base time range but loses any non-default ephemeral filters (user-level or org-scoped query filters). The snapshot produced and attached to the scheduled report shows filters as cleared, which breaks downstream alert links and tracehook anchors for the customer report recipients.

Impact:
- Customer-reported: scheduled PDF snapshots and exported snapshot URLs show empty or default filters even though the dashboard in the UI had filters applied at snapshot time.
- Alerts linked from those snapshots point to dashboards without the expected tracehook context, causing recipients to open dashboards that no longer highlight the same traces/annotations.
- Affects enterprise BrightAssist (multiple teams), observed across 3 org-scoped scheduled snapshots in us-east. Potential wider exposure for other orgs using impersonation-based support workflows.

Environment:
- Production console (prod: us-east)
- Customer: BrightAssist (enterprise)
- Dashboard types affected: saved dashboards with ad-hoc filters, saved snapshot scheduler, and ad-hoc "Save snapshot" export.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Support user impersonates BrightAssist: Using the console impersonation toggle (Support > Impersonate org).
2) While impersonating, open a saved dashboard that has ephemeral filters applied (e.g., service:search-api, tag:payment-flow) and a non-default time range (Last 24h).
3) Click "Save snapshot" (ad-hoc) or trigger a scheduled snapshot run for the same dashboard.
4) After snapshot job completes, open the generated snapshot URL or download PDF/PNG.
5) Observe that filters are reset to the dashboard base state (no ephemeral filters), and tracehook/alert links in the snapshot no longer include the original filter query parameters.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot should capture the UI state visible to the impersonating user, including ephemeral filters and time range; tracehook links should preserve query params that anchor traces.

Actual behavior:
- Snapshot preserves time range but clears ephemeral filters. Tracehook query params are truncated (trace_id and anchor params missing). Snapshots saved under the customer's scheduled report appear to come from an unfiltered dashboard.

Logs / Observations:
- Support session logs show impersonation header X-Redwood-Impersonate: org=brightassist and a snapshot job request POST /api/snapshots with a payload containing filters.
- Snapshot worker log for job id snap-20260310-87 shows worker accepted payload but subsequent snapshot-render request to renderer service omitted the `filters` parameter in the query string.
- Renderer service trace: renderer-3 reported 200 for render call but request path lacked ?filters=... segment.
- No 5xx errors observed; flow completes successfully but with mutated payload.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Instructed BrightAssist users to create a new saved dashboard variant with desired filters (persisted saved-dashboard) and schedule snapshots from that saved-dashboard instead of relying on ad-hoc filters at snapshot time. This preserves filter state in scheduled snapshots until a fix is rolled out.

Business impact and urgency:
- Customer-facing produced artifacts (scheduled snapshots) do not reflect the intended investigation context; slows down incident response for their SREs. Customer escalated due to cross-team workflows relying on snapshots for on-call. Recommended P1 / Sev2 escalation and assignment to console/dashboard + snapshot pipeline owners.

title: Half-open socket flood after model-variant swap causing burst 5xx and streaming drops
body:
Half-open socket flood after model-variant swap causing burst 5xx and streaming drops

Issue summary: Acme Health observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses and frequent streaming session drops beginning 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC following a customer-initiated model-variant switch. The spike was concentrated in eu-west and impacted active streaming chat sessions and large-embedding uploads.

Impact: ~18% elevated 5xx rate for the tenant over a 30-minute window, ~12% of active streaming sessions terminated early (socket resets). Customer reports production user-facing errors and increased latency.

Initial triage: Support escalated to SRE at 02:35 UTC after customer provided request IDs and trace samples. No scheduled platform deploys were shown in the tenant's control plane around the time of the spike; however an automated model-variant swap for the customer's pinned route completed at 02:12 UTC and triggered a tenant warmup burst.
1) Customer pins a route to a new model variant and triggers warmup/prefetch.
2) Warmup creates short-lived high-concurrency prefetch requests that flood connection pools.
3) Under sustained warmup plus concurrent customer traffic, the API gateway accept queue begins to backlog and many downstream proxies start returning 502/503.
4) Streaming sessions hit half-closed socket conditions and get reset when upstream runtime threads block on connection cleanup.

Note: We reproduced a similar failure in staging by running the customer's warmup script (prefetch=8x baseline for 30s) combined with ongoing streaming traffic at 60 concurrent streams.
Excerpt of correlated logs (masked):
[2026-03-10T02:12:09Z] route-manager: variant-swap completed route=/customers/acme-tenant route_id=rt-abc123
[2026-03-10T02:12:33Z] apigw: accept_queue_length=128/1024 conn_backlog=95 thread_pool_util=92% route=rt-abc123
[2026-03-10T02:13:05Z] proxy[ephemeral-17]: tcp_half_open_count=64 keepalive_reaped=0
[2026-03-10T02:13:17Z] runtime: kvcache_lock_wait_ms=2100 gpu_watchdog_reset=false pid=23456
[2026-03-10T02:14:41Z] apigw: outbound_error=502 upstream=proxy/ephemeral-17 details=\"connection_reset\"
[2026-03-10T02:16:02Z] sres-alarms: tenant_rt-abc123_5xx_rate=0.18 threshold=0.03

Stack traces and full logs uploaded to support bundle: s3://support-bundles/SUP-163845/2026-03-10/supp_bundle.tar.gz
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - Customer-initiated model-variant swap triggered automated prefetch/warmup.
2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - Customer reported elevated errors (first contact).
2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Support collected traces and escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 02:30 UTC - Reproduced in staging with synthetic warmup+stream load.
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Hotfix (apigw threadpool pruning fix + temporary accept_queue sizing) rolled out to eu-west.
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Customer traffic returned to baseline; streaming disconnects dropped to <1%.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Post-incident review and runbook items created.
Hypothesis: Sudden warmup prefetch created a burst of short-lived connections that exposed a latent bug in connection pool pruning logic in the API gateway. The bug left half-open sockets in the ephemeral proxy (keepalive not reclaimed), creating accept_queue pressure and causing downstream runtime threads to block on socket cleanup while kvcache locks contended.

What we checked:
- apigw thread pool and accept queue metrics (elevated during window).
- proxy half-open socket counts (spike concurrent with warmup).
- runtime kvcache lock wait and prefetch latencies (elevated).
- GPU watchdog and driver logs (no driver resets observed).

Staging reproduction: By replaying the customer's warmup script while streaming 60 concurrent session simulations we observed quick growth in tcp_half_open_count and an apigw thread_pool exhaustion that produced 502s and forced runtime request cancellations. This reproduced core symptoms (502/503, streaming resets).

Root cause: combination of aggressive prefetch/warmup traffic pattern for this tenant + a connection-pruning bug in apigw that failed to reclaim half-closed sockets rapidly enough, producing accept-queue saturation and upstream request cancellations.
1) Applied a temporary tenant-level rate cap on warmup/prefetch to smooth ramp.
2) Increased apigw accept_queue sizing for eu-west domain and tuned keepalive reclaim interval to be more aggressive.
3) Customer temporarily reduced prefetch multiplier from 8x to 2x while we validated the fix.
Deployed hotfix 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC: apigw PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428) which:
- fixes connection pool pruning bug that left half-open sockets unreclaimed,
- improves threadpool pruning heuristics to prevent starvation under warmup bursts,
- adds a short-term mitigation to backpressure new warmup requests when accept_queue occupancy exceeds threshold.
After rollout, accept_queue occupancy dropped and 5xx rates returned to baseline for the tenant. Customer verified recovery and we kept the temporary tenant prefetch cap for 24h as a precaution.

Post-incident: change merged and monitored for 48h; no regressions observed. Incident closed 2026-03-12 after postmortem review.
- Add a runbook section for model-variant warmup patterns and recommended tenant prefetch limits.
- Implement an automated alarm that triggers when apigw accept_queue > 70% and tcp_half_open_count rises for >60s.
- Add an integration test simulating large warmup bursts with concurrent streaming to catch regressions.
- Coordinate with product to provide guidance to customers on safe prefetch multipliers for enterprise/private tiers.
- Schedule postmortem doc and share with SRE and Solutions Engineering teams.
Bug in API gateway connection-pruning logic combined with aggressive tenant warmup (prefetch) behavior leading to persistent half-open sockets, accept-queue saturation, and cascading upstream cancellations.

title: Hostname suffix truncation during imaging causes Intune device object merge and check-in flapping
body:
Hostname suffix truncation during imaging causes Intune device object merge and check-in flapping

Issue summary: Devices imaged with the new OEM task sequence (ts-2026-03) are being assigned hostnames that get truncated by a legacy hostname-sanitize script to 15 characters. When the corporate DNS suffix is later appended by the join script the resulting FQDN collides with an existing device name in Intune/Azure AD. Intune merges device objects in some cases when the primary DNS/hostname matches, causing device check-in to alternate between two device objects (flapping) and blocking configuration profiles/policy assignment.

Impact: Multiple newly imaged seats in prod-us-west and APAC are failing to receive critical configuration profiles; desktop management and endpoint security policies not applied. Affected users report intermittent policy loss and inability to access mapped network printers. No data loss reported, but this blocks autopilot/dedicated device rollouts and delays repairs.

Observed behavior: Hostnames generated by ts-2026-03 look correct during imaging (example: rw-infer-nyc-emb-20260312), but after the legacy sanitize step the local .computername gets truncated to 15 chars (rw-infer-nyc-eb). When domain join/appending-suffix runs we end up with rw-infer-nyc-eb.corp.redwood.com which matches an existing old device object (previously registered) and Azure AD/Intune merges or links to the older object. This creates two Azure device IDs with the same physical machine reporting intermittently and both show check-ins.

Expected behavior: Hostname sanitization should preserve uniqueness used by TS naming templates or the join process should ensure a stable, unique device identifier is used for Intune registration (preferably HW hash/autopilot entry), avoiding collisions with legacy objects.
1) Use imaging task sequence ts-2026-03 that runs hostname template: rw-infer-<region>-<team>-<shortdate>.
2) Run legacy hostname sanitize script (hostname-sanitize.sh) which truncates to first 15 characters for legacy NetBIOS compatibility.
3) Complete OOBE and domain join which appends corporate suffix.
4) Observe Intune portal: device appears to merge with an existing device object which has matching shortname; check-in timestamps alternate between two device IDs.
5) Reproducible on repro VM/hardware with imported autopilot hardware hash for same model.

Notes: Repro only after the sanitize step is executed; skipping sanitize prevents the merge.
AzureAD join trace: 2026-03-12T09:42:11Z - JoinService: SetComputerName='rw-infer-nyc-eb'
Intune MDM enrollment: EnrollmentID=9f2b3c... status=success (deviceId: d-0a1b2c)
Intune device sync: 2026-03-12T09:45:02Z - DeviceObjectMerge detected - matched on NetBIOSName 'RW-INFER-NYC-EB' with existing object id e-5d6f7g
AAD logs: 2026-03-12T09:46:10Z - Duplicate device claim attempt resolved by merge policy -> resulting hybrid object mapping.
SCCM client log (clientid.log): 2026-03-12T09:47:30Z - Client registered new GUID; policy request failed: 0x87d00324 (no policy assigned)

Initial hypothesis: hostname truncate to 15 chars causes name collisions with older device records created prior to autopilot rollouts. Verified by imaging a test unit and checking AAD device list - old device (decommissioned) reused same shortname.
What we tried:
- Re-imaging and excluding sanitize script -> new device registers cleanly (no merge).
- Created synthetic long hostnames and observed Azure registers new device id consistently.
- Queried AAD for duplicates: ran Powershell 'Get-AzureADDevice -Filter "startswith(displayName,'rw-infer-nyc')"' and found 3 objects with same shortname lowercased causing merge logic to trigger.
- Cross-checked with #internal-provisioning Slack thread and found a recent deploy of hostname-sanitize.sh with change that enforces NetBIOS only; likely merged in January image baseline (ref: git commit abc123 in infra-images).

Root cause candidate: combination of (a) legacy sanitize step truncating NetBIOS name to 15 chars, (b) autopilot/device enrollment behavior that sometimes links by hostname when HW hash is missing or duplicate, and (c) leftover old AAD device objects that match truncated names.

title: Epochal pin drift after hotfix commit causes split-cohort model routing
body:
Epochal pin drift after hotfix commit causes split-cohort model routing

Issue summary: After a hotfix commit was deployed to edge-proxy and serving-runtime, a subset of NimbusHealth tenant sessions began receiving responses from an older model variant despite tenant-level version pin. Impact: intermittent mixed-model responses and occasional semantic regressions in production traffic for a high-volume customer on Dedicated capacity. Scope: ~2% of requests for the tenant across two API routes were routed to legacy variant; visible for ~30 minutes during a regional rebalancing window.
Customer-reported model inconsistencies (different generations for same session), increased error rate for downstream validation checks, and 3 customer-facing support cases opened. Business impact: potential quality regression for patient-facing summaries; customer flagged as escalated.
1) Customer has tenant-level pin to redwood/gpt-infer-v1.2.
2) Deploy hotfix that increments edge-proxy epoch used for cohort merges (edge hotfix applied at 08:22 UTC).
3) Trigger tenant traffic (steady load).
4) Observe that ~2% of requests return tokens with generation signatures matching older variant.
Note: issue reproduced in prod only when regional rebalancer moved a small number of routing shards at 08:46 UTC.
Edge trace snippets: span=edg-router-9345 trace_id=7f2a1c start=2026-03-10T08:46:03Z routing_decision=COHORT_MERGE epoch_old=89 epoch_new=90 pin_token=tn-9843 map_hash=0x4f3b
Serving runtime logs: warn: pin_coherence: token epoch mismatch for session tn-9843 expected=90 observed=89
Healthcheck events: probe=region-rebalancer shard_move=shard-137 => 24s delay
Request IDs: r-20260310-8f7a, r-20260310-8f7b, r-20260310-8f7c (samples attached in ticket).
Initial hypothesis: epoch increment during hotfix created a transient window where edge used new epoch while routing-coordinator still had cached cohort maps on old epoch. Evidence: routing_coordinator metrics show a 22s TTL eviction spike at 08:46:03Z; edge proxy shows commit timestamp 08:22 but persisted epoch header 90. Correlation with rebalancer: rebalancer log shows simultaneous shard moves which triggered local cache rebuilds and a race between pin reconciliation and cohort-merge reconciliation. Verified that fallback-routing was exercised because several backends returned 503 for the new variant; fallback routed to older variant that was still considered compatible.
Race between edge hotfix rollout (epoch bump) and routing-coordinator cache invalidation during a shard rebalancing window. The epoch token in the pin header did not reconcile atomically across all routing layers; some routers accepted older epoch pin mapping and routed to legacy instances. Additionally, fallback policy allowed migration to legacy variant when a subset of nodes reported degraded health during the rollout.
1) Temporary pin refresh: instruct customer to issue a pin-refresh API call which forces token re-issuance tied to epoch 90. 2) Increase routing-coordinator cache TTL to avoid immediate evictions during coordinated rollouts. Workaround applied at 09:05 UTC; customer reported reduction in mixed responses within 3 minutes.
Short term: backport a coordination barrier so that serving-runtime and edge-proxy epoch bumps use an orchestrated commit fence during region rebalances (PR created: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/6123). Medium term: introduce pin-epoch handshake and optimistic validation on edge to detect mismatched epoch early and queue requests for atomic reconciliation. Ops action: a runbook update to pause shard rebalancer during hotfix epoch bumps for Dedicated tenants for next 30 days.
Action items: (1) add an e2e test that simulates epoch bump + shard move, (2) update canary rollout playbook to include atomic pin handshake, (3) increase observability: add metric 'pin_epoch_mismatch_rate' and dashboard, (4) schedule a customer check-in with NimbusHealth for 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC.

title: Buffer credit escrowed after org consolidation refunded to wrong billing profile, provisional negative balance
body:
Buffer credit escrowed after org consolidation refunded to wrong billing profile, provisional negative balance

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a planned org consolidation on 2026-03-10, a held hourly buffer credit (warmup/escrow) was released but applied to an unrelated billing profile within the consolidated tenant. This produced a provisional negative balance on the customer's primary billing profile and blocked autopay on the next cycle.

Impact:
- StellarVoice reported a provisional negative balance of $-1,234.56 on their primary billing profile; autopay blocked.
- Their production inference traffic in us-east experienced quota throttling for ~3 hours while finance blocked charges.
- Customer requests a full reconciliation audit and corrective credit move rather than a blanket refund.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-east region)
- Consolidation event executed via org-service migration job on 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC

Expected behavior:
- Held buffer/warmup credits associated with an API key or subaccount should migrate with the corresponding billing profile or be flagged for manual reassignment when consolidation maps keys to a different profile. Credits should not be auto-applied to unrelated billing profiles.

Actual behavior:
- Escrowed buffer credits were released and attributed to a different billing profile created during consolidation (billing_profile_789). The original billing profile (billing_profile_123) shows missing credits and provisional negative balance.

Steps to reproduce / observed timeline:
1) 2026-03-10 01:50 UTC - Org consolidation job started (migration job ID: org-mig-20260310-01).
2) 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Postback reconciliation worker processed buffered escrow records for tenant.
3) 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - Credits released; credit-escrow records assigned to billing_profile_789.
4) 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC - Customer noticed autopay block; opened support chat.
5) 2026-03-10 04:10 UTC - Customer escalated to account team.

Relevant logs and evidence:
- Postback reconciler logs (postback-worker-11): "escrow_record id=esc-44321 assigned_profile=billing_profile_789 source=org-mig-20260310-01"
- Billing audit: "credit_adjustment: -1234.56 from billing_profile_123 (orphaned)"
- Console screenshot attached by customer showing negative balance and blocked autopay timestamped 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC.

Customer request:
- Move escrowed credits back to billing_profile_123 or apply equivalent credit to that profile.
- Provide reconciliation CSV with mapping and timestamps, and explain root cause so customer can update internal finance records.

2026-03-12 09:12 - Maya Chen: Ticket opened after handoff from account team; customer requests audit CSV and non-refund remediation.
2026-03-12 10:03 - Priya Natarajan: Assigned for billing investigation. Noted potential postback routing mismatch after consolidation job. Collecting logs from postback reconciler and org-service mapping table.
2026-03-12 14:21 - Billing SRE (Evan Morales): Found that 18 escrow records processed in same batch were attributed to billing_profile_789. Saving raw reconciler output to /internal/logs/postback/2026-03-10/worker-11/escrows.log and linking PR for potential fix.

Postback reconciler processes escrow records using 'migration_profile' from org-service mapping cache. Cache stale TTL set to 6h; consolidation job updated mapping table but did not publish mapping events to cache invalidation topic.
Batch id org-mig-20260310-01 triggered reconciler run that looked up billing_profile via cached mapping which still pointed to interim auto-created profile billing_profile_789.
Reconciler code path handles missing exact key matches by falling back to 'first-found' profile in tenant; this behavior caused misassignment in consolidation edge case.
18 escrow records (total $1,234.56) affected; no other tenants in same batch showed anomalies. The recon flow kept full audit logs which we can export per request.
Preliminary hypothesis: cache invalidation race + fallback logic in reconciler led to wrongful assignment.
Finance Ops can apply a manual credit-adjustment entry to billing_profile_123 to restore balance while engineering prepares an idempotent migration script.
If customer prefers, a provisional invoice waiver can be applied to unblock autopay in the short term.

2026-03-15 08:30 - After validation, a controlled live remediation executed: 18 escrow records were reattributed to billing_profile_123; finance issued matching negative adjustment to billing_profile_789. Total moved amount: $1,234.56.
2026-03-15 09:10 - Autopay unblocked; customer confirmed balance returned to expected positive state.
Root cause: reconciler fallback to 'first-found' billing profile when cache returned stale/incomplete mappings during org consolidation. Fix: change reconciler to reject ambiguous mapping and queue records for manual review; add cache invalidation publish after org-service updates. PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/214.
Follow-up actions: add integration test for consolidation flows, add alert on >5 escrow reassignments in single batch, and update runbook to include manual verification step for large consolidations.

title: Unexpected OAuth app conceding API-scoped token and creating service key after vendor onboarding form
body:
Unexpected OAuth app conceding API-scoped token and creating service key after vendor onboarding form

Issue summary: An employee clicked a vendor onboarding form link (recruited-vendor.example.com) that initiated an OAuth consent flow. The external app requested limited API token scopes. Post-consent, an API-scoped token and a service account key named 'vendor_onboard_2026' were observed in the org via audit logs. Impact: potential unauthorized service-level access that was subsequently used by CI pipelines to run a privileged job and fetch secrets. Timeline and observed activity are below.
2026-03-12 09:14 - Aisha Patel: User reported that the vendor's form asked them to 'connect with Redwood' to prefill company info. User accepted the prompt. They later noticed a CI job triggered overnight they didn't recognize.
2026-03-12 09:42 - Marcus Nguyen: I've captured the user's session id and started pulling audit logs for OAuth grant events. Assigning to SecOps for token analysis.
2026-03-12 11:05 - SecOps (Elena Ruiz): Preliminary log parse shows an OAuth app with client_id 'vendor-5123' granted by the user. App requested scopes: read:org, write:ci, create:service_keys. Found a service key creation event 3 minutes after grant.
2026-03-12 13:22 - SRE (Daniel Cho): The service key was used by runner 'ci-runner-9' at 03:12 UTC from IP 198.51.100.42 to pull a privileged job 'deploy-metrics'. We have paused that runner and blocked the IP in firewall rules.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Marcus Nguyen: Revoked the OAuth app's active tokens and disabled the created service key. Rotated affected CI credentials; announced mandatory credential rotations for teams referenced in logs.
2026-03-13 08:10 - Elena Ruiz: Adding detection rule to flag any future vendor OAuth grants that request create:service_keys. Filing follow-up policy task for onboarding flow changes.
2026-03-13 12:00 - Marcus Nguyen: Updated incident status; Security will continue root-cause. No evidence so far of data exfiltration beyond CI job logs; however, we are treating this as a potential compromise until full audit completes.
User flow: Clicked link -> vendor page presented OAuth consent -> user accepted using SSO session. OAuth grant recorded at 2026-03-11T23:58:12Z.
Audit evidence: oauth.grant events show client_id vendor-5123, redirect_uri vendor callback URL vendor-5123.example.com/cb, scopes included 'create:service_keys'. service_keys.create event by actor user:ap.patel@redwood at 2026-03-11T24:01:05Z creating 'vendor_onboard_2026'.
Service key activity: key 'vendor_onboard_2026' used by ci-runner-9 to call /api/v1/ci/jobs with token presented in Authorization header. Job pulled secret store keys for deployment 'deploy-metrics'.
Network: outbound connections from CI runner to vendor endpoints observed following job. External IP 198.51.100.42 resolves to a hosting provider used by multiple vendor forms; reverse lookup inconclusive.
Hypotheses: (A) Malicious vendor form requested excessive scopes and created a service key to escalate access; (B) Vendor form was legitimate but compromised; (C) User consent was coerced by deceptive UI (consent phishing).
Risk assessment: High — service-level credential creation and CI usage gives attacker a lateral path to internal infra; priority high until keys rotated and further evidence is negative for exfiltration.
Data search: No S3 or database export events linked to this service key in the 24 hours following creation. CI job logs show read-only metrics fetch and a call to an internal telemetry endpoint; exfil not confirmed.
Detection gaps: Current OAuth app onboarding allows create:service_keys scope by default for vendor apps. No org-level denylist existed for apps requesting service key creation.
Related indicators: vendor client_id vendor-5123, service_key name vendor_onboard_2026, runner ci-runner-9, external IP 198.51.100.42, redirect domain vendor-5123.example.com.
Suggested evidence collection: full CI job logs, container snapshots for job run, VPC flow logs for runner, complete OAuth grant history for user and org.
Communication: Notified Legal and Incident Response. Drafted user-facing advisory advising not to reauthorize external apps until review completes.
Immediate mitigation actions taken 2026-03-12: revoked vendor-5123 tokens, disabled service key 'vendor_onboard_2026', paused ci-runner-9, blocked external IP 198.51.100.42 at perimeter, rotated CI credentials referenced in logs.
Policy changes implemented: added org-level rule to block OAuth apps requesting create:service_keys and implemented manual approval for any vendor app requesting elevated scopes.
Detection and monitoring: new alert created to flag OAuth grants that include service_key or admin-equivalent scopes; added logging retention for IAM events for 90 days.
Follow-ups (owner: SecOps): investigate vendor-5123 provenance, request vendor's security posture and supply chain evidence, run deeper forensics on paused runner container and any outbound connections.
Runbook tasks: update onboarding templates to remove one-click OAuth for non-SSO-approved vendors; add mandatory security review checkbox on onboarding form.
Status: Containment successful; keys revoked and runner paused. Incident remains open for forensic analysis and vendor validation. Expected update 2026-03-18 with forensic summary.

title: WDAC policy hash mismatch after imaging prevents smartcard & corporate SSO logon on several device models
body:
WDAC policy hash mismatch after imaging prevents smartcard & corporate SSO logon on several device models

Issue summary: After routine depot-repair imaging we are seeing Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy hash mismatches on boot for a subset of devices. Affected machines drop the corporate SSO/Netlogon smartcard auth path and fall back to local credential screens, which blocks automated post-imaging enrollment tasks (Intune/AAD join) and prevents users from completing first-login flows.

Impact: Affected users cannot complete provisioning during first sign-in; automated device configuration (policies, cert enrollment, company portal) does not complete. This impacts onboarding for employees receiving repaired machines and delays returns to service. Estimated ~6-9% of depot-imaged devices from last week's imaging bundle.

Environment: Production fleet (depot repair image) in us-east and eu-west regions. Primary models observed: Dell Latitude 5430, Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen11. Imaging performed via SCCM task sequence (corp-imaging-v3.4) with post-image WDAC registration step.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Re-image device using SCCM task sequence corp-imaging-v3.4 with WDAC policy package applied.
2) Complete OOBE and network join steps.
3) Sign in with corporate SSO (smartcard or Windows Hello for Business).
4) Observe that Windows shows WDAC hash mismatch event and LSA/Winlogon rejects enterprise authentication flows.

Observed behavior: WinEvent shows WDAC Policy Integrity Error (Event ID 799) during early logon; LSA reports Smartcard logon path disabled due to code integrity failure; Intune device check-in stalls and never reaches "Compliant" state. Devices sometimes prompt for BitLocker recovery on first resume.

Expected behavior: WDAC policy should validate against the policy catalog shipped in the image; post-image registration should succeed, allowing SSO and Intune enrollment to complete without manual intervention.

Relevant logs & artifacts:
- C:\Windows\System32\winevt\Logs\Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity%4Operational.evtx shows Event 799 and code integrity hash mismatch entries.
- SCCM task sequence smsts.log entries show WDAC registration step completing with exit code 0 on some machines but event mismatch on others.
- USB-attached smartcard readers show driver load sequences in SetupAPI logs that overlap with policy registration on affected devices.

Temporary workaround: In depot, imaging techs can skip the WDAC registration step and instead stage a follow-up script that runs after first user login to register the WDAC policy (delays enforcement until authentication subsystems are fully initialized). This allows Intune enrollment to complete.

Notes: This appears correlated with a FW revision in the NVMe controller and a changed driver load timing on a subset of inventory. Hypothesis is a timing window between WDAC policy application and device driver signature validation leading to a transient policy hash recalculation.

Workaround implemented: Imaging team created corp-imaging-v3.4a which defers WDAC registration until after first-user login, allowing Intune/AAD join to complete. Depot technicians updated runbook and were instructed to apply deferred-registration variant for affected models. Long-term fix: Security and Endpoint Eng to coordinate with NVMe vendor and WDAC maintainers to ensure deterministic policy application; plan to update the task sequence to include a driver-init wait-step or registry flag to stabilize hash calculation. Follow-up ticket planned for FW/vendor engagement and permanent task-sequence change.
Preliminary RCA: A timing-dependent interaction between NVMe controller driver initialization (newer FW) and the WDAC policy registration step in the imaging sequence caused a non-deterministic recalculation of the policy/runtime hash. When the runtime hash differs at early boot, the code integrity subsystem rejects enterprise authentication paths until policy is re-registered under stable driver load ordering.
1) Use corp-imaging-v3.4a (deferred WDAC) in depot for Dell 5430 and X1 Carbon Gen11 until permanent fix is deployed.
2) If device is already affected, have depot tech login with local admin, run: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\scripts\deferred-wdac-register.ps1" to register the policy post-login and reboot.
3) If smartcard authentication still fails, escalate to Security with collected EventLog bundle (CodeIntegrity, System, SetupAPI).

title: Uneven quota enforcement for subpath routes causing intermittent 429s during signed URL fan-out
body:
Uneven quota enforcement for subpath routes causing intermittent 429s during signed URL fan-out

Issue summary: BrightCart reports intermittent 429s observed only during large import jobs that use signed upload URLs. The pattern is uneven: some files always succeed while others from the same job get rate limited. Impact: customer ingestion pipeline for product images stalls ~10-30% of files, causing downstream retry storms and timeouts in their processing queue. Environment: BrightCart on a Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-11) with inbound uploads routed through the signed-url service and an edge API gateway in us-east-1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a batch of 500 signed upload URLs from BrightCart UI. 2) Kick off 50 parallel worker processes (same host pool) to PUT files using signed URLs. 3) Observe successful 200s interleaved with 429s on a subset of PUT/POST calls. 4) Reduce parallelism to <8 workers and retries succeed without sustained 429s. Observed behavior: 429s appear within first 30s of a job and persist for several minutes. Throttled requests indicate tenant token exhaustion but the tenant quota dashboard shows credits still available. Temporary workaround: advise customer to stagger signed-url generation and reduce parallel PUT concurrency to 8-12 per host while we investigate.
2026-03-10 09:13 - Aisha Patel (Support): Logged initial report from BrightCart. Provided guidance on short-term concurrency limit and requested request_id headers for failing calls.
2026-03-10 11:02 - BrightCart (Customer): Provided sample request_ids: req_4729, req_4730, req_4731 and tcpdump of upload worker. Reported that signed URLs are created in one API call then distributed to workers.
2026-03-10 13:45 - Diego Morales (SRE): Correlated request_ids to edge logs. Noted that token accounting increments at edge ingress and again at signed-url validation path for some flows. Created hypothesis that subpath normalization mismatch causes double-counting for certain URL patterns.
2026-03-11 08:21 - Eng (Rate Limiter): Added debug hooks to rate-limiter in staging for subpath normalization. Observed that path suffixes containing query param order permutations were not canonicalized and resulted in per-route counters treating same logical route as multiple routes in the token window.
2026-03-11 15:10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Shared mitigation steps with customer (stagger and limit concurrency). Customer reported immediate reduction in 429s but wants permanent fix.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Diego Morales (SRE): Pushed a non-disruptive guard (edge filter) that normalizes signed-url paths for counting while we prepare a full patch. Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-12 17:42 - BrightCart (Customer): Confirmed error rate dropped from ~18% to ~1% after guard applied. Requested postmortem and clarification on configuration they can set in Console.
2026-03-12 18:05 - Diego Morales (SRE): Noted follow-up action items: backfill missing counts to reconcile billing, publish Console toggle 'Normalize signed-url path counting', and schedule full fix for next sprint. Linked PR created.
Findings: 1) The signed-url generator emits URLs with embedded query parameters in non-deterministic order. 2) Our edge token-accounting layer uses the raw request path+query as the key for per-route token buckets in the short refill window. 3) For some PUT flows an upstream validation request (signed-url verification) was hitting a different route variant before the actual upload, causing the tenant quota to be decremented twice in quick succession. 4) NAT/pooled IP reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing further amplify observed bursts because multiple logical connections map to the same client token window. Evidence: correlated edge logs (edge-logs-us-east-2026-03-10.gz) show paired count decrements for request_ids supplied by the customer. Rate-limiter debug trace: rl.trace.833123 shows double-debit events when query param order differs. Hypothesis: lack of canonicalization for signed-url subpaths + preflight validation calls leads to uneven quota consumption and perceived early exhaustion.
Workaround implemented: edge normalization filter that canonicalizes query parameter order and strips non-accounting prefixes from signed URLs; customer advised to limit parallel PUTs and to batch signed-url issuance with a small splay. Permanent fix: engineering PR https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/7890 implements canonicalization in the token-accounting path and adds a de-duplication check for back-to-back validation+upload pairs. Rollout notes: feature gated and deployed to us-east canary on 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC, monitored for 24 hours. Post-deploy result: BrightCart reported reduction of 429s to baseline. Follow-ups: (1) run a quota backfill job to reconcile short-lived double-debits and issue credits to affected billing accounts, (2) add Console toggle and documentation page explaining signed-url counting semantics, (3) schedule a runbook update for support. Related PRs and runbooks listed in metadata. Ticket to be closed after backfill complete and docs published.
Action items:
- ENG: merge PR and schedule full rollout to all dedicated regions (owner: Diego Morales)
- Billing: run reconciliation job for affected tenants (owner: Priya Gupta)
- Docs: add signed-url counting guidance and Console toggle documentation (owner: Laura Kim)

title: Tenant burst traffic caused cascading 502s at API proxy and unhealthy upstreams leading to runtime restarts
body:
Tenant burst traffic caused cascading 502s at API proxy and unhealthy upstreams leading to runtime restarts

AtlasRetail reported a sudden increase in 502 errors for their production routes after a traffic surge. Errors are observed at the API proxy layer with upstreams marked unhealthy and several serving runtime worker processes restarting under load. Customer reports higher latency and partial request failures across their pinned model routes.
~15% of requests for AtlasRetail returned 502 during the peak (12:10-12:35 UTC). Multiple realtime features degraded (recommendations and chat) for their enterprise customers. No broad customer-facing status page incident was triggered, but SLA exposure for this tenant is possible if unresolved.
Scale a single tenant's traffic from 50 RPS to 1200 RPS within 1 minute against pinned model route
Observe API gateway returning 502 and upstream health checks flipping to UNHEALTHY
Confirm serving-runtime worker processes restart logs and OOM/killed-by-kernel not present
Initial metrics show a sharp request concurrency spike for AtlasRetail routes starting 12:09 UTC
API gateway connection pool saturating: #active connections reached configured proxy limit and started returning 502 to client
Upstream health checks started failing 502/503 and api-gateway marked multiple serving-runtime instances as UNHEALTHY which triggered retries and increased load on remaining instances
Serving runtime logs show continuous eviction and GC spikes; not classical OOMs but process restarts correlated with high load and frequent cache thrashing
2026-03-13T12:12:07Z apigw[proxy-12] ERROR upstream response 502 for tenant=atlas_tenant route=/v1/generate
2026-03-13T12:12:09Z runtime[worker-7] WARN eviction: kv-cache thrash detected (cache miss ratio 86%)

title: Negative credit line and cents-level rounding discrepancy after clock-skewed usage postbacks from edge proxies
body:
Negative credit line and cents-level rounding discrepancy after clock-skewed usage postbacks from edge proxies

Issue summary: Customer Ledgerly reported a small negative credit line (-$0.03) on their monthly invoice for 2026-02-28. The credit references an automatic adjustment labeled 'hourly_metering_reconciliation'. Impact: customer is concerned about unexplained negative credit lines and cents-level rounding affecting their automated accounting exports. Environment: dedicated account, us-west serving region, hourly metering enabled, reserved capacity with burst.

Observed behavior: an automatic reconciliation job created a negative credit (-$0.03) on a line item for time window 2026-02-28T05:00:00Z-06:00:00Z. The customer says they did not change usage and their internal meter shows no duplicate requests in that hour.

Steps to reproduce observed invoice line (investigation reproduction steps):
1) Review ingestion logs for hourly aggregator for 2026-02-28 05:00 UTC.
2) Inspect postback event ordering for Ledgerly's edge proxies (proxy host ids: ledgerly-edge-01..03).
3) Replay postbacks into metering staging pipeline with original timestamps and with corrected NTP-synced timestamps.

Expected behavior: reconciliation job should create either zero net adjustment or a positive charge if duplicates were found; rounding should not create a negative credit unless a true overcount occurred.

Actual behavior: reconciliation computed a -$0.03 credit. Preliminary evidence shows out-of-order postbacks with timestamps ~30s earlier than upstream ingestion due to clock skew. The aggregator's dedupe logic used (event_id + timestamp) to detect duplicates; when an out-of-order postback arrived with a timestamp less than the previously recorded one, the reconciliation path applied a differential tariff (reserved->hosted) before rounding, producing a small negative residual credit after the rounding step.

Attachments: excerpts from ingestion logs, reconciliation job output (below) and meter postback payload samples included in comments.

Pull ingestion logs for account Ledgerly around 2026-02-28T05:00:00Z - 2026-02-28T05:05:00Z
Identify postback event_ids and their timestamps from ledgerly-edge-01..03
Replay the same postbacks into the metering staging pipeline and compare reconciliation outputs with production
Toggle NTP-corrected timestamp on edge postbacks and observe adjustment behavior
[2026-02-28T05:00:12.123Z] ingestion-service INFO received postback event_id=evt_7f8a account=ledgerly timestamp=2026-02-28T04:59:42Z host=ledgerly-edge-02
[2026-02-28T05:00:12.456Z] ingestion-service INFO received postback event_id=evt_7f8a account=ledgerly timestamp=2026-02-28T05:00:12Z host=ledgerly-edge-01
[2026-02-28T05:02:00.789Z] hourly-aggregator WARN duplicate detection: event_id=evt_7f8a seen with earlier timestamp 2026-02-28T04:59:42Z (current window 05:00)
[2026-02-28T05:02:01.002Z] reconciliation INFO computed_adj gross=0.24 applied_rate=0.10 adjusted_amount=-0.027 rounding_delta=-0.003 final_credit=-0.03
2026-03-10 10:22 - Aisha Patel: Opened on behalf of Ledgerly finance (attached invoice screenshot). They see a -$0.03 line labeled 'hourly_metering_reconciliation' and want explanation before they post month-end entries.
2026-03-10 14:04 - Marcus Chen: Assigned. Initial triage: looks like a reconciliation rounding edge-case. Asking SRE to pull ingestion logs + edge proxy timestamps. Filing INT ticket for deeper ingestion trace (INT-4812).
2026-03-11 09:30 - SRE (J. Alvarez): Found NTP drift on ledgerly-edge-02 (~30s behind) for the window. Two postbacks for same event_id arrived with different timestamps; our dedupe key includes timestamp which caused the reconciler to compute a differential. Copying sample logs to this ticket.
2026-03-11 11:18 - Marcus Chen: Replayed events into staging reconciler with both original and corrected timestamps. With corrected (NTP-synced) timestamps, no adjustment generated. With original out-of-order timestamp, reconciler produced -$0.03 due to reserved->hosted tariff interpolation followed by rounding. Will propose a fix to dedupe logic.
2026-03-12 08:05 - Ledgerly (M. Ito): Thanks for quick triage — they request a formal explanation and a one-time credit to avoid manual reconciliation on their side if fix will take more than 48 hours.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Marcus Chen: CS proposed temporary manual credit of $0.03; awaiting billing approval. Engineering to implement dedupe change to prefer event_id-only deduping (with timestamp used only for window assignment) — tracked in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412
Root cause hypothesis: edge proxies with NTP drift emitted duplicate postbacks with identical event_id but different timestamps. Aggregator dedupe key used (event_id + timestamp) causing the reconciliation path to treat the out-of-order record as a separate usage and then apply a retroactive differential adjustment when it observed the true ordering.
Tariff interpolation path: when an out-of-order event shifts assignment between reserved and hosted rate buckets within the same hour, the reconciler computes a fractional adjustment. The rounding function applied at final line-item level can produce small negative values in a tiny percentage of cases when the adjustment magnitude is near 0 and sign flips due to floating point/cent rounding.
Staging repro confirmed: replay with original timestamps reproduces -$0.03. Replaying with normalized NTP-corrected timestamps yields no adjustment.
Engineering proposes changing dedupe to key on event_id only and to perform window-assignment using the ingestion_arrival_time (server-side canonical time) rather than client-provided timestamp for dedupe decisions. Also add a final reconciliation floor to prevent sub-cent negative credits (treat adjustments < $0.01 as zero) and log hits for auditing.
Pending billing approval for one-time manual credit of $0.03. Engineering PR merged to staging (https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412) implementing event_id-only dedupe and final-floor logic. Rollout plan: canary to prod-us-west on 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-17. Once change is in prod, we will reverse the manual credit if not required.
Billing: approve one-time $0.03 manual credit to Ledgerly and notify finance for entry (action owner: T. Nguyen)
SRE/Edge: ensure ledgerly-edge-02 NTP sync patch applied; confirm no further drift (action owner: J. Alvarez)
Engineering: monitor reconciliation-floor hits for next 7 days post-rollout and report any occurrences (action owner: Marcus Chen)
CS: send formal explanation and remediation plan to Ledgerly and confirm acceptance (action owner: Aisha Patel)

title: Negative invoice line after mid-cycle reserved swap and delayed postback in EUR->USD billing
body:
Negative invoice line after mid-cycle reserved swap and delayed postback in EUR->USD billing

Issue summary:
Customer report: AtlasHealth AI discovered a negative invoice line (-0.02 EUR) on their finalized invoice for billing period 2026-02-15 -> 2026-03-15 after they performed a mid-cycle reserved capacity swap (hosted -> dedicated) and associated tariff change. The negative line caused autopay failure and flags in their accounting system.

Impact:
- Finalized invoice shows a -0.02 EUR line labelled 'currency-reval-adjustment' which led to invoice being flagged.
- Customer requests an explanation and immediate credit to allow autopay to succeed.
- Affects a small number of invoices for other dedicated customers that performed mid-cycle reserved swaps (suspected).

Environment:
Prod (eu-west). Dedicated reservation id: resv-az-77. Customer account id: acct-ATLAS-77. Billing conversion: EUR -> USD internal rate applied on 2026-03-01.

Steps to reproduce (reported):
1) Customer executed reserved swap on 2026-02-28 at 18:47:02 UTC (hosted->dedicated) via Console.
2) Backend applied new reserved rate and currency conversion snapshot effective 2026-03-01 00:00:00 UTC.
3) Several asynchronous postbacks (batch embed completion + KV cache warmups) from eu-edge were received late (2026-03-01 02:12:33 UTC onwards) and processed by postback-processor.
4) Finalized invoice generated 2026-03-05 included a -0.02 EUR adjustment line.

Observed behavior:
- Postbacks that arrived after the rate snapshot were revalued with the new conversion but a small rounding delta in the aggregator produced a negative micro-line when aggregated with prior pro-rated reserved credits.

Expected behavior:
- Late postbacks should be reconciled without producing negative invoice lines; any micro-deltas should be absorbed into smoothing or allocated to a 'micro-adjustment' bucket, not as a negative finalized line that blocks autopay.

Customer request:
- Immediate provisional credit for -0.02 EUR (or waiver) and written explanation.

- Ran billing aggregator in dry-run mode with original hosted rates vs post-swap rates; micro-deltas appear when pro-rate credits are merged with late postbacks re-valued at new rate.
Hypothesis:
- Rounding/allocations during cross-currency revaluation combined with pro-rated reserved credits produced negative residuals when aggregated into single invoice lines.
Next steps taken:
- Eng (Alejandro) opened quick PR to add micro-adjustment bucket to invoice finalizer for late postbacks (see PR 1428).
- Billing ops applied provisional waiver for acct-ATLAS-77 to unblock autopay (ticket to finance created).

title: Trace span anchor misalignment in console causing dashboard 'open logs' to jump to wrong time window
body:
Trace span anchor misalignment in console causing dashboard 'open logs' to jump to wrong time window

Issue summary: Customers using console trace links (Dashboard -> "open logs" / "view trace") are being taken to a time window that does not match the selected trace span. The link opens the logs 30–90 seconds earlier than the selected span, which breaks direct investigation workflows and correlating trace->log events.

Impact: Multiple enterprise customers (reported by NebulaPayments) are unable to correlate low-latency 5xx spikes with trace spans during cross-region fallbacks. This increases MTTI and requires manual time adjustments in Kibana. Not a full outage but blocks timely RCA for P1 incidents.

Environment: Production console, traces collected via obs-ingest and forwarded to the tracing indexer; customers on dedicated routing with cross-region fallback enabled. Problem reproducible most frequently when the original request is routed from eu-west to us-east and the console trace span includes multiple 'fallback' child spans.

Observed behavior: Clicking the dashboard trace tile opens the trace viewer and then the "Open Logs" link directs to the logging console with a start time ~30–90s earlier than the selected span start. The time window width appears correct but the anchor is shifted.

Expected behavior: The console should open logs anchored to the exact span start time (with a small tolerance of +/-2s) and preserve the same trace id in the log query so engineers can immediately see the related logs.

Relevant links: NebulaPayments tenant dash with reproducer: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/nebula/payments/dash/trace/rcv-20260309-11 
Tracing sample span: trace-id=994f8c2aef32
Console tracing trace viewer event: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/994f8c2aef32

Logs collected: Available in centralized logging with indices: traces-2026.03.09, logs-2026.03.09. Kibana query examples and timestamps included in comments.
Login to console as NebulaPayments user and open the Payments SLA dashboard
Find a trace tile showing a cross-region fallback (eu-west -> us-east) and open the trace viewer
Note the span start/end times shown in the trace viewer and click 'Open Logs'
Observe the logs UI opens with a time window earlier than the span start (typically -30s to -90s)
Repeat with a non-fallback single-region trace — link anchors correctly (helps isolate cross-region path difference)
03/10 09:22 - Support triage: confirmed with customer video; reproduced in our staging with simulated cross-region fallback
03/10 11:05 - Hypothesis: timestamp normalization step in obs-ingest applies region-local clock adjustment when spans are merged across collectors; anchor uses merged trace timestamp while logs use original event timestamp
03/10 15:40 - Checked trace indexing pipeline: trace spans are merged by trace-id and then re-anchored using earliest span.start_time in the merged trace. Logs anchor generation code was using 'trace_timestamp' field emitted by trace-joiner service which currently records pre-merge collector-local time for fallback paths.
03/11 08:12 - Local repro: instrumented traces with a 45s synthetic clock skew; UI link anchored to 'trace_timestamp' not 'merged_span_start' in trace-joiner index. This reproduces observed offset.
03/11 14:30 - SRE note: cross-region fallback is expected to preserve original timestamps from the origin collector; we need to update trace-joiner to emit 'merged_start_time' and ensure console uses that field when generating log anchor queries.
03/12 10:04 - Workaround identified: console can use the earliest span.start_time from trace payload as a fallback if 'trace_timestamp' delta > 5s (temporary UI patch suggested), but full fix requires backend change and a small UI dropdown indicating source of anchor time.
03/13 09:00 - Created backend issue (INT-4110) to change trace-joiner emission and added unit test to ensure merged_start_time is used; change is non-breaking but requires rolling update to trace-joiner fleet across regions.

2026-03-10 10:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): 'Thanks Rachel — we've reproduced and escalated to SRE. Adding details and a reproducible capture.'

2026-03-11 11:20 - Engineer (Lina Zhao): 'Confirmed: trace-joiner populates trace_timestamp from the first collector event it receives; when fallback spans arrive later the merge adjusts span.start but does not update trace_timestamp. Console currently reads trace_timestamp for log anchor.'

title: Duplicate function/tool calls from Go SDK when behind corporate proxy that sanitizes idempotency header
body:
Duplicate function/tool calls from Go SDK when behind corporate proxy that sanitizes idempotency header

Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool/function invocations when using the Go streaming SDK behind their corporate HTTP proxy. Duplicate invocations are observed intermittently during streaming retries and on connection resume.

Impact:
- Customer observed duplicated payment authorization webhook calls which triggered duplicate downstream billing events for a small fraction of users (~0.4% of streams during peak).
- Affects production traffic for Acme Payments (dedicated account).

Environment:
- Customer: Acme Payments (dedicated)
- Region: prod-us-east
- SDK: redwood-go-sdk v1.3.7 (reported), also reproduced on v1.3.9 in our lab
- Proxy: Corporate HTTP proxy (SymProxyCorp 4.2) that performs header sanitization/normalization
- Model: redwood/gpt-4o-mini-2026 pinned in route config

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a streaming function-call flow from Go SDK with per-tool idempotency tokens (UUIDs).
2) Allow streaming to encounter a transient network blip; SDK reconnect/resume is triggered.
3) On resume, tooling observes the downstream webhook job executed twice for some sessions.
4) Observed pattern: duplicate function invocation when idempotency header values differ only by characters removed by proxy (e.g., dashes or upper-case characters).

Expected behavior:
- Each function/tool invocation should be executed at most once for a given idempotency token. Retries/resumes should not cause repeated side effects if the token is unique.

Actual behavior:
- The corporate proxy rewrites/sanitizes the idempotency header (drops non-alphanumerics, lowercases, collapses multiple header values). Different original idempotency tokens become identical after sanitization, causing server-side deduplication to consider separate requests identical or to mishandle header parsing, which in turn triggers re-execution in edge cases.

Logs / traces (redacted):
- request_id: req-20260310-7a9f3c (first attempt) -> function_call_id: fc-0a3b22
- request_id: req-20260310-7a9f3c-resume -> function_call_id: fc-0a3b22-2 (duplicate observed)
- HTTP header snapshot (from packet capture):
  - X-Redwood-Idempotency: "8f14-7A:9b-cc" (original from client)
  - X-Redwood-Idempotency: "8f147a9bcc" (after proxy sanitization)
- Server dedupe key logged as: "8f147a9bcc" for both requests

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Configure corporate proxy to preserve header value exactly (disable sanitization for X-Redwood-Idempotency) OR create an allowlist rule for that header.
- As an immediate SDK-side mitigation, set an explicit header name using the SDK option to use "X-Redwood-Idempotency-Base64" which encodes tokens in base64url (avoids characters proxies remove). This option is available as an experimental flag in SDK v1.4.0-beta and later.
- If proxy changes are not feasible, avoid using characters likely to be stripped (dashes, colons) by generating idempotency tokens as base64url strings in the application layer until a permanent fix is deployed.

- Packet capture snippet (redacted): s3://acme-poc/captures/2026-03-09-proxy-pcap-01
- Sample request IDs and webhook receipts included in ticket comment

Hypothesis 1: Corporate proxy normalizes or sanitizes header values, causing distinct client tokens to map to the same server-received token. Confirmed by pcap and local NGINX reproduction.
Hypothesis 2: Some proxies collapse multiple headers into a comma-separated single header value. Server-side parser treats comma-joined value differently leading to missed dedupe path. Confirmed in lab with comma-joined header simulation.
Finding: Server dedupe currently normalizes nothing and expects exact-match idempotency string. When proxy mutates header, dedupe misfires or treats resume as new request depending on how the token is parsed. Edge case observed when resume request arrives with two idempotency header fragments concatenated by proxy; server sees first fragment only and yields fallback to executing tool again.
Reproduction steps validated in lab using NGINX config 'merge_slashes off; proxy_set_header X-Redwood-Idempotency $http_x_redwood_idempotency;' with rewrite rules to strip non-alphanum. Behavior matches customer reports.
Short-term mitigations tested: application-level base64url tokens work; proxy allowlist eliminates issue. Experimental SDK flag that sets header name to X-Redwood-Idempotency-Base64 avoids proxies that only sanitize the canonical header name but not values encoded in base64url.
Long-term remediation options: (a) server-side canonicalization and strict validation + warning logs; (b) publish header allowlist guidance and SDK opt-in to encoded idempotency tokens; (c) add advisory guidance on proxies in onboarding docs for dedicated/private customers.
Risk assessment: low risk to platform correctness if customer proxies configured properly; medium risk of subtle duplicates across customers with aggressive proxies. Recommend proactive messaging in onboarding docs and SDK changes to minimize blast radius.

Recommended customer follow-up: keep proxy allowlist in place and instrument streams for 72 hours. Will track permanent fix in INT-4021; estimate 2 sprints for rollout and SDK stable release to v1.4.x with official base64url idempotency option.

SDK TASK: Expose stable option for base64url-encoded idempotency header and document in 'Idempotency and proxies' section
DOCS: Update onboarding guide for dedicated/private customers to include proxy allowlist example for X-Redwood-Idempotency

title: Corporate card reimbursement stuck in suspense due to PO allocation mismatch
body:

Issue summary: A corporate card transaction (employee reimbursement) is stuck in the finance suspense queue because the AP system rejected the invoice mapping to the Purchase Order. Impact: employee reimbursement delayed; month-end accruals understated for the GL code; finance cannot close the affected vendor ledger line.
