title: Erroneous reserve-credit offset after mixed quantized hosted + dedicated usage
body:
Erroneous reserve-credit offset after mixed quantized hosted + dedicated usage

Issue summary: BrightVoice Labs reports an apparent negative-line offset on their March 2 invoice where reserved capacity credits from Dedicated usage appear to have been offset by hosted quantized model consumption, resulting in a net negative charge line for reserve credits. Impact: customer-facing finance and accounting team is unable to reconcile month-to-date spend; they paused automated invoice reconciliation and requested audit. Environment: prod-us-west (primary), some batch runs in eu-west. Business impact: accounting hold, delayed month-end close, potential provisioning freeze if unresolved.

Observed behavior:
- On 2026-03-02 02:00-05:00 UTC, BrightVoice consumed dedicated reserved hours and concurrently sent bursts to hosted endpoints using the quantized variant of gpt-j-7b.
- The billing job that runs hourly produced a negative-line offset on invoice line item "Reserved Capacity Adjustment" totaling -$12,430.00 on the customer's billing ledger.
- Finance UI shows the reserve-credit as applied and then a second adjustment that nullified the reserved-credit without a matching reversal event.

Expected behavior:
- Reserved capacity credits should be applied against dedicated-hour usage only. Hosted usage (even if it uses quantized variants) should be billed separately and should not trigger negative reserve-credit offsets.

Steps requested from support:
1) Audit the ledger entries and provide a timeline of the adjustments.
2) Identify whether the hourly metering aggregation job double-applied reconciliations when mixed queues (dedicated + hosted quantized) were present.
3) Provide a provisional credit or hold adjustments until ledger is corrected.
4) Root cause and mitigation plan to prevent recurrence.

title: Unexpected model-pin transfer after prewarm expiry causes silent fallback and duplicate billing
body:
Unexpected model-pin transfer after prewarm expiry causes silent fallback and duplicate billing

Issue summary: Customer ClipperAI reports that during yesterday's staggered canary rollout their tenant traffic silently diverted to a degraded variant shortly after a prewarm step expired. Impact: multiple production requests returned the degraded model (gptx-3.0-quantized) for ~16 minutes and the customer observed a billing delta for both primary and degraded variant usage. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, tenant-specific routing with model pin grace-period configured to 30s, prewarm window configured to 5m.

Observed behavior: At 2026-03-09T22:14:05Z the canary prewarm job finished and the tenant had an active pin to redwood-v2-medium. At 2026-03-09T22:19:12Z the pin lease expired but instead of keeping the tenant on the primary variant until explicit commit, control-plane initiated a silent transfer that left some edge nodes routing to gptx-3.0-quantized. This created mixed responses and duplicate tallying in usage metrics.

Expected behavior: Pin grace-period expiry should not trigger an automatic model transfer during a staggered prewarm unless orchestration confirms cohort commit. Tenant should either remain on primary variant or be explicitly failed over with audit log and customer-visible event.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Create staged canary with staggered prewarm (prewarm 5m, pin grace 30s). 2) Finish prewarm then intentionally delay canary commit by ~2 minutes. 3) Observe edge routing and billing metrics for cross-variant request counts and check control-plane commit logs.

Business impact: Customer reported degraded quality for conversation flows and unexpected billing spike across both variants; they are asking for a remediation timeline and potential credits.

Deploy redwood-v2-medium as primary and gptx-3.0-quantized as canary degraded variant
Allow prewarm to complete then delay commit signal for >60s
Generate steady traffic from tenant and observe routing traces and usage counters

Hypothesis 2: orchestrator's pin handoff path contains a race where a failed prewarm/commit leaves metadata in "transfer_pending" state; edge reconciler treats transfer_pending as a valid variant
Observed: some edges reported decision_source=local-cache while control-plane recorded lease_expired and then later abort commit

Recommended mitigation applied for ClipperAI: extended tenant pin_grace to 120s and temporarily disabled staggered auto-commit in the dedicated pool. These changes prevented further mixed-routing during the next prewarm window.
Under investigation — initial SRE findings point to a race in the orchestrator's pin handoff logic where 'transfer_pending' metadata allowed edge reconcilers to consider the canary as active when central commit later aborted. Edge local-cache TTLs exacerbated the window of mixed routing.
In progress — hotfix PR to change transfer_pending semantics and add explicit 'force-hold-until-commit' flag for pin leases. Once validated, we'll coordinate a staged rollout and notify the customer. Billing has started credit assessment for the duplicated usage records.

title: Implement conditional Slack channel claim flow with TTL retention and Confluence seed + optional Jira project orchestration
body:
Implement conditional Slack channel claim flow with TTL retention and Confluence seed + optional Jira project orchestration

Issue summary: Request to build a conditional channel-claim automation that: (1) exposes a lightweight Slack 'Claim' button for ephemeral project channels, (2) when claimed creates a templated Confluence seed page and optionally provisions a scoped Jira project, and (3) applies a configurable TTL retention policy that auto-archives or marks channel for review when expiry reached.\n\nImpact: Currently teams manually claim ephemeral channels and create associated docs; channels either remain orphaned or get prematurely archived. This automation reduces orphaned channels, enforces retention guardrails, and ensures discoverability (seeded Confluence page). Helps compliance and on-call handoff for experiments.\n\nEnvironment: Production Slack workspace (redwood-prod), Confluence (prod), Jira (prod). Primary scope: public and private ephemeral channels created by self-service pod bootstrapping.\n\nRequest details:\n- Add a Slack workflow button (or message action) \"Claim channel\" that opens a small modal: owner, team, expected TTL (7/30/90 days), opt-in for Jira project creation.\n- On claim: create Confluence seed page from a template (metadata: channel-name, owner, claim-date, TTL), tag page with 'ephemeral-claimed', and post link to channel.\n- If Jira project requested: call existing provisioning webhook to create a lightweight project with restricted permissions and link project key in Confluence.\n- TTL enforcement: scheduled job evaluates claimed channels; for channels approaching TTL-7d send reminder DM to owner; at TTL expiry automatically archive channel or mark for retention-review (based on channel policy).\n- Audit: write claim, reminders, archive actions to central audit log (Confluence page comment + centralized log file + optional S3 export).\n\nAcceptance criteria, rollout plan, and runbook details below.

title: Edge connection pool timeout leads to orphaned SSE stream coroutine and mid-generation silence
body:
Edge connection pool timeout leads to orphaned SSE stream coroutine and mid-generation silence

Issue summary: Customers reported SSE/chat streams that begin producing tokens but then stop sending any bytes for >30s without an explicit error. The client stays connected; no socket close is observed from the client side. Impact: multiple NoteHub users experienced mid-generation stalls that required them to cancel and resend prompts, impacting product UX and causing increased token replays. Environment: production us-east, dedicated cluster for NoteHub (tenant-id nh-894). Occurred 2026-03-09 22:12 - 23:45 UTC during a small traffic spike.
1) Create a long-form chat request that triggers >1000 token generation using redwood-13b-v1 via SSE streaming API
2) Route through the customer's dedicated endpoint in us-east (note: route uses edge-proxy connection pooling to backend cluster)
3) Simulate intermittent 503 from one backend worker for ~200-400ms to trigger edge pool failover
4) Observe SSE stream: initial tokens arrive, then stream becomes silent for >30s while client socket remains ESTABLISHED
Stream emits partial content and then stops sending further chunks without socket close or 5xx. Server-side worker logs show coroutine cancellation followed by no explicit release of the per-session KV cache. Edge logs show backend connection pooled socket timed out and was re-used. Retry/resume attempts from client sometimes result in duplicate session IDs and permanently paused generator coroutine on the worker node.
If a backend connection is timed out or pooled away, the platform should either gracefully resume generation on an available worker or return an explicit error to the client so the SDK can retry. No worker coroutine should be left indefinitely paused holding KV cache/state.

2026-03-10 03:15 - Support: validated customer reproduction with NoteHub engineer; captured pcap and SSE timeline.
2026-03-10 06:40 - SRE: correlated silence events with edge connection_pool idle_timeout log lines; hypothesized interaction between HTTP/2 pool reuse and in-flight streaming coroutines.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Runtime team: observed coroutine cancellation path that does not always run the full cleanup routine if cancellation originates from connection reset at the edge; KV cache lock can remain held leading to generator pause state.
2026-03-11 14:00 - Reproduced locally with controlled socket reset; confirmed that when edge reassigns a socket mid-stream, worker might transition to a 'paused' coroutine state if the resume handshake from edge is missing the session handshake header X-RW-Stream-Session.
Hypothesis: a) Edge pool re-use causes RST/timeout followed by reuse without performing full stream handshake; b) Runtime's stream-resume path assumes either full reconnect or full close; intermediate state leaves coroutine paused and does not emit heartbeat leading to silent stall.
Alyssa Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after customer call. Attached client-side capture and timestamps. Customer reports 30-90s stalls where token generation resumes only after new request.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial triage suggests edge connection_pool config and runtime coroutine cancel path are involved. Escalating to runtime oncall.
Maya Gupta (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-11: Reproduced with harness. Adding instrumentation to mark session handed-off and ensure resume handshake includes X-RW-Stream-Session. Will push debug build to staging.
NoteHub Eng (customer) 2026-03-11: We're seeing this primarily during our peak ingestion where we have many concurrent long-chat streams. Happy to test changes in a staging mirror.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-11): 1) Edge: increased connection_pool idle timeout from 10s to 45s for NoteHub tenant to reduce mid-stream socket reassignments. 2) Support: advised customer SDK to fallback to non-streaming (polling) for long jobs as short-term mitigation. Permanent fix (in progress): Runtime patch to ensure coroutine cancellation triggers full session cleanup and to make resume handshake idempotent. Edge change to ensure any socket handed to a new request performs a full stream-session handshake or returns 409 if session mismatch. Target PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1874. Follow-ups: automated test for socket-pool reuse + streaming, postmortem document and rollout plan.

title: DNS answer oscillation from split-horizon forwarder causes control-plane backoff and serving-node selection flap
body:
DNS answer oscillation from split-horizon forwarder causes control-plane backoff and serving-node selection flap

Issue summary:
Customers on private deployment (CerebriX) reported intermittent 5xx control-plane errors and repeated model-serving node re-selection. Impact observed as increased tail latency for inference calls and occasional failed request routing to serving nodes.

Impact:
- ~10-15% of requests to Redwood API return control-plane 503 or experience >2s additional latency during spike windows.
- Serving node selection (by control-plane) flips between two AZ-local endpoints every ~90s causing in-flight connection resets and KV cache warm-up penalties.

Environment:
- Private deployment behind customer-managed split-horizon DNS forwarder and corporate firewall.
- Region: us-east-1, deployment: private VPC with VPCE to control-plane.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run continuous generation load against the API (100 rps) for 10 minutes.
2) Observe intermittent 503s and increased p99 latency.
3) On control-plane, tail logs show frequent health-check failures and node eviction/reattachment.

Observations / Logs:
- Control-plane logs show repeated cache-miss and re-resolve for serving nodes: "Resolver: received 2 different answers for service.redwood.svc - switching" every ~80-100s.
- tcpdump performed by customer on forwarder captured alternating A records from two resolvers with different TTLs (60s vs 300s).
- dig +short @10.0.0.2 service.redwood.svc returned IP set A, then B on subsequent queries; dig on port 53/udp sometimes returned "Truncated" and the forwarder fell back to TCP and returned a different IP order.
- Control-plane backoff logic (designed to avoid thrash) triggered and momentarily suspended sticky routing, causing selection to re-evaluate and pick different node.

Immediate customer impact: ongoing - customers report production errors and elevated latency.

1) Initial hypothesis: upstream split-horizon DNS forwarder is returning different IP sets due to inconsistent resolver responses; control-plane treats differing answer sets as topology change and triggers rebalancing.
2) Correlation observed between DNS TTL oscillation and serving-node flaps; when TTL decreased to 60s client-side re-resolve frequency increased and exposed alternating answers.
3) Packet captures show UDP responses occasionally truncated (EDNS0 buffer size mismatch). When truncation occurs, forwarder falls back to TCP and queries a different authoritative path (via corp DNS forwarder chain) which returns a different IP ordering and TTL.
4) Control-plane currently performs an answer-set comparison to detect endpoint changes; differing order or slight TTL variations are interpreted as a substantive change.
5) Customer's forwarder has a feature that performs parallel queries to two upstream resolvers (internal authoritative and corporate resolver) and races the earliest response. This racing combined with UDP truncation/TCP fallback created non-deterministic answers.
6) Metrics: elevated control-plane re-resolve count from 12/min -> 95/min during incident windows; correlated with increase in dig truncation events and tcp retransmits.

Key artifacts attached (copied into ticket):
- excerpt of tcpdump (udp/truncation timestamps)
- control-plane resolver debug logs (timestamps and answer-sets)
- customer dig sequence showing alternating answers and TTLs

Temporary workaround: pinned service.redwood.svc to a stable IP set on customer's forwarder and increased local DNS cache TTL to 300s to reduce re-resolve frequency.

Permanent actions planned:
- Short term (patch within 72h): Change control-plane resolver logic to treat answers as a set (order-insensitive) and tolerate TTL variance up to 5% before triggering topology re-eval. (PR #7842)
- Medium term: Add optional jitter and debounce window for re-resolve-triggered rebalancing to avoid reacting to transient DNS races.
- Customer ops recommendation: align EDNS buffer size with corporate resolver and disable parallel-racing feature on forwarder if split-horizon behavior is required.

- Alert: if control-plane resolve-rate > 50/min for customer => page oncall.
- Dashboard: DNS truncation events and tcp fallbacks correlated with control-plane re-resolves.
Workaround applied; fix in PR review. Monitoring enabled; customer to confirm stability for 72h before closing.

title: Staged proxy window shift suppresses final paragraph on streaming resume for large HTML responses
body:
Staged proxy window shift suppresses final paragraph on streaming resume for large HTML responses

Issue summary: Customer reports that when a long streaming response (HTML-encoded, ~2.5k chars) is interrupted and the client resumes via SSE, the final paragraph (usually the last ~120-300 chars) is missing from the assembled output. The problem appears only when the request path traverses two chained proxies (Corp CDN -> customer edge proxy) that perform HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 conversion and have differing idle/keepalive settings.

Impact: Affects production users at BlueArc Health with private deployment. Missing concluding sentences in generated reports cause critical downstream ingestion failures (data validation rejects the document). Approximately 3–7% of resumed streams in this customer's traffic show the symptom during peak hours.

Environment: prod | us-east | private deployment behind corporate CDN + customer edge proxy.

1) Create a long HTML streaming request via SSE that produces a ~2.5k char response (we used a summarization prompt producing HTML lists and a closing paragraph).
2) Route traffic through staged proxies: our edge (envoy-based) -> customer CDN that performs h2->h1 conversion and buffers small chunks.
3) Trigger an interruption (network flake) mid-stream so client reconnects and performs resume.
4) Observe assembled stream at client; compare original vs resumed output.

Repro script used: curl --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' "https://api.redwood.example/sse?model=rw-gpt-8k&stream=true" then induce TCP RST on the middle proxy for 1–2s to force a resume.

When resume happens behind the chained proxies, the final paragraph is truncated entirely in some sessions. In other sessions the final paragraph arrives but the trailing metadata event ('event: end') is duplicated and the parser rejects the payload. Binary/special HTML entities like & and < are sometimes split across chunk boundaries and not reassembled correctly, producing corrupted final markup.
Logs show resume delta mismatches: worker logs report resume_offset 12478 but incoming bytes resume at 12452; edge-proxy logs show a buffered flush at the same time with a rewrite of chunk framing.

On resume, the assembled stream should contain the complete final paragraph and a single well-formed terminal metadata event. HTML entities should not be corrupted by chunk boundary manipulation. Resume offset calculations should map to logical token/byte offsets so no bytes are dropped.

[serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T08:17:21.452Z INFO request_id=abc123 resume_requested offset=12478
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-10T08:17:21.460Z DEBUG connection=conn-33 flush_buffer length=512 coalesce=true
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-10T08:17:21.461Z WARN rewriting: h2->h1 content-length injected=chunked
[worker-12] 2026-03-10T08:17:21.492Z ERROR reassembly: expected_end_offset=12603 actual_last_received=12579 keys mismatch
[client SDK] 2026-03-10T08:17:21.500Z INFO reconnect sequence=6 resume_token=tok-9 last_chunk_hash=0x7a1f

- Replicated in staging with a two-proxy chain that mirrors customer's timeout settings (customer edge: 60s idle, corp CDN: 15s idle).
- When corp CDN aggressively coalesces small keepalive frames and converts h2->h1, the byte boundaries we rely on for resume deltas shift by small amounts (tens to hundreds of bytes).
- Hypothesis: resume protocol currently assumes a stable mapping between server-side byte offsets and client-visible chunk boundaries. Chained proxies that rewrite HTTP framing break that assumption.
- Found one correlated pattern: sessions where corp CDN performed a buffered flush during the last heartbeat/keepalive before the connection drop had the highest failure rate.
- SDK behaviour: older JS SDK (v1.3.2) retries resume with chunk-based offsets; newer SDK includes an experimental header 'X-RW-Resume-Mode: token' which uses token-level checkpoints; still under test.
- Edge-proxy change in PR #5287 attempted to mark streaming responses as 'connection: keep-alive' and add a boundary marker for our runtime; initial tests reduce but do not eliminate the failure (still occurs when CDN rewrites content-length).

1) Use websocket streaming instead of SSE for affected clients (bypasses HTTP framing conversion at CDN).
2) Upgrade JS SDK to v1.4.0-beta which enables 'X-RW-Resume-Mode: token' to use token checkpoints rather than raw bytes.
3) Configure customer CDN to disable h2->h1 coalescing for streaming endpoints (if possible).

- Short term: update edge-proxy to emit a robust resume boundary marker (both content and a sideband 'resume-checkpoint' header) so downstream rewrites can preserve mapping. This is the change in PR #5287; needs further hardening to survive content-length injection.
- Medium term: extend resume protocol so server and client negotiate resume-mode: byte vs token vs sequence; prefer token-mode for multi-proxy topologies.
- Long term: add a validation handshake where the runtime returns a short suffix hash (SHA1) for the last N bytes before disconnect; on resume the client verifies hash and requests retransfer for any mismatch.

In Progress — edge-proxy PR #5287 deployed to staging and reduced failure rate from ~5% to ~0.7% in replicated tests. Next steps: iterate on handling of CDNs that inject content-length and run a controlled customer bypass test.

Elena Park (Support) 2026-03-10: Collected sample IDs and stack traces from BlueArc; customer sees issue ~3% of resumed streams.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-11: Replicated with env config; confirmed corp CDN h2->h1 coalescing reproduces symptom.
Priya Shah (Platform) 2026-03-12: Working on adding resume-checkpoint header to edge-proxy; will post canary tomorrow.

title: Cosine similarity saturation for int8-packed embeddings causing many-tied top-k and p99 rerank latency spikes
body:
Cosine similarity saturation for int8-packed embeddings causing many-tied top-k and p99 rerank latency spikes

Issue summary:
Customers report that after we enabled the new fast_pack int8 embedding pipeline in front of the reranker, rerank responses intermittently return a large number of ties in top-k (many items with identical cosine scores) and reranker p99 latency increases from ~120ms to >2s. Impact: LexiSearch search quality degraded (user-visible duplicate results) and backend tail latency caused timeouts in their UI.

Observed behaviour:
- Endpoint returns candidate lists where many top-k items have identical similarity scores (to 6 decimal places) leading to unstable ordering.
- Reranker falls back to CPU ANN path on tie-handling code path causing p99 latency spikes and occasional 502s.
- Problem started after a staged rollout (fast_pack=true) of the embeddings-service on 2026-03-08.

Environment details:
- Customer on dedicated plan (enterprise) using model alias open-embed-1024.
- Traffic flows through api-gateway -> embeddings-service (quant pack) -> indexer -> reranker.
- Observed in us-west and eu-central production regions, intermittent (approx 0.5-2% of requests).
1) Use LexiSearch test account with their dataset (shared via secure S3 link in ticket).
2) Send batch of 256 document embeddings via embeddings endpoint with header X-Embed-Pack: fast_pack and algorithm=int8.
3) Call /rerank endpoint with those embeddings and same model alias. Observe top-k equal scores and slow responses on ~1% of requests.
4) Repeat without fast_pack header (server falls back to fp16 path) — behaviour not reproduced.
5) Reproduce reliably in a canary deployment when canary has mixed replicas (some still on old packing).
2026-03-10: Initial hypothesis - int8 packing algorithm reduces dynamic range for this customer's corpus (many near-identical vectors) causing cosine similarity quantization and ties.
Reproduced in staging when mixing packed-int8 replicas with fp16 replicas — tie rate increases when some upstream replicas return packed payloads with slightly different normalization handling.
Observed that the fast_pack pipeline applies a per-shard min-max scale before int8 quantization; small differences in scaling across replicas (floating point rounding) is producing identical integer vectors after packing for different originals.
Tie-handling code in reranker falls back to an expensive CPU-based stable-sort when more than 16 exact-equal scores are present; this is the immediate driver of p99 latency spikes.
Related linked issues: SUP-331210 (embed-timestamp-drift-cache-missstorms) — customer was part of same canary cohort; may have increased cache churn.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after customer LexiSearch reported production impact. Provided initial logs and dataset slice to Eng. Customer experiencing duplicates in top-10, p99 latency > 1.5s.
Customer (LexiSearch SRE - Jordan Park) - 2026-03-10: We saw the issue surface after the new packing flag was enabled for our tenant; disabling it returned behavior to normal. Happy to provide traffic trace and emb payloads.
Eng (Marco Liu) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging. Confirmed tie rate correlates with packed-int8 path. Hypothesis: per-shard quant scale rounding causing integer collisions. Investigating whether normalization is applied pre-pack consistently.
Eng (Priya Sharma) - 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation: added server-side post-unpack epsilon jitter to break exact ties before tie_resolver threshold; added feature flag to disable jitter for testing. Preparing PR to make tie-resolver threshold adaptive.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12: Communicated temporary mitigation to customer; LexiSearch enabled jitter on their tenant and reported reduction in duplicates. Requested ETA for permanent fix and rollout plan.
2026-03-09T18:12:03Z embeddings-svc[replica-12] WARN QuantPack: detected high-value clustering after pack -> variance=2.3e-9
2026-03-09T18:12:03Z reranker[replica-7] ERROR tie_resolver: candidate_scores all_equal_count=48, fallback_to_cpu=true, elapsed_ms=1876
2026-03-09T18:12:03Z api-gateway TRACE req_id=abc123 status=504 downstream_timeout=true
Temporary mitigation deployed to affected canaries: server-side epsilon jitter added after unpack to break exact integer collisions (feature-flagged). A code change was merged (reranker PR #980) to make the tie-handling threshold adaptive and avoid CPU fallback for moderate equality clusters. Embeddings team opened PR #2244 to harmonize per-shard scaling and ensure normalization occurs pre-pack consistently. Next steps: staged rollout of packing fix in embeddings-service, monitor tie-rate and p99 latency, and add an integration test that simulates near-colocated vectors to prevent regressions. Customer notified and will remain on monitor for 72 hours; support to follow up for SLA credits if issue recurs.
1) Embeddings: make per-shard scale deterministic across replicas and add pre-pack L2-normalization (PR #2244).
2) Reranker: remove expensive CPU fallback path for equal-score clusters <64 and replace with fast tie-breaker that preserves determinism (PR #980).
3) Add synthetic suite test covering pack->unpack roundtrip for corpora with low variance to CI.
4) Post-deploy: monitor tie-rate, p99 latency, and customer-reported duplicates for 7 days and report back to LexiSearch.

title: HSM-signed idempotency token truncated by edge proxy on Private deployment causing duplicate function-call executions across SDKs
body:
HSM-signed idempotency token truncated by edge proxy on Private deployment causing duplicate function-call executions across SDKs

Issue summary:
Customer running Redwood Private behind a customer-managed edge proxy + HSM for signing idempotency tokens reports duplicate external tool/function executions originating from function-calling requests. The idempotency token is produced by the customer's HSM-signing flow and attached as X-Idempotency-Sig header.

Impact:
- Duplicate function calls (webhook/post) observed intermittently for high-value payments related workflows.
- Duplicates occur across both Go and Python SDK clients used by the customer.
- Customer is on a Private deployment with an on-prem edge proxy that performs header processing.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) deployed in us-east
- Customer HSM: Vault HSM-backed transit/signing
- SDKs: go-sdk v1.8.2, python-sdk v2.1.0
- Customer edge proxy: Envoy v1.28 with custom header sanitizer filter

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Client generates idempotency payload: JSON blob (request_id, ts, action, args).
2) Customer code signs payload with HSM (RSASSA-PSS, signature length ~512 bytes) and base64url-encodes signature.
3) Signature is sent in X-Idempotency-Sig header to Redwood Private endpoint via Envoy.
4) On occasional requests, the downstream Redwood runtime receives a truncated header value (first ~256 chars) and treats it as a distinct idempotency token, allowing duplicate tool invocation when client retries.

Expected behavior:
- Signed idempotency tokens should be treated as opaque strings and never truncated by proxies or any inline middleware. SDKs and server should use the full header value for deduplication.

Observed behavior:
- Envoy filter appears to truncate/normalize long header values (observed limit ~256 characters) when forwarding requests to backend.
- When truncated, the token no longer matches the original HSM-signed value; server records a different idempotency key and executes the function call again.
- Duplicates are reproducible when customer forces long signatures by switching from RS256 to RSASSA-PSS (longer output).

Relevant logs (customer-provided):
- Client send: X-Idempotency-Sig: AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABAQC3...<512-char base64url>
- Backend received: X-Idempotency-Sig: AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABAQC3...<truncated to ~256 chars>
- Redwood runtime trace: dedup lookup miss -> function.exec id=fn-7623 created -> webhook POST sent -> external system processed twice

Attachments provided by customer: edge proxy config snippet, HSM signing config, request/response HAR samples.

Initial hypothesis and notes:
- Likely root cause: customer-managed Envoy header sanitization and/or internal header size limits on the proxy. Could also be an HTTP/2 header compression/continuation framing bug when large header values are present.
- Possible mitigation: recommend switching to short deterministic idempotency keys (e.g., HMAC-SHA256 of payload truncated to 64 chars) or pass signature in request body rather than header. However, customer requires header approach for routing.

Next steps (in-progress):
- SRE to reproduce locally with Envoy + HSM-signed long header values (INT-2022).
- Confirm server side will treat X-Idempotency-Sig as opaque and not perform internal normalization/truncation.
- Provide guidance to customer on Envoy config to allow long headers and ensure HTTP/2 continuation frames preserved.
- If Envoy behavior is unavoidable in their environment, propose SDK guidance and code samples to produce shorter canonical idempotency tokens that still provide collision resistance.

title: Large artifact (model shard) download stalls over VPCE + IPsec tunnel due to DF-bit/PMTU blackhole
body:
Large artifact (model shard) download stalls over VPCE + IPsec tunnel due to DF-bit/PMTU blackhole

Issue summary: Customers report intermittent stalls when Redwood private deployment attempts to download large model shard objects (range GETs) over a VPCE path that traverses an on-prem IPsec/MPLS tunnel. Impact: model pulls fail or hang for minutes causing serving nodes to fail healthchecks and autoscale. Root suspicion is DF-bit interplay and PMTU discovery being blocked by an intermediate firewall appliance, creating a blackhole for large TCP segments.

Impact: Several production serving nodes entered degraded state causing increased latency and two autoscale events. Customer observed repeated chunk retries and eventual fallbacks to smaller shards which increased latency and cost.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC + VPCE to S3), on-prem termination via IPsec to a third-party WAN appliance. Artifact downloader uses ranged HTTP(S) GETs for shard streaming. VPCE configured with prefix lists and NAT/Egress appliances on customer's transit path.

Observed behavior: TCP connections for large range requests establish successfully then stall after transfer hits ~1450-2800 bytes per segment boundary depending on egress path. Packet captures show IP header DF=1 and intermittent ICMP "Fragmentation needed" (Type 3 Code 4) being produced by an intermediate device, but those ICMP packets are not reaching the client (likely filtered). When ICMP is blocked, senders retransmit and eventually time out, causing the downloader to retry smaller ranges and ultimately fail if retries exceed thresholds.

Expected behavior: Path MTU discovery should either receive ICMP PMTU messages so endpoints lower MSS/fragment appropriately, or the tunnel/egress should allow fragmentation/clear the DF bit so large shards stream successfully.

Reproduction window: Issue reproduced during a controlled test using 256MB shard GETs while toggling WAN optimizer features on the customer's edge appliance.

Attachments: pcap snippets, traceroute --mtu output, downloader logs with byte offsets and retry counts are attached in ticket attachments.
1) Deploy private agent in customer VPC with VPCE to S3 and route default egress via customer transit (IPsec).
2) Trigger model download of large shard (256MB) via Redwood artifact-downloader using ranged GETs (concurrent ranges).
3) Observe transfer progress; capture tcpdump on serving node and on the VPCE/egress device.
4) Toggle WAN optimizer / IPSec fragmentation settings on the on-prem appliance and repeat transfers to see differences.
5) Run traceroute/mtr with packet sizes and check for ICMP Type 3 Code 4 responses.
artifact-downloader.log: 2026-03-09T14:12:03Z GET /bucket/shard-0001 Range=bytes=0-4194303 200 partial content; progress stops at ~1.5MB; retry count increments.
tcpdump-serving-node.pcap.gz: packets show IP DF=1 on outbound segments; no matching ICMP reaching node; several retransmits and dup acks.
egress-appliance.log: 2026-03-09T14:12:04Z 'Fragmentation needed' sent to 10.1.2.5 but dropped by firewall upstream (ICMP blocked by policy).
traceroute-mtu: shows first hop MTU 1500, then 1400 over IPsec tunnel (ESP+FRAG mismatch).
Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage — customer reports 2x serving nodes failed healthchecks during model bootstrap. Suspect PMTU/DF issues because serving logs show stalls at consistent offsets.
Customer (NimbusHealth): Confirmed WAN vendor recently enabled 'DF-preserve' on transit firewall as part of an optimization; rolling back that change temporarily reduces failures.
Marco Ruiz (SRE): Requested pcap on both sides of VPCE and IPsec tunnel. Observed ICMP Fragmentation Needed generated by the tunnel egress but blocked by an upstream inspection appliance.
Marco Ruiz (SRE): Implemented temporary workaround to reduce downloader range window to 1MB on agent (config override) for customer's private deployment; transfer completed reliably during test.
Customer (NimbusHealth): Will coordinate with WAN vendor to either allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 or enable MSS clamping on the NAT/egress device.
Hypothesis: Intermediate firewall or WAN optimizer is blocking ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages and/or preserving DF bit across tunnel encapsulation, preventing endpoints from lowering MSS leading to packet blackholing.
Evidence: PCAP shows outbound TCP segments with DF=1 and subsequent 'Fragmentation needed' logged on egress appliance but no ICMP seen on serving node capture; traceroute-mtu exposes MTU mismatch on IPsec tunnel (1400) vs host (1500).
Triage steps: reproduced with jumbo ranged GETs; toggling DF-preserve setting on customer's WAN appliance made issue appear/disappear. Reducing range size or enabling MSS clamp fixes in tests.
Related config: VPCE uses prefix list + egress NAT device that does not perform MSS clamping. IPsec tunnel uses ESP without fragmentation support at vendor default.
Temporary workaround applied: configured customer's private agent to use smaller concurrent range window (1MB) and backoff retries; this restored shard downloads for the current deploys.
Customer applied immediate mitigation with WAN vendor: enabled MSS clamping on transit NAT/egress appliance and allowed ICMP Type 3 Code 4 from the IPsec egress to propagate back to the client side.
Permanent fix options presented: 1) Configure customer edge to perform MSS clamping at tunnel ingress/egress; 2) Update IPsec/ESP tunnel to allow fragmentation or to perform fragmentation before encapsulation; 3) Greenwood (artifact-downloader) change to adaptive chunking and fallback to smaller range sizes on DF=1 detection. Customer chose option 1 + partial 3.
Related PR merged: artifact-downloader PR #412 adds adaptive chunking when repeated stalls are detected (reduces default range size from 8MB to 1MB when PMTU signals are absent). Deployed to customer's agents on 2026-03-12.
Status: Customer confirmed stable downloads after combined mitigations; monitoring window started 2026-03-12 00:00Z.
PMTU blackhole caused by DF-bit preservation across IPsec + an upstream firewall blocking ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' messages, combined with artifact-downloader default large range sizes that exceeded the effective MTU on the encapsulated path.
1) Ops: Add a small PMTU detection check in private-deploy agent boot to detect obvious MTU mismatches and recommend MSS clamping if needed.
2) Engineering: Backport adaptive-chunking downloader logic to the stable agent channel and add a configuration flag 'force_small_ranges' for emergency support overrides.
3) Support: Create KB article outlining steps for customers and WAN vendors (MSS clamping, allow ICMP type3, IPsec fragmentation settings).
4) Security/Policy: Validate that recommending ICMP allowances is acceptable for enterprise security teams and provide hardened guidance (source-limited ICMP).
5) Postmortem: Draft incident postmortem and share with customer and internal stakeholders (owner: Marco Ruiz).

title: Intermittent dashboard metric drop and missing trace-links during ingestion backoff window

title: Midday burst causes repeated throughput collapses and GPU allocation failures for AtlasAI dedicated pool — suspected short-lived-stream thrashing (noisy tenant)
body:
Midday burst causes repeated throughput collapses and GPU allocation failures for AtlasAI dedicated pool — suspected short-lived-stream thrashing (noisy tenant)

Issue summary: AtlasAI reports repeated midday drops in end-to-end throughput (p50 throughput falls ~40%, p99 latency spikes >5x) on their dedicated pool during a customer load window (approx 12:00–13:30 UTC). The failure mode includes failed GPU allocations for new requests, high queue depth, and a short-lived pattern of many tiny streams that appear to 'thrash' batch slots. Impact: production degradation for AtlasAI ML feature endpoints; customers see 5xx/timeout spikes and elevated token latency. Hypothesis: noisy tenant or short-lived ephemeral jobs creating slot churn combined with autoscaler cooldowns and insufficient burst headroom leading to temporary GPU shortages and preemption events.
1) Observe dedicated pool metrics for AtlasAI between 12:00 and 13:30 UTC on 2026-03-10.
2) Send a burst of 1000 short requests (approx 50–200 token responses each) across 30 concurrent clients to the customer's pinned route.
3) Watch scheduler slot allocation, GPU attach logs, and autoscaler events in the same window (k8s events + autoscaler audit).
4) Note that many streams are <300ms and cause rapid open/close of batch slots, increasing fragmented utilization.
5) Confirm that new requests either queue for >30s or return 503/504 while existing longer-lived streams complete.
6) Reproduce shows autoscaler did not open new nodes quickly due to a 10m cooldown and conservative scale-up policy.

Initial triage: confirmed spike window and correlated with a large number of short-lived streams from a single tenant (inbound request sampling showed 70% of streams <500ms).
Autoscaler behavior: scale-up cooldown of 10m and pod startup time ~3.5–4.5m meant new capacity did not arrive fast enough for the burst. Max_replicas for the pool was set to 8 — headroom was insufficient for the observed burst.
Scheduling details: we observed high slot fragmentation (fragment_ratio ~0.6) caused by many small streams preventing efficient packing into batches; batcher metrics show small-batch rate increased 7x during spike.
Node-level failures: transient NVML detach errors on 2 GPUs across two nodes (error code 43). Not a full GPU OOM, but caused momentary attach failures and contributed to reduced effective GPU count.
Evictions/preemption: cluster preemption removed several ephemeral pods (best-effort job) to free GPU but thrash continued from other ephemeral workloads on the same nodes.
No evidence of model-level regressions or kernel crashes; no new serving-runtime release at the time.
1) Temporary tenant-level concurrent request cap applied to AtlasAI pinned route (cap=150 concurrent short streams) at 2026-03-10T13:00Z to limit slot churn.
2) Raised dedicated pool max_replicas from 8 to 12 for the emergency window and lowered autoscaler cooldown to 2m as a mitigation (applied 2026-03-10T13:10Z).
3) Drained and reprovisioned two nodes that showed repeated NVML detach errors; NV driver updated on those nodes (rolled 2026-03-11).
4) Added temporary anti-affinity for ephemeral training/ephemeral batch jobs to avoid co-located noisy workloads on AtlasAI nodes.

1) Product: evaluate permanent autoscaler policy change for customer-dedicated pools to allow faster burst headroom (add configurable emergency_headroom param).
2) Infra: implement per-pool short-stream smoothing policy in the scheduler/batcher to reduce slot churn (throttle tiny streams or aggregate micro-batches).
3) SRE: run a 72-hour monitoring window with synthetic short-stream bursts against a staging mirror to validate mitigations do not cause regressions.
4) Customer success: discuss traffic-shaping options with AtlasAI and recommend client-side exponential backoff + jitter and/or prefix caching for small repeat requests.
5) Follow-up ticket to implement an automated recovery action for transient NVML detach errors (SUP-430210-FIX-DRIVER-ROLL).
Partial mitigation applied: temporary caps, raised pool max, and driver updates restored baseline throughput. Long-term fixes planned (autoscaler policy and batcher smoothing). Customer reports recovered at 2026-03-11; ticket remains open to track product/infra follow-ups.
Schedule incident debrief with AtlasAI and internal stakeholders (target date 2026-03-18).
Produce a short postmortem summarizing root cause (slot thrash from short-lived streams + autoscaler cooldown + transient GPU detach errors) and list action owners.
Track implementation of autoscaler emergency headroom and scheduler smoothing in a follow-up epic.

title: WAF header injection causes SSE resume to rebind to stale conversation snapshot; embedded image link dropped and duplicate system notes
body:
WAF header injection causes SSE resume to rebind to stale conversation snapshot; embedded image link dropped and duplicate system notes

Issue summary:
Customer reports that during SSE streaming sessions behind their corporate WAF an injected header (X-Cluster-Prefix) causes the service-side resume flow to attach the incoming reconnect to a stale conversation snapshot. Symptoms are: the final embedded image URL is omitted from the resumed stream and the stream contains duplicated system messages (two identical 'system: snapshot restored' events).

Impact:
- NovaDocs users see truncated output for image-heavy responses (image markdown point to null/missing).
- Duplicated system annotations confuse downstream parsers and client SDKs, leading to UI glitches.
- Affects small percentage of reconnects (~0.4% of sessions reported by customer during peak).

Observed behavior:
- Normal initial stream from model completes with image embed metadata.
- After a transient network drop and SSE reconnect, the resumed stream contains the final text but not the image_url field; instead a second system annotation appears before the final text.
- Replay logs show the resume request path includes the injected header value.

Hypothesis:
- The WAF injects X-Cluster-Prefix which changes the request routing key used by the edge layer when reconstructing resume state. The resume key lookup falls back to a different snapshot ID (an older snapshot with no image metadata) and also replays a 'snapshot restored' system event from that older snapshot; downstream reassembly merges the two sequences, producing duplicated system messages and missing final image_url.
1) Customer flow: use NovaDocs private tenant behind corporate WAF with header injection configured.
2) Start a SSE streaming generation that ends with an embedded image URL (example prompt attached).
3) Force a short network disconnect (client toggles offline for ~2s).
4) Let client reconnect and resume SSE.
5) Observe the resumed stream payload: missing image URL and duplicate system annotation.

Note: repro rate low locally; the problem is reproducible when the WAF inserts/rewrites X-Cluster-Prefix and edge picks up header during resume request.

[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] resume-lookup: computed_key=tenant:42:session:abc123 alt_key=cluster-17:tenant:42:session:abc123 -> matched snapshot id=snap-20260211-9 (stale)

[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] sdk-client: received system:event 'snapshot restored' then system:event 'snapshot restored' (duplicate)

2026-03-12 11:04 - Eng (Raj): Temporary mitigation deployed to staging: normalize resume key extraction to ignore X-Cluster-Prefix for /v1/stream/resume endpoints. Will push to prod after smoke tests.
2026-03-12 16:00 - NovaDocs-Support: Confirmed mitigation in prod toggled for their tenant; customer reports resumed streams now include image URL and no duplicate system messages in 5/5 recent reconnects.
Edge router's resume key algorithm concatenates: prefix_header | tenant_id | session_id if prefix_header exists. When WAF injects a cluster prefix, the computed key points to a different snapshot namespace.
Stale snapshots still stored for a period (30m) - resume will match the first snapshot found; when cluster prefix is present it yields an older snapshot with no attachments.
Local repro done by injecting X-Cluster-Prefix header into resume request; behavior matched customer logs. Unit tests for header-normalization absent prior to this report.
Related to prior resume-key bugs: linked to SUP-318207 where proxy rewrite caused truncated streams; pattern consistent: header/path rewriting affects resume namespace.
Hotfix rolled out: edge/router now strips X-Cluster-Prefix and similar WAF-inserted headers when computing resume lookup key for streaming resume endpoints. Patch: runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2897
Customer tenant-specific toggle applied while we fully validate (mitigation flag set for NovaDocs).
Post-deploy monitoring: added a resume-failure alert that fires if >0.1% of resumes return incompatible snapshot schema (attachment missing) over 5m window.
Follow-ups: (1) add unit + e2e tests for header normalization on resume, (2) update runbook to include WAF header check for streaming issues, (3) propose documentation blurb to recommend WAFs do not inject routing headers for resume-call paths.
Status: Mitigation applied and verifying. Recommend keeping ticket open until two full business days of normal traffic without regressions. Customer reported initial positive validation.

title: PXE boot timeout: initramfs checksum/ramdisk validation failure after BIOS firmware flash
body:
PXE boot timeout: initramfs checksum/ramdisk validation failure after BIOS firmware flash

Issue summary: After a coordinated BIOS firmware flash for a batch of staging workstations, ~12% fail PXE boot with a timeout during initramfs/ramdisk validation. Impact: Staging provisioning pipeline stalls, blocks test environment imaging, and increases re-image retries. No data loss; devices fail to reach SCCM task sequence.
Environment: Staging PXE fleet, us-east TFTP/PXE servers, BIOS versions updated to 1.23.4 on Dell/HP images. Boot path: UEFI PXE -> iPXE -> download initramfs and kernel -> initramfs checksum and signature verification -> mount ramdisk -> continue.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Flash BIOS 1.23.4 on a freshly provisioned Dell Latitude 7440.
2) Boot to network PXE (UEFI). 3) Choose provisioning task sequence. 4) Observe PXE log on server and client serial console.
Observed behavior: Client downloads kernel and initramfs, then stalls ~45s waiting for ramdisk verification; TFTP retransmits and eventually client times out with PXE timeout and reboots. Some clients proceed successfully; failure rate ~12% across batch.
Logs: Attached dmesg snippets, iPXE debug trace, and PXE server tftpd logs (filenames in attachments). iPXE shows 'initrd verification failed: signature mismatch' on failing hosts but succeeding hosts show valid signature and continue.
Initial hypothesis: BIOS firmware change affects UEFI runtime or Secure Boot variables leading to corrupted retrieval of initramfs or altered memory alignment that triggers signature check discrepancies. Alternative: race in PXE server compressed payload delivery, tied to a new kernel/initramfs size exceeding negotiated window with older NIC firmware.
Impact owner: Imaging/Provisioning team. Escalation path: Support -> Infra SRE -> Firmware vendor escalation if needed.
Flash BIOS 1.23.4 on supported model
Boot UEFI PXE and select provisioning task sequence
Monitor iPXE client console and PXE server logs for initramfs verification step
02/18: Priya verified failure reproduction on 3/25 devices in staging. 02/19: Collected iPXE logs and kernel/initramfs SHA256 manifests. 02/20: Noted that failing hosts have identical initramfs SHA reported by server but client reports verification mismatch. 02/22: Eng hypothesis: firmware update changed UEFI variable ordering causing dpkg-signed initramfs verification library to use wrong key slot. 02/24: SRE reproduced with custom iPXE build that logs more verbose UEFI variables; observed difference in SecureBoot db ordering on failing hosts. 03/01: Created test image with stripped signature check; those hosts boot successfully (mitigates immediate provisioning). 03/05: Filed PR to add a more tolerant fallback (see related_github_prs); still under review. 03/09: Opened vendor support ticket with BIOS vendor referencing serial numbers and Secure Boot variable dumps. See Slack thread #imaging-pxe-T1245.
Priya Nair (02/18): Initial report and reproduction steps provided. Uploaded logs: tftpd-staging-20260218.tar.gz, ipxe-debug-1.log, dmesg-fail-01.txt.
Ethan Cole (02/20): Confirmed mismatch in client-reported signature vs server manifest. Added kernel debug prints to show UEFI variable snapshots. Linked to PR for permissive fallback.
Nadia Ruiz - SRE (02/24): Reproduced failure on emulated QEMU environment by swapping UEFI variable order; confirms firmware influence. Suggest testing a signed initramfs with alternate key ordering to validate.

Ethan Cole (03/08): Temporary mitigation rolled out - provisioning task sequence now skips signature verification on affected models in staging only. Patch ID: IMAG-2026-033. Need decision for production rollout.
Mitigation: Added a staging-only temporary bypass for initramfs signature enforcement for affected models and BIOS versions to unblock provisioning (IMAG-2026-033). Ongoing: Eng to complete PR for tolerant verification fallback and automated detection of broken SecureBoot variable ordering. Vendor engagement open for firmware fix. Full resolution pending firmware vendor patch or upstream initramfs verifier update. Post-mortem planned after vendor response; follow-up tasks assigned to Imaging and Firmware teams.
03/10: Temporary bypass held in staging; imaging throughput returned to baseline. PR for fallback verification remains under code review. Vendor acknowledged issue and requested additional traces; expected ETA for vendor patch ~4 weeks. Postmortem and rollout plan to be scheduled after vendor fix or upstream change is released.
Finalize PR to implement tolerant verification fallback and add unit tests
Create detection alert for downstream provisioning failures tied to BIOS version and model
Coordinate with vendor for firmware remediation and plan controlled production rollout
Document mitigation steps in Confluence runbook and notify SRE on-call rotations

title: snapshot-alignment-drift-causing-periodic-p99-pulses
body:
snapshot-alignment-drift-causing-periodic-p99-pulses

Issue summary:
Customers (LexiDocs, dedicated) began reporting recurring p99 latency pulses and occasional 504s on text-generation endpoints. The pattern is periodic (roughly every 7-12 minutes) and correlates with increases in request queue depth for short requests. Impact: production user-facing latency spikes and failed responses for interactive flows.

Impact:
- Intermittent p99 spikes from baseline ~220ms to 1.8-2.2s for generation endpoints.
- ~0.3% increase in 504s observed over a 3-hour window for LexiDocs traffic.
- Affects short-sequence use cases (chat/assistant).

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer LexiDocs) in prod us-east.
- Serving runtime v1.42.0 with continuous-batcher enabled and default alignment snapshotting enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Baseline low-latency traffic of small requests (~5-20 tokens) for 5-8 minutes.
2) System enters periodic alignment snapshot cycle tied to batcher metadata (every ~8 minutes).
3) During the snapshot window, multiple short requests queue while a larger snapshot I/O and KV alignment job runs, increasing per-request wait time and generating p99 pulses.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic p99 spikes aligned to snapshot window start times in metrics.
- Traces show requests waiting in the coalescer queue for 600-1800ms before entering a microbatch.
- Snapshot job logs show brief I/O stalls and a GC spike on the batcher worker during the same interval.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot/metadata maintenance should not cause request queuing that elevates tail latency beyond configured SLO. Maintenance should be staggered or performed off the hot path.

Initial logs/metrics references:
- Grafana dashboard: /d/serve/continuous-batcher?orgId=1&view=lexidocs-prod (p95/p99 panels)
- Traces: jaeger/trace/7f8b2e... (examples attached by customer)
- Batch worker logs: /var/log/redwood/serving/batcher-0.log lines 12430-12490 (I/O snapshot start/finish entries)

Temporary workaround offered:
- Switched LexiDocs traffic to a dedicated tenant routing policy with lower snapshot frequency (config override) which reduced the amplitude of pulses by ~60% for the short term.

Next steps requested:
- Engineering investigation to confirm root cause and provide a patch or recommended configuration.
2026-03-10 09:14 - Amina Patel (Support): Customer reported recurring tail latency every ~8 minutes resulting in visible delays for end-users. Provided initial traces and asked to escalate to batcher owners.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Jared Kim (SRE): Acknowledged ticket, started correlating batcher snapshot logs with customer traces. Assigned INT-4021 to track internal investigation for batcher worker GC/IO behavior.
2026-03-11 01:38 - LexiDocs (Customer): Confirmed rollback to previous routing config stabilized UX but wants permanent fix. Attached additional traces where p99 jumps to ~2.1s.
2026-03-12 16:24 - Jared Kim (SRE): Applied conservative config change to reduce snapshot frequency for LexiDocs tenant as a mitigation. Observed reduction in pulse magnitude; still seeing smaller periodic bumps. Captured heap/GC info from batcher process during a pulse and uploaded to shared drive.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Elena Rossi (Eng - batcher): Noted correlation between snapshot alignment windows and an opportunistic metadata compaction job introduced in serving-runtime v1.42.0. Drafting a targeted patch to run compaction asynchronously and add jitter to snapshot start times.
2026-03-13 15:30 - Jared Kim (SRE): Informed customer of planned fix and timeline; scheduled controlled rollout to dedicated fleets early next week. Marked ticket In Progress.
2026-03-13 16:02 - Amina Patel (Support): Customer acknowledged the plan and requested post-deploy monitoring and a follow-up summary.

Hypothesis 1: Snapshot/compaction job is running synchronously on batcher main loop, briefly blocking coalescer flush and increasing queue wait time.
Hypothesis 2: GC activity on batcher worker coincides with snapshot window due to increased allocation during compaction, amplifying pause time.
Evidence collected: Time-aligned logs show snapshot:start and p99 spike within <100ms. Heap profile sampled during pulse shows temporary retention increase and a STW GC mark phase lasting ~200-400ms on the batcher worker.
Experiment: Disabled compaction in a canary fleet; observed p99 pulses disappear in canary (0 instances) and persist in control group. This supports compaction as the main trigger.
Temporary mitigation applied: Reduced snapshot frequency and added tenant-scoped scheduling so LexiDocs snapshots are offset from global windows. Reduced but did not eliminate pulses.
Planned fix: Alter compaction to run off-thread (background worker) and add randomized jitter to snapshot start times per-tenant; add defensive backpressure so metadata maintenance yields to hot request path.
Related artifacts: INT-4021 (internal instrumenting of batcher compaction), PR #2843 implements background compaction and per-tenant jitter, Confluence runbook updated for postmortem.
Risk assessment: Low-risk change if compaction moved off hot path and controlled; however need canary validation on dedicated fleets to ensure no regression in memory stability.
Monitoring additions: Add an alert for 'batcher.snapshot_queue_wait' > 500ms for 5m on dedicated customers and create a dashboard tile showing alignment-phase overlap with p99.

Work in progress - patch authored to decouple compaction from main batcher loop and introduce per-tenant jitter. Patch under review (PR #2843). Plan: canary deploy to two dedicated fleets (including LexiDocs) 2026-03-17, monitor p99 for 48h, then schedule broader rollout if stable. Post-deploy summary and postmortem to be attached to this ticket.
We identified a periodic metadata compaction job in the continuous-batching subsystem that was running on the hot path and causing short bursts of queueing for small requests. We're moving that work off the hot path and adding jitter to snapshot timing; a canary rollout is planned and we'll follow up with results and recommended permanent configuration changes.

title: 429s after enabling token-smoothing policy for mixed low-latency and bulk traffic
body:
429s after enabling token-smoothing policy for mixed low-latency and bulk traffic

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 Throttling responses after we enabled a tenant-scoped token-smoothing (refill-smoothing) policy to reduce spike throttles. The behavior appears only when the customer's traffic mixes low-latency prioritized streams (short sessions, function-calling) with large bulk embedding jobs.

Impact: Customer sees ~2-7% of requests return 429s across both streaming and non-streaming routes; this is causing degraded UX for their real-time features and partial failures for bulk imports. Affects production workload in us-west-2 for Maple Analytics' dedicated pool.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 03:15 UTC: Maple enabled refill-smoothing:window=60s, smoothing-alpha=0.8 via Console (supported config).
- 2026-03-09 03:18–04:00 UTC: Bulk ingest jobs overlap with real-time user sessions.
- 2026-03-09 03:19–03:28 UTC: ~3% of client requests returned 429.
- 2026-03-10 14:05 UTC: Customer opened support ticket reporting sporadic 429s with request-ids.

Environment / config: Dedicated pool. Tenant-level token bucket with per-route burst allowance (route_weighting used to favor low-latency streams). Custom refill smoothing enabled at tenant level. The customer rotates short-lived API keys frequently (every ~5 minutes) for security.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Start a steady stream of prioritized short sessions (chat/function-calls) at ~30rps.
2) Kick off parallel bulk embedding worker at ~20 documents/s.
3) Observe that after ~2–5 minutes some short sessions receive 429s intermittently even though overall consumption is below published tenant sustained quota.

Observed headers from sample failed request (customer provided):
- x-rw-retry-after: 5
- x-rw-tenant-tokens-left: 12
- x-rw-route-burst: 0
- x-rw-request-id: rw-req-0a4f6b3c

Expected behavior: Mixing low-latency and bulk traffic with a smoothing policy should reduce microbursts and avoid cross-route starvation; low-latency routes should receive their route_weighted burst allowance without unexplained 429s.

Actual behavior: Intermittent 429 responses appear even when per-tenant token metrics do not show exhaustion in the long window. The failures correlate with short API-key rotations and periods where many short-lived sessions start in the same 10s window.

Logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- request IDs: rw-req-0a4f6b3c, rw-req-0a4f6b7f, rw-req-0a4f6d22
- session traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/rw-req-0a4f6b3c (customer-shared)
2026-03-10 14:12 UTC - Support (Evelyn): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and triaging to rate-limiter team. Asking for a couple sample request-ids, exact console change (smoothing params), and a short timeline of the key rotations.
2026-03-10 15:02 UTC - Customer (Maple SRE - Arun Patel): Provided three request-ids and confirmed smoothing set to window=60s alpha=0.8 at 2026-03-09 03:15 UTC. Key rotation: ephemeral tokens created by their edge proxy every 5 minutes; authors say they are not seen before enabling smoothing.
2026-03-10 16:40 UTC - Support (Diego): Reproduced similar pattern in a synthetic canary using their mix of traffic and short-lived keys. Initial hypothesis: per-key orphaned token buckets + smoothing-induced refill delay can create temporary route-level depletion when many new keys are created simultaneously.
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - SRE (Marina): Dug into rate-limiter logs. Found token-bucket allocation events showing per-key buckets created with zero initial burst when keys are short-lived and smoothing is active. Logged sample: rate-limiter/alloc key=ephemeral-20260309-xx burst=0 smoothing-delay=45ms
2026-03-11 12:00 UTC - Support (Diego): Shared interim mitigation: advise customer to enable per-route reserved-burst cushion (route_burst: +50) or increase smoothing window to 120s while we validate patch. Customer asked for risks; we noted temporary cost increase for burst cushion.
Queried rate-limiter events in us-west-2 for tenant maple-123 between 2026-03-09 03:00 and 03:30 UTC. Observed per-key bucket creation spikes coincident with key rotation TTL renewal window.
Confirmed smoothing algorithm reduces refill quantum for newly created buckets; combined with zero-initial-burst config for ephemeral keys this yields brief route_burst exhaustion even though tenant-level tokens remain available.
Ran canary reproducer (script attached to internal issue): start 30 short sessions + bulk workers. Canary showed ~2.8% 429 rate after smoothing enabled; disabled smoothing removed 429s in same pattern.
Checked scheduler logs for autoscale; no GPU shortage or serving-runtime errors correlated with times of 429s. 5xxs were not present.
Short-term options provided to customer: 1) Set per-route reserved burst (route_burst) for the low-latency route to +50 tokens; 2) Increase smoothing window to 120s (reduces abrupt per-key creation effect); 3) Delay ephemeral key rotation jitter to spread bucket creation over time. All are live-config changes via Console.
SRE to prepare PR that initializes ephemeral key buckets with a minimal initial-burst when smoothing is enabled (infra PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1543).
Product/Rate-Limiter team to review smoothing math for interaction with zero-initial-burst keys and add automated detection to Console to warn when tenant smoothing + frequent key churn is configured.
If customer opts in, run controlled rollout of initial-burst patch in their dedicated pool canary for 24h and monitor x-rw-429-rate and tenant-token-metrics.
Follow up with customer by 2026-03-13 with canary results and recommended permanent config or patch rollout schedule.

title: Intermittent connection reset / early termination during prolonged generation with deep chat history
body:
Intermittent connection reset / early termination during prolonged generation with deep chat history

Issue summary:
Customer observes occasional connection resets and early completion when requesting long-form generation against a stream-enabled endpoint. The requests include ~100k token-like priming history (many short turns) plus ask for an additional large generated output (max_tokens ~ 65k).

Impact:
- Customer production flow intermittently receives an HTTP/502 or TCP connection reset mid-stream and client reports incomplete generation.
- Occurs for ~5-15% of long-history requests during peak hours, causing failed user flows.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) assigned to Peregrine Labs, region us-west-2.
- Model: redwood-open-7b-v2, runtime config uses streaming=true, batching=enabled, kv_cache=enabled, quantization=8-bit.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Recreate session with 300+ turns of short exchanges (~tokenized length ~95k).
2) Send stream completion request with max_tokens set to 65000 and temperature=0.7.
3) Observe streaming chunks for ~20-40s, then connection abruptly resets or server returns 502 with no final chunk.

Expected behavior:
- Stream should return incremental chunks until completion or a graceful timeout with error including reason.

Actual behavior:
- Abrupt connection reset or 502/504 with no clear server-side error in the immediate HTTP logs. Customer-side logs show socket closed by remote. Some attempts return partial output; some appear to stall and then cut.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided client-side pcap excerpt and request/response headers (attached to ticket).
- Example request id from customer: req-pleg-20260310-8492

Logs & quick traces (support captured):
- API gateway shows TCP FIN for the connection around 26-45s into the request. No 5xx body payload returned.
- Serving runtime trace (partial) for the same window shows last seen server-side logs: "stream_chunk_sent seq=124" then no further successful send entries before worker reports "stream flush error: write: connection reset by peer".
- No explicit OOM in the instance metrics; GPU memory remained within expected bounds.

Immediate customer impact: partial/failed responses for long-history, high-cost requests.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Devon Chen): Initial triage — checked node health and autoscaler events around timestamps. No cluster-wide preemptions recorded but saw transient high send-queue wait on a few worker pods at 2026-03-10T14:22:xxZ. Creating trace to correlate with runtime logs.
2026-03-11 - Runtime Eng (Priya Rao): Hypothesis — long prefix + large max_tokens increases KV cache churn and causes larger-than-expected flush sizes; if a streaming TCP write blocks then upstream may reset. Asking for sample request bodies and exact retry headers to reproduce locally. Assigned to dedicated runtime team for replication.
2026-03-11 - Customer (Peregrine Labs - ops@peregrine.example): We attached replay file and we can open a maintenance window next Wednesday. Blocking user-facing feature until resolved.
2026-03-12 - Support (Ava Martinez): Added temporary mitigation suggestion: reduce max_tokens to <= 16k or disable streaming for those specific long-history flows. Customer confirmed temporary fallback works but not acceptable long-term.
2026-03-12 - Eng (Devon Chen): Running isolated repro using customer's replay — managed to reproduce socket reset when batching and streaming enabled with very large response budgets. Captured runtime logs and increased socket-level send buffer to test; observed fewer resets but not eliminated.
Reproduction: Using customer replay on a dedicated test pool reproduced early TCP resets when streaming + batching + kv_cache active and requested max_tokens >= 60k.
Observation: When KV cache grows beyond threshold, worker performs more frequent KV serialization and small synchronous disk writes which coincide with spikes in send latency for the streaming socket.
Hypothesis A: Head-of-line blocking on the streaming TCP socket combined with synchronous KV writes causes upstream timeouts or remote resets from the API gateway when latency exceeds connection timeouts. Gateway did not log a 504 but closed socket after inactivity window.
Hypothesis B: Batching scheduler occasionally groups a very large request with other long-history requests causing worker thread exhaustion; subsequent flushing attempts collide with kernel-level TCP backpressure and the gateway or client closes.
Metrics: send_queue_latency 95th escalated from 120ms to 1.3s during repro. Worker CPU and disk IO show short spikes at the moment of reset.
Temporary test mitigation: increasing streaming socket send buffer by 2x reduced occurrence in lab but is not acceptable as a long-term fix. Disabling batching for these requests prevented the issue in repro.
Related findings: Similar patterns referenced in SUP-29541 and SUP-60735 (linking established above).
Workaround provided to customer: (1) set max_tokens <= 16k or (2) disable streaming for deep-history flows or (3) pin model config to disable batching for affected route. Customer accepted workaround for now.

Long-term plan (next steps):
- Runtime team to implement non-blocking KV serialization path and move heavy IO operations off the main send thread (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4189 created).
- Scheduler update to detect very large-response budget requests and route them to isolated worker slots without batching.
- Add monitoring alert for send_queue_latency and KV-serialize spikes for Dedicated pools.

Status: In Progress. Tracking in internal epic INT-13402 for runtime change and INT-13403 for scheduler change. Expected release in 2 sprints subject to QA.

title: Intermittent DNS failures: stale UDP responses due to misrouted source routes on TGW
body:
Intermittent DNS failures: stale UDP responses due to misrouted source routes on TGW

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent DNS resolution failures from model-serving nodes in their Private deployment. Failures are transient and correlate with increased traffic spikes. Impact: model pulls and control-plane name lookups intermittently time out causing model download retries and elevated latency for inference (observed 95th percentile token latency spikes).
1) In customer VPC (Finlytics prod), run repeated DNS lookups for control-plane hostnames and S3 presigned hostnames from a serving node behind the TGW-attached subnet.
2) Simulate load with concurrent model-downloads or many concurrent inference requests to raise egress rate.
3) Observe intermittent NXDOMAIN/timeout or stale A answers for a subset of queries; behavior disappears when traffic volume drops.
- Intermittent DNS timeouts and stale UDP responses for ~0.5-2% of queries during traffic surges.
- Serving nodes retry over TCP/HTTPS and eventually succeed, causing client-visible latency spikes and extra egress.
- Customer sees increased model-download retry rates and occasional gRPC stream resets tied to DNS failures.
All DNS queries to control-plane and artifact endpoints should resolve reliably; UDP responses should be routed back to the original requesting ENI and not be dropped or mismatched.
Excerpts from tcpdump on serving node (src/udp dst mismatch):
- 10:12:23.456 IP 10.50.12.34.33333 > 172.31.8.10.53: 1234+ A? cp1.redwood.internal. (45)
- 10:12:23.457 IP 172.31.8.10.53 > 10.50.12.34.33333: 1234 1/0/0 A 54.239.26.90 (61)
- 10:12:23.457 IP 172.31.8.10.53 > 10.50.12.99.33333: 1234 1/0/0 A 54.239.26.90 (61)  <-- response delivered to different source port/ENI
Customer router logs show asymmetry: reply path traversed a different attachment and hit a NAT gateway with source NAT enabled, changing source IP and hitting customer's DNS cache which rejected the unsolicited response.
- Initial hypothesis: upstream DNS server (forwarder) sending responses that do not match original source tuple due to ECMP or TGW route table asymmetry.
- Pulled TGW route tables and attachment propagation logs: found a stale route originating from a prior maintenance change that created a longer, preferred path for the return traffic for the subnet range used by serving nodes.
- NAT devices observed performing source NAT for replies when they egressed via a different path; customer's DNS forwarder discards responses if the 5-tuple doesn't match an outstanding query.
- Packet captures show consistent pattern: DNS request leaves via ENI-A, response returns via ENI-B because TGW route propagation selected a different Transit Gateway attachment for that return prefix.
- Correlation with traffic spikes: when flow hashing changed (due to increased concurrent flows) packets were more likely to take alternate attachments and hit the stale propagated route.
Short-term workaround: customer removed source NAT on the affected NAT gateway and temporarily pinned route propagation to the intended attachment for the serving subnets. This reduced failed responses to near-zero while we prepared a permanent fix.
Operational workaround: disable aggressive ECMP on the TGW attachment or apply flow-affinity rules on the customer's edge to preserve symmetric routing.
Engineering (network team) prepared two changes: 1) Clean stale propagated route entries in the customer's TGW route table (completed 2026-03-14 09:20 UTC). 2) Added validation in the control plane to detect mismatched 5-tuples for UDP responses and trigger an alert when prevalence exceeds threshold.
Status: route cleanup rolled out and customer confirms reduction in DNS failures. Follow-up PR merged to add detection telemetry (PR #6287).
If issue recurs before full remediation: 1) Temporarily disable SNAT on NAT gateway for serving subnet egress to preserve original source IP. 2) Pin TGW route propagation for the affected prefix to the primary attachment. 3) Throttle connection churn on serving nodes to avoid flow-hash rebalancing during maintenance windows.
- Platform: add TGW route-propagation audit in daily infra health check.
- SRE: add dashboard showing mismatched DNS 5-tuple rate and alert at 0.1% baseline.
- CS: notify Finlytics when next maintenance window scheduled and validate after.
- Docs: update Private Deploy runbook with symmetric-routing checklist.

title: Intermittent power blips on Floor 3 causing devices to reset
body:
Intermittent power blips on Floor 3 causing devices to reset

Multiple employees on Floor 3 reported brief power blips between 09:30-11:00 local time over the past three weekdays. Symptoms: monitors briefly go black and reboot, USB hubs drop devices, some VoIP phones restart. No server-side outages observed. Blips correlate with use of kitchen appliances (coffee grinder, blender) but correlation is noisy. Impact is localized to non-critical desk equipment but is causing meeting interruptions and lost work. Steps attempted: swap power strips, moved a few affected desks to different PDUs, tested with dedicated UPS at one desk (no blips while on UPS). Building facilities team dispatched on 2026-02-15 and did a basic panel inspection; they reported no obvious loose breaker but noted voltage dips on monitoring probe during a simulated blender run. Next steps: schedule electrician to check floor-level breaker and isolation; provision temporary UPS units for high-priority desks and conference rooms; collect longer-term voltage logs for 24–48h.
