title: Ingress header clipping truncates Authorization bearer token for private deployment, causing 401 errors
body:
Ingress header clipping truncates Authorization bearer token for private deployment, causing 401 errors

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 401s from the Redwood private API for requests proxied through their on-prem ingress. Impact: Customer's production integration cannot complete inference calls; errors began after a recent rollout that added a long service-account assertion header. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane), prod, us-east-1. Observed behavior: Requests that include a long Authorization header (service-to-service bearer token which includes a long nested JWT) receive 401 Unauthorized from the identity-proxy. The token appears truncated in the proxy logs. Expected behavior: Identity proxy should forward the full Authorization header to the auth service and validate the token, returning 200 for valid tokens. Workaround: Short-term workaround was to reduce the size of the assertion header (customer-side) and use token introspection endpoint for smaller tokens.
1) Configure private deployment with customer ingress (NGINX/HAProxy) that proxies requests to Redwood identity-proxy. 2) Attach an Authorization header containing a long bearer token (>8192 bytes) produced by the customer's token service (includes nested claims). 3) Send standard generate/chat request to Redwood API route. 4) Observe 401 response and identity-proxy logs showing 'Authorization header truncated' or token decode error.
identity-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:10Z] ERROR token_validation.go:86 invalid token: token parsing failed: unexpected EOF
nginx[2026-03-10T14:22:09Z] upstream sent invalid response while reading response header from upstream
-- captured truncated header (authorization): 'Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Ij...' (length reported: 4096)
-- original token length reported by customer: 12048 bytes
2026-03-10 | Support (Maya): Opened ticket after initial CS report. Requested full proxy config, ingress type, and sample failing request headers. Asked for test token and timestamp of failures.
2026-03-10 | Customer (Aurelia Eng, Jordan): Provided nginx.conf snippet and sample token. Noted failures started after their auth pump that appended long trace metadata to assertions.
2026-03-10 | SRE (Daniel): Reproduced locally using customer's token shape. Observed header truncated by nginx default buffer size. Added hypothesis: ingress is dropping/truncating headers exceeding buffer limits, leading to corrupted tokens reaching identity-proxy.
2026-03-11 | Eng (SRE): Validated that identity-proxy can accept large headers (no hardcoded limit), upstream proxies are the culprit. Opened PR to docs and runbook recommending ingress config and updated onboarding checklist for private customers.
2026-03-12 | Support (Maya): Confirmed with customer that after adjusting nginx proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size per recommended values and removing appended metadata, requests are succeeding. Customer validated end-to-end traffic in prod with no 401s for >24h.
Checked identity-proxy codepath: no arbitrary header length cap found; decoding libraries return EOF when token truncated.
Reproduced with a local nginx using default large_client_header_buffers (8k per buffer). Token >8k leads to truncation in proxy_pass path.
SRE test: increased nginx large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size to 32k, and upstream requests succeed.
Observed error pattern distinct from JWKS rotation or SAML issues: token was malformed due to truncation rather than signature mismatch.
Customer ingress earlier had a vendor default that strips header segments after a specific byte length; vendor docs confirmed this behavior for legacy builds.
Related internal ticket INT-4321 created to add an ingress checklist item and automated verification for private customer deploys to detect unsafe header truncation defaults.
Root cause: Customer's ingress (NGINX with vendor defaults) was configured with insufficient header buffer sizes which resulted in Authorization header truncation for very large bearer tokens. Remediation: 1) Provided documented recommended ingress settings (large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size >= token size). 2) Customer removed non-essential metadata appended to tokens and switched to compressed token format for long assertions. 3) Added runbook entry to private-deployment onboarding: verify ingress header buffer limits and run a synthetic request with oversized token. 4) Internal follow-up INT-4321 to add an automated check in deployment scripts.
Explained issue root cause (ingress header buffer limits) and provided step-by-step mitigation. Customer implemented recommended nginx config changes and validated success. Customer accepted the fix and requested the updated docs be added to their onboarding checklist.

title: Intermittent 403: 'sub' claim collision after Azure AD B2B token-exchange maps session to wrong tenant causing RBAC failures
body:
Intermittent 403: 'sub' claim collision after Azure AD B2B token-exchange maps session to wrong tenant causing RBAC failures

Customer on a private deployment (HelioHealth) reports intermittent 403s for admin-console and API routes after enabling Azure AD B2B guest invitations. Issue appears after a user accepts B2B invite and signs in; sometimes their session is created but RBAC lookups return no role bindings, resulting in 403 Authorization failures. Customer sees this across multiple users and tenants, not correlated to a specific model or route.
Several HelioHealth admins cannot access the Redwood Console or call admin APIs intermittently. Affects production users in us-east-1; customer reports degraded ops and blocked workflows for compliance-sensitive tasks.
1) HelioHealth invites external user via Azure AD B2B (guest); 2) User accepts invite and completes sign-in against HelioHealth tenant; 3) Fronting identity-proxy performs token-exchange to issue Redwood session token; 4) User attempts to access /console (admin) or call admin API; 5) Observe 403 returned intermittently with 'role binding not found' in logs.
Identity-proxy request trace: request_id=ip-ctx-0d9f3a, incoming id_token claims: {"sub": "user:oid:1111", "email": "guest.user@example.com", "tid": "a1b2c3"}. After token-exchange we emit session cookie (session_id=sess-7f2b). RBAC lookup using cache key 'sub:user:1111' returned empty. Later a subsequent login for the same user produced id_token with sub 'guest.user@example.com' (email-as-sub) and RBAC lookup succeeded. See snippet: [identity-proxy.log: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] "session-lookup key=sub:user:1111 -> MISS"; [rbac.log] "binds for tenant a1b2c3 not found for key sub:user:1111".
- Reproduced with HelioHealth testing account; observed two different 'sub' formats emitted by Azure AD in B2B flows depending on token audience and whether token came from token-exchange vs initial id_token.
- Our session-store keys sessions by raw 'sub' claim. RBAC resolution pipeline later normalizes principal to email and looks up role bindings by email; mismatch causes empty binding results.
- Cache layer (memcached) contains stale entry for some 'sub' variants leading to repeated failures until TTL expires.
- Hypothesis: Azure AD B2B sometimes returns pairwise subject (opaque oid) vs emails-as-sub depending on token version / conditional access or token-exchange parameters. Our code assumes 'sub' is stable across exchanges.
- Also saw one request path where identity-proxy performed a token-exchange with &client_id=legacy-client which returned different sub format.
1) Asked customer to reconfigure Azure AD token issuance to include stable 'email' claim as part of id_token and to prefer 'oid' consistently; 2) Temporary workaround: restart identity-proxy to clear memcached entries for HelioHealth tenant (restarted staging proxy and observed reduction in repro rate). 3) Added request-level fallback in session-lookup to attempt email-based RBAC lookup when 'sub' lookup misses (hotfix branch applied to canary).
Priya Nair (Support): Collected sample tokens and requested logs from customer; escalated to ENG because this is an interoperability issue with Azure AD B2B.
Miguel Santos (SRE): Reproduced locally against customer's test tenant. Confirmed memcached entries for mixed sub formats. Working on a safe fallback in identity-proxy to attempt normalized lookups.
HelioHealth SRE (customer): We observed this for 4 of 12 invited guest users. Guest accounts sometimes work on retry. Happy to provide tenant logs and an invite pair for repro.
Jordan Blake (Eng): Rolling a canary hotfix that attempts email fallback and also logs both raw_sub and normalized_principal for future debugging.
Miguel Santos (SRE): Canary deployed hotfix to two gateways in us-east-1 at 2026-03-11T18:40Z. Initial telemetry shows 80% drop in 403s for affected users.
Deployed identity-proxy hotfix (v1.9.3-canary -> v1.9.3) that: 1) normalizes principal resolution to prefer email claim if present, 2) falls back to alternate sub formats when RBAC lookup misses, and 3) emits detailed logging for sub/email/oid for future debugging. Cleared memcached keys for HelioHealth tenant and coordinated with customer to request consistent token format from Azure AD.
Hotfix rolled to canary 2026-03-11 18:40Z (2 gateways), verified reduced error rate. Full rollout to all us-east-1 gateways completed 2026-03-12 03:15Z. Added migration script to sweep session-store for mixed-format entries and normalize principal index.
Engineering to add robust principal canonicalization in identity-proxy (ENG-5042).
Product to update Private deployment KB with Azure AD B2B recommendations (KB-Priv-AD-B2B).
Customer success to confirm HelioHealth reconfigures token issuance and reports back in 2 weeks.

title: High 5xx/504 error rate on embeddings bulk upload following client retry amplification
body:
High 5xx/504 error rate on embeddings bulk upload following client retry amplification

Issue summary:
Customer reported elevated 5xx (predominantly 504) responses during a large embeddings bulk upload. Error rate started at ~14:22 UTC and persisted for ~45 minutes, coincident with a spike in retry traffic from the customer's client. Impact: multiple embedding jobs failed, delays for downstream inference consumers, and increased costs due to amplification.

Impact:
- ~40% of the customer's requests returned 504 during the window.
- Other tenants on the same Dedicated pool saw latency bumps but lower error rates.
- Business impact: delayed ML pipeline runs for Noteable Analytics (non-prod downstream jobs also affected).

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (shared GPU pool)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Customer: Noteable Analytics (dedicated tier)
- Affected models: text-embedding-3-small (primary), fallback embedding-1b-quant

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Customer ran a bulk embeddings upload: 24k texts in 200-file parallel multipart batches with client concurrency=200.
2. Several individual batch requests hit 30s client timeout and retried immediately with exponential backoff but effectively very tight (no jitter).
3. Retries amplified request rate to the API gateway and upstream runtime; queues filled and connections entered TIME_WAIT.
4. Serving runtime threadpool reached saturation and started returning 504s as requests timed out waiting for worker availability.

Relevant logs / metrics / traces:
- APIGW 5xx rate graph: spike at 14:22 UTC from 1.2% -> 38% for the customer's route (link: https://dash.redwood.ai/apigw/graph?range=1h&panel=5xx).
- Runtime busy workers: worker_util peaked at 98%, queue_latency increased from 12ms -> 620ms.
- Kernel socket backlog (netstat): SYN_RECV queue grew; ephemeral port exhaustion warnings in edge proxies.
- Runtime logs: repeated "worker threadpool exhausted" entries and "dispatch timeout - returning 504".
- Customer-provided client logs show repeated immediate retries (no jitter) after 30s timeouts.

Initial hypothesis:
- Client-side retry amplification combined with heavy multipart batching overwhelmed the gateway and upstream runtime.
- Runtime inability to shed load quickly caused queue growth and timeouts rather than graceful backpressure.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support requested that the customer back off concurrency to <= 16 and enable jitter on client retries (applied at 14:37 UTC).
- We applied a quick ingress rate cap for the customer's tenant on the API gateway (soft cap) at 14:40 UTC to reduce immediate pressure.
- Restarted two runtime workers on the affected Dedicated pool to clear threadpool leaks (rolling restarts 14:45–14:50 UTC).

Current state: partial stabilization as of 15:05 UTC. Error rate dropped to ~3% for the customer's route; background tail latency remains elevated while caches warm and connection pools recover.

Proposing rolling restart of two affected runtime pods and temporary per-tenant soft rate limit. Workaround implemented: advised customer to reduce concurrency to <= 16 and enable exponential backoff with jitter; implemented soft per-tenant cap and rolled two runtime workers to clear threadpool state.
Fix plan (short term): Adjust default per-tenant ingress soft limits for Dedicated customers who run large bulk jobs; add client best-practice guidance to Support KB. Assigned INT-4412 to infra to evaluate ingress default caps.
Fix plan (medium term): Improve runtime load-shedding behavior so requests are rejected earlier (503) rather than queued to timeout; add metrics to detect retry amplification patterns and trigger automated throttles. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2794.
Follow-ups: 1) Call scheduled with Noteable Analytics on 2026-03-12 to review recommended client configuration and discuss Dedicated pool sizing. 2) Post-incident postmortem to be written in Confluence and linked here.

title: Office inventory + keycard audit + disposal request (storage shelves + access system cleanup)
body:
Office inventory + keycard audit + disposal request (storage shelves + access system cleanup)

Request type: Internal support / facilities + security coordination

Background
Office moved desks last quarter; storage now contains untagged peripherals, old keycards, and leftover badge holders. This ticket consolidates the remaining cleanup work so we can reconcile inventory, tidy shared spaces, and reduce risk from stray credentials.

Scope / Goals
- Produce a concise inventory of unassigned equipment (monitors, keyboards, spare GPU boxes, dongles)
- Audit and deactivate lost/old keycards in the access system and return/re-enroll active ones
- Clean and label community storage shelves and identify disposal candidates for Facilities pickup

Updates vs earlier plan
- Security requested we export access logs for the last 12 months (not 18) for the initial cross-check; they will expand the window only if anomalies are found.
- Anything that could contain data-bearing media (NVMe/SSDs/USBs) must be separated into a "Security review" bin and cannot go directly to e-waste.
- Facilities asked that disposal candidates be grouped into: e-waste, donation, recycle, landfill, and "needs approval".

Acceptance criteria
- CSV inventory uploaded to Drive with columns: item_id, type, location, status, owner_hint, notes
- Keycards deactivated or reassigned; list of card IDs with current status documented (include reason: lost, terminated, replaced, active)
- Disposal list handed to Facilities with approval note and the category breakdown

Planned steps
1) Quick sweep team (1-2 eng volunteers + Facilities) to inventory storage (target: 1 day on-site)
2) Collate CSV + apply physical tags/labels to boxes/shelves (target: 0.5-1 day)
3) Keycard audit with Security (Omar to coordinate) (target: 1-2 days, mostly admin work)
4) Disposal / reallocation decisions + update asset tracker (target: 0.5-1 day)

Notes / investigation log (messy)
- Found box labeled "quantization-experiments-2019" that may contain an older NVMe; moved to Security review bin (do not e-waste yet).
- Some badge IDs show up in access logs in 2024 despite being physically in lost-and-found; need cross-check against HR termination list and replacement cards.
- Facilities prefers completion before holiday break; if we slip, we should at minimum complete the keycard deprovisioning and isolate data-bearing media.

Links / artifacts

title: Burst of 5xx errors after global config sweep — runtime restart loops and API failures
body:
Burst of 5xx errors after global config sweep — runtime restart loops and API failures

Issue summary:
Customers observed a sudden burst of 5xx responses (502/503) across multiple NovaDocs tenants in us-east following a global configuration sweep at ~2026-03-10T09:45Z. The API gateway returned upstream 502/503; behind the gateway several serving-runtime pods entered a fast restart loop and produced OOM/gpu-mmap errors in kube logs.

Impact:
- ~12% increased 5xx rate for NovaDocs over a 25-minute window, causing degraded user-facing document generation.
- Short-lived elevated latency for all streaming sessions; some streaming sessions terminated with connection reset.
- Customer workspace on dedicated capacity experienced reduced throughput until mitigation applied.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: gke-us-east-prod-3
- Region: us-east-1
- Customer tier: enterprise (dedicated pool pinned to redwood-v1-medium)

Steps to reproduce / timeline:
1) 2026-03-10T09:44Z: config-service roll-out initiated — global batch/concurrency policy change (increase max_concurrent_infers from 8 to 16, change prefetch target ratio).
2) 2026-03-10T09:45Z: config sweep completed and new policy applied to target tenants including NovaDocs.
3) 2026-03-10T09:46Z: first 502s observed by API gateway health monitors for NovaDocs route.
4) 2026-03-10T09:50–10:10Z: multiple serving-runtime pods for the dedicated pool OOM/killed and restarted; kubelet logs show repeated gpu memory fragmentation warnings and device mmap failure.
5) 2026-03-10T10:02Z: Support contacted; mitigation (rollback policy -> previous batch/concurrency) started at 10:08Z.
6) 2026-03-10T10:20Z: 5xx rate returned near baseline; pods stabilized by 10:35Z.

Recent config changes associated:
- max_concurrent_infers: 8 -> 16
- batch_latency_target_ms: 10 -> 50
- aggressive prefetch enabled for pinned models

Logs / evidence (key excerpts):
- api-gateway: upstream_err="502" upstream_addr="10.24.5.12:8080" request_id=rn-3e1c
- kubelet pod/runtime: "OOMKilled" status, dmesg: "nvmap: mmap failed - mmap_device_io failed"
- runtime stderr: "KVCache::realloc failed, fragmentation detected, attempted fallback kernel; watchog_reset()"
- monitoring: GPU mem util sudden drop to 20% followed by repeated allocation spikes and then GPU driver ENOMEM events.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated the timing of the global config sweep with the start of error surge; all impacted runtime pods received updated batching/concurrency flags via config-service.
- Hypothesis: increasing concurrency and batch_latency_target allowed more inflight requests to accumulate on dedicated GPUs that already had fragmented KV cache state, triggering fallback kernel paths that are sensitive to contiguous device memory. That led to allocation failures, watchdog resets, and pod restarts.
- Autoscaler did not add nodes quickly because pods were restarting before new capacity could be scheduled; backpressure amplified at api-gateway leading to 502s.
- Not a network/TLS issue — connection logs show normal handshake; failures are from upstream process exit.

Mitigation applied:
- Rolled back config sweep for affected tenant group at 2026-03-10T10:08Z (reverted max_concurrent_infers and prefetched disabled).
- Temporarily increased pod restart backoff and hysteresis to avoid thundering restarts while kube drains were happening.
- Throttled incoming rate at API gateway for NovaDocs for 20 minutes via route weight reduction to give serving-runtime time to recover.

Resolution / current status:
- After rollback and gateway throttling, runtime pods stopped restarting and 5xx returned to baseline by 2026-03-10T10:35Z.
- Customer reports partial service degradation resolved; no data loss.

Follow-up actions / owners:
- Engineering (runtime team) to add safety cap in config-service that prevents doubling concurrency for pinned/dedicated pools without preflight simulation (Owner: @Luca Martinez; due 2026-03-17).
- Runtime team to add diagnostics to detect KVCache fragmentation and trigger a graceful fallback before kernel swap (Owner: @Priya Shah; due 2026-03-24).
- SRE to add a short delay/rolling-apply strategy for config sweeps that affect pinned dedicated pools (Owner: @Noah Kim; due 2026-03-14).
- Support to contact NovaDocs CSM and schedule a post-incident review (Owner: @Asha Rao; due 2026-03-12).

Notes:
- Linked to prior incidents involving model prefetch amplification (see SUP-51234) and rollout-induced 5xx waves (see SUP-214890).
- No billing or invoice impact recorded.

2026-03-10 11:10 - Luca Martinez (Runtime): Reproduced locally with a smoke harness that mimics high fragmentation states. Kernel fallback path triggers OOM on contiguous allocation. Doubling concurrency is risky on pinned pools. Investigating safe cap.
2026-03-10 11:26 - NovaDocs-ops (Customer): We saw many 502s for ~20 minutes. Rollback helped — thanks for the quick response. Would like a postmortem and steps to avoid this in future.
2026-03-10 12:05 - Noah Kim (SRE): Applied temporary gateway rate reduction at 10:10Z; this breathing room appears to have stopped restarts. Planning to change rollout strategy for config-service.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Priya Shah (Runtime): Adding KVCache fragmentation counters and a heuristic to refuse kernel swap if fragmentation threshold exceeded. Draft PR available for review.

title: Request: per-role field allowlist forwarder with HSM-backed redaction and signed delivery receipts for audit evidence
body:
Request: per-role field allowlist forwarder with HSM-backed redaction and signed delivery receipts for audit evidence

Issue summary: NovaBank requests a near-real-time audit forwarder that enforces per-role field allowlisting, performs on-the-fly PII redaction using HSM-backed salts, and delivers cryptographically signed per-batch receipts for compliance evidence. They need a samplable evidence bundle and short answers to a security questionnaire covering key management and redaction proofs. Impact: This is a compliance blocker for a major production integration; customer cannot certify log delivery without per-event allowlist enforcement and signed receipts. Environment: Production tenant in us-east, delivering to customer's Graylog cluster over TLS. Desired delivery is RFC5425-style TLS syslog over mTLS or HTTPS POST to a secure endpoint with resume tokens and sequence manifests.
1) Customer configured a generic syslog bridge in Console -> Audit exports with destination = graylog-prod.novabank.example:6514 (TLS).
Excerpt from customer ingestion failure: 
2026-03-04T18:03:11Z ERROR forwarder: missing-field=customer_email tenant=novabank-123 endpoint=graylog-prod.novabank.example:6514 seq=00000045
2026-03-04T18:04:02Z INFO forwarder: batch-sent seq=00000046 manifest=hmac:abcd...
Customer observed events arriving at destination with PII fields still present and some events dropped due to 'field-mismatch' errors. They also require per-role allowlist that strips all non-allowed fields before export; current console-level redaction is insufficient because it operates post-export in their SIEM ingestion. They asked for proof-of-delivery receipts that contain batch check-hash and HSM-attested signature, plus a resume token for ordered replay.
2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel (Reporter): Opening ticket — attaching customer questionnaire and sample log extract in Confluence link. Slack: #support-novabank thread started.
2026-03-05 - Support (Marco Chen): Acknowledged. Assigned to Marco for initial triage. Opening internal investigation and pinging infra on mTLS tunnel feasibility. Linked INT-4021 for infra work.
2026-03-06 - SRE (Leah Gomez): Investigated forwarder logs for tenant novabank-123. Found repeated 'field-mismatch' rejections originating from the exporter schema enforcement layer (exporter v1.9). Sketched hypothesis: exporter applies allowlist only at destination mapping, not at per-role evaluation. Logged findings to internal runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Export+Schema+Enforcement.
2026-03-06 - Eng (Dom Singh): Confirmed exporter binary lacks hooks for HSM salts per-tenant. We can implement per-tenant salt retrieval via KMS/HSM API and compute redact-to-hash prior to payload serialization. Estimated patch: 3 sprints for full prod hardened release; can provide a short-term patched canary for NovaBank in 5 business days.
2026-03-06 - Support (Marco Chen): Proposed interim workaround: enable console-level 'pre-export transformation' to drop all fields except the minimal allowlist NovaBank provided and send that to their Graylog. This removes PII but does not provide HSM-signed receipts. Customer accepted interim but requested signed manifests as evidence before go-live.
2026-03-07 - Security (Riley Huang): We can create per-batch manifests signed by platform HSM using an ED25519 key with attestation. Will need IAM authorization from NovaBank to reference their tenant-scoped key alias if they want customer-owned keys. Documented approach and questions in Confluence QA page.
2026-03-07 - Customer (NovaBank Security Contact - Elena Morozova): Prefers Redwood signs manifests using our HSM and includes the X.509 attestation. Also requested a short answers doc for the vendor security questionnaire about key rotation, KMS separation, and replay protection. Open to canary as long as we provide 24/7 point-of-contact during test window.
Hypotheses: (1) Exporter enforces schema-level allowlist at mapping time, not as per-role runtime policy. (2) Redaction to irreversible hash requires tenant-specific salt stored in KMS/HSM; exporter currently uses a global salt. Findings: found exporter v1.9 config lacks 'role-policy' hooks; observed 'missing-field' errors match a recent schema push for redaction rules. Referenced logs and PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-exporter/pull/482. Next steps: patch exporter to evaluate allowlists at request-time, integrate KMS/HSM per-tenant salt retrieval, and add manifest generation endpoint signed by HSM.
Workaround: Enabled console pre-export transform to drop customer-requested non-allowlisted fields (applied 2026-03-06 21:00 UTC). This neutralizes PII exposure for now. Medium-term fix: engineering will ship a canary build with per-role allowlist evaluation and HSM manifest signing to NovaBank by 2026-03-12. Permanent rollout planned across prod with a canary followed by a 2-week observation window. Deliverables: (1) evidence bundle (sample redacted events, per-batch signed manifests, resume tokens) exported to S3 and shared with NovaBank; (2) security questionnaire answers (attached in Confluence page). Follow-up: open INT ticket for automated audit-forwarder smoke tests (INT-4075).
Schedule: Canary to NovaBank on 2026-03-12; production rollout 2026-03-26 pending canary success. Owner: Dom Singh (Eng). QA: SRE and Security to validate attestations and replay protections. Customer comms: Support to send a formal timeline and sample evidence bundle link by 2026-03-09.
2026-03-07 - Interim transform enabled. Customer confirmed no PII seen in sample exports after transform. Engineering scoping complete; PR drafted for exporter hooks and HSM integration. Will provide signed-manifest prototype and an evidence pack to NovaBank for audit review.
Create canary environment and deploy patched exporter (owner: Dom Singh)
Produce signed-manifest prototype and deliver evidence bundle to NovaBank (owner: Riley Huang)
Update Console UI to surface per-role allowlist controls (owner: UX Team)
Close ticket after customer acceptance and evidence confirmation

title: Schema-handoff parse backpressure causing long-tail completion and request timeouts in JSON mode
body:
Schema-handoff parse backpressure causing long-tail completion and request timeouts in JSON mode

Issue summary: Customer observes intermittent long-tail completion latency and client timeouts when using JSON/structured-output mode with a large schema. Impact: Several production requests (5-10% of sessions during peak) exceed 10s final-chunk latency and cause downstream service timeouts. Environment: dedicated cluster serving Noteable Analytics in us-east-1, pinned to redwood-open-13B model variant with streaming JSON output and schema validation enabled.

Observed behaviour: Most requests complete within SLO (<=500ms tail), but a non-trivial tail of requests stalls at finalization step for 2-20s before the final token is emitted. Clients receive partial streaming chunks then a long silence, then either a final chunk or a connection timeout (504). This happens only when strict schema validation is enabled and the schema includes many optional nested fields (schema size ~120KB).
1) Customer sample code: create streaming completion with json_schema set to large schema (~120KB) and schema_validation: strict; 2) Send varied prompts that cause deeply nested objects and optional lists to be emitted; 3) Observe streaming trace for final-chunk gap and client-side timeout around 8-12s on a subset of requests; 4) Repeat under load (50-100rps) to reproduce long-tail spikes.
Selected server logs (truncated):
- 2026-03-10T14:22:53Z [serving-runtime] request-id=... token_generation_complete but parser-handoff queued for 3.8s
- 2026-03-10T14:22:53Z [parser-service] request-id=... schema-validate start
- 2026-03-10T14:22:56Z [parser-service] request-id=... schema-validate CPU spike (80% core)
- 2026-03-10T14:23:03Z [parser-service] request-id=... validation complete, final-chunk emitted
- 2026-03-10T14:23:05Z [api-gateway] request-id=... client timeout 504 after 12s
Profiler snippets: incremental JSON-schema validator shows worst-case O(n*m) behavior on highly-branching schemas and large arrays.
2026-03-10 15:10 - Priya Kapoor: Acked. Reproduced on staging; starting profiling on parser-service to capture CPU/hot functions.
2026-03-11 09:27 - Support (Ana Ruiz): Shared example trace with customer and asked for reduced schema to test impact. Customer confirmed reduced schema removes the long-tail.
2026-03-12 11:02 - SRE (Marcus Li): Observed parser-service instances on node gpu-10 show sustained user CPU at 70-85% during validation. Suspect synchronous full-schema validation is blocking IO loop and delaying final-chunk emission.
2026-03-13 08:45 - Priya Kapoor: Applied temporary account-scoped flag json_validation=lax for Noteable Analytics to mitigate immediate timeouts. Monitoring shows tail reduction to <0.5%.
Hypotheses: 1) Synchronous strict validation of the full JSON schema after tokenization blocks parser-worker thread and accumulates backlog under bursty traffic. 2) Large schema with many optional branches forces backtracking and expensive canonicalization during validation. 3) Interaction between streaming chunk buffering and validation means final token waits until entire object validated. Evidence: profiler traces point to validation functions (validateObject, validateArray) dominating CPU time; removing/shortening schema removes delay in controlled tests. Related PR found in parser repo to improve incremental validation (PR 412).
- Turned on account flag json_validation=lax for Noteable Analytics (temporary)
- Customer advised to reduce schema size and avoid deeply nested optional lists where possible
- Increased client timeout for critical routes to 20s as a safety buffer (temporary)
Mitigation: rolled out account flag to avoid strict post-handoff validation that blocked final-chunk emission. Customer confirmed improvement (time-to-final token median reduced from 1.2s to 0.3s, tail reduced significantly).
Next steps: engineering to implement incremental/streaming-friendly schema validation in parser-service so validation can progress concurrently with token streaming; target patch scheduled (parser-service PR 425) and follow-up test plan logged.
Follow-up owner: Priya Kapoor (parser-service team).
1) Deliver parser-service incremental validation (PR 425) and run load tests against large schema scenarios (owner: Priya). 2) Add server-side metric json_validation_queue_latency and expose per-account in Console. 3) Update runbook with guidance to temporarily switch to json_validation=lax and schema size limits. 4) Post-mortem/retrospective in #incidents and Confluence page.
Mitigated (temporary) - account-scoped lax validation flag enabled; engineering patch in progress

title: Delegated provisioner token rotation fails after IdP certificate refresh, blocking RBAC propagation
body:
Delegated provisioner token rotation fails after IdP certificate refresh, blocking RBAC propagation

Issue summary:
Delegated provisioner service intermittently fails to exchange refreshed IdP tokens after a scheduled Okta certificate rotation. When the exchange fails, downstream RBAC updates (SCIM -> internal roles) do not apply for a subset of service accounts, resulting in 403s for runbooks and internal tooling that depend on newly granted entitlements.

Impact:
- Several runbook operations and internal tooling (analytics portal, secrets-runner) report 403 for service-runner accounts issued in the last 12 hours.
- On-call productivity impacted: manual role re-provisioning required for 6 service accounts.
- No reported customer-facing outages; this affects internal automation and scheduled jobs.

Environment:
- prod-us-west cluster running identity-proxy v2.4.1 and provisioner-service v1.8.3
- Okta tenant: redwood-prod (certificate rotation completed 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. IdP cert rotation triggers Okta metadata change and IdP thumbprint update at ~03:00 UTC.
2. Provisioner-service attempts delegated token exchange for newly-created service account within 5–15 minutes and receives 401/403 from identity-proxy intermittently.
3. When exchange fails, SCIM propagation completes but authz-cache does not pick up role assignment; affected service accounts continue to be rejected by RBAC checks.

Logs / Observations:
- identity-proxy logs (2026-03-09T03:05:22Z): "WARN token-exchange: token validation failed: cert thumbprint mismatch".
- provisioner-service logs: repeated "token exchange 401" followed by "scim: user created, roles pending cache refresh".
- authz-cache metrics show "cache_misses" spike and "refresh_errors" correlated with the rotation window.
- No schema changes or recent deploys besides scheduled Okta cert rollover.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Manual re-run of role-sync job for affected accounts cleared the 403s for 6 service users.
- On-call has applied a patch to force authz-cache refresh on failed exchanges as a stopgap (deployed to prod-us-west at 2026-03-11 11:30 UTC).

Requested outcome:
- Root-cause analysis of why token exchange fails when Okta rotates certs (thumbprint handling, IdP metadata fetch, or caching TTL).
- Long-term fix to make provisioner-service resilient to IdP key rotation without manual re-syncs.
2026-03-10 09:12 - Asha Patel (reporter): Initial ticket created after oncall escalated — see attached logs in pastebin (internal).
2026-03-10 10:05 - Marco Ruiz (assignee): Reproduced pattern in staging cluster using a cert swap test; identity-proxy returns 401 when thumbprint cache stale. Added hypothesis: proxy caches IdP thumbprints for 6h; rotation window smaller than cache TTL causes mismatch.
2026-03-11 02:40 - SRE Pager (system): Deployed temporary authz-cache-refresh hook on provisioner-service to bypass stale state — mitigated most failures. Monitoring for recurrence.
2026-03-12 15:22 - Olivia Chen (identity team): Confirmed Okta metadata fetch endpoint returned new cert bundle immediately; suspect our proxy's cache layer didn't hit refresh due to conditional GET headers. Will investigate http-cache behavior in identity-proxy v2.4.1.
Ran reproducible test in staging by forcing Okta cert rotation; observed identity-proxy thumbprint cache not refreshed until TTL expiry (6h).
identity-proxy code path: fetches idp metadata using If-Modified-Since; Okta metadata endpoint returned 200 OK with new cert but identity-proxy ignored because local cache timestamp considered fresh due to time-skew edge case.
Provisioner-service does not currently retry token exchange on explicit cache-refresh; it treats 401 as terminal for that attempt and moves forward assuming eventual SCIM propagation will reconcile roles.
Authz-cache lacks a fast-path invalidation trigger tied to identity-proxy cert refresh events; role assignments left in "pending" until manual job or cache expiry.
No related recent code deploys in provisioner or identity-proxy preceding the outage window.
Workaround: implemented and deployed forced authz-cache refresh on token-exchange failure (prod-us-west) which restored access for affected service accounts.
Long-term fix plan: (1) identity team to update identity-proxy to perform unconditional metadata re-fetch when token-exchange returns 401 due to thumbprint mismatch (PR opened). (2) Add a hook so identity-proxy emits a key-rotation event to the provisioning queue which triggers authz-cache invalidation and immediate role re-evaluation. (3) Add retry logic in provisioner-service for token-exchange where first attempt fails with identity error and include exponential backoff + forced metadata refresh.
Target timeline: PRs for proxy + provisioner by 2026-03-18, staged rollout 2026-03-19, prod rollout 2026-03-21 subject to validation.

title: Batch canonicalization variance causes overlapping SLA macro matches after template import
body:
Batch canonicalization variance causes overlapping SLA macro matches after template import

Issue summary: After a bulk template import via the new UI, the canonicalization step for SLA/macros produced inconsistent keys. Multiple distinct templates collapsed to overlapping canonical keys, causing routing to match multiple escalation policies and the SLO reporting pipeline to double-count matches. Impact: internal routing automation misrouted approximately 18% of support traffic for a cohort of accounts during the nightly import window (03/05 02:00-03:00 UTC). Several internal pages in the SLO reporter show inflated counts and some alerting cohorts triggered incorrectly. Environment: production, us-east, bulk import UI v2.1.1, canonicalizer service version 1.8.2. Observed behavior: templates that previously produced unique macro keys are now producing identical canonical keys after the import. Expected behavior: canonicalization should deterministically normalize to unique keys per logical template; imports should preserve separation unless explicit duplicates exist. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations applied, and next steps to roll a permanent fix.
1) Navigate to Console > Templates > Bulk Import (v2 UI)
2) Upload a CSV with 1,200 SLA templates that include minor punctuation/whitespace variations (sample provided in attached), e.g. 'SLA: 24h - Billing', 'SLA 24h Billing', 'SLA:24h:Billing.'
3) Start import with 'canonicalize on' and default locale en-US
4) Observe job completes with success code but canonicalizer emitted warnings in logs
5) Query /internal/slo-reporter/match_counts for the imported cohort and compare pre-import vs post-import counts
2026-03-05T02:12:41Z canonicalizer WARN canonicalize_batch: found 42 collisions while deduplicating batch id=import-2026-03-05-0211
2026-03-05T02:12:41Z canonicalizer DEBUG sample_collision: ['SLA: 24h - Billing', 'SLA 24h Billing'] -> 'sla-24h-billing'
2026-03-05T02:12:41Z template-importer INFO import_complete: imported=1196 duplicates=0 canonicalized_groups=114 total_time_ms=18234
2026-03-05T02:43:02Z slo-reporter ERROR aggregation_pipeline: cohort=enterprise-us count_mismatch=+214 (expected 120, reported 334) trace_id=abc123
Initial hypothesis: canonicalizer's normalization rules were tightened in v1.8.2 to strip punctuation and adjacent stopwords, which increased collision surface for similar templates.
Reproduced locally with a reduced set (20 templates) and confirmed the same collisions when using en-US locale and default stopword list.
Telemetry shows canonicalizer emitted per-key hashes; collisions happened when whitespace/colon removal combined with aggressive stopword removal (e.g., 'the', 'and').
Impact analysis: collisions cause multiple routing macros to map to the same canonical id; router uses canonical id to select escalation policy, so multiple logical templates can be treated as a single policy leading to both misrouting and inflated metrics.
Related config: canonicalizer config uses 'stopword_set=v2' and 'collapse_digits=true' changed in PR 1528 (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-06T09:14 Maya Alvarez (Support): Noted spike in internal routing mismatches during nightly import. Opening ticket and collecting sample CSV. Slack thread: #support-tooling (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT)
2026-03-06T11:22 Ravi Patel (Infra): Reproduced collisions locally. Confirmed PR 1528 changed stopword behavior. Assigning to rule-engine owners for triage.
2026-03-07T08:05 Priya Singh (SRE): As a temporary mitigation, we disabled 'canonicalize on' for bulk imports in us-east at 02:45 UTC. This prevents new collisions but requires a cleanup for the already-imported templates.
2026-03-08T16:30 Alex Chen (Platform Eng): Investigating two remediation paths: 1) Rollback canonicalizer change to previous stopword_set, 2) Implement a scoped de-duplication that preserves template boundary metadata and avoids collapsing distinct templates.
2026-03-09T10:12 Ravi Patel (Owner): Ran a one-off re-canonicalization job with conservative rules to split the collided groups. Reconciled routing tables and pushed a fix to the reporter ingestion to correct double-counting for the affected cohort. Monitoring for 48 hours. See run in github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions/2874
Mitigations applied: (a) Immediate - disabled canonicalize-by-default for bulk import UI in prod-us-east; (b) Short-term - re-canonicalization job run with conservative rules to restore separation for affected templates; (c) Mid-term - revert or patch canonicalizer stopword behavior and add a collision-score threshold before collapsing groups. Both the router and reporter were patched to include a guard that consults template metadata before treating a canonical id as authoritative. No customer-facing incidents were triggered; impact limited to internal routing and reporting metrics. Next steps include a full rollout plan and a test harness for large bulk imports.
1) Platform Eng to open a PR that reverts stopword_set=v2 or adds opt-in switch for aggressive canonicalization (owner: Alex Chen, ETA: 2026-03-12)
2) Add unit+integration tests for bulk imports with 10k+ templates to CI (owner: QA team, ETA: 2026-03-19)
3) Run a controlled import in staging with v1.8.3 (patched canonicalizer) and validate reporter counts and router behavior (owner: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2026-03-14)
4) Postmortem to be drafted and linked to this ticket; include SLO for bulk import detection and alerting (owner: Maya Alvarez, ETA: 2026-03-17)
5) Backfill corrected counts for affected cohorts in the SLO reporter and reconcile dashboards (owner: Analytics, ETA: 2026-03-15)

title: Embedding orientation mismatch causing rerank order inversions and intermittent latency spikes
body:
Embedding orientation mismatch causing rerank order inversions and intermittent latency spikes

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a recent ingest job, rerank responses from rwd-rerank-v1 return inverted orderings intermittently (top results move to bottom) and request p95 latency doubles for affected queries. The problem is non-deterministic and correlates with particular embed batches.

Impact:
- LexiSearch reports degraded search quality for ~3% of queries; visible inverted top-k in production dashboards.
- Tail latency increases up to 2x for affected requests (p95 from ~120ms to ~280ms) and we observe retry storms causing transient 503s on the rerank service.
- Customer uses dedicated capacity and pins to rwd-embed-v2 for embeddings.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster in us-east (prod).
- Ingest pipeline: batch-encoder -> augment-service -> embed-ingest -> cache -> reranker.
- Rolling upgrade of embed workers completed 2025-02-16.

Steps to reproduce (initial report):
1) Run ingest job with sample dataset attached by customer (provided below).
2) Issue /v1/rerank with query ids qids in the sample and compare top-10 ordering across two runs.
3) Observe that ordering flips for the same query in ~3% of requests; tail latencies spike and retries are observed.

Logs / Observed traces:
- Example trace: trace_id=trc-20250218-9a7b, request_id=req-77c2; reranker logs show a cache-miss and then synchronous fallback to CPU path with multiple small batches.
- Embed ingest logs show intermittent warnings: "orientation mismatch detected: norm-toggle inconsistent" with meta=encoder-instance-17.
- Router logs show retries: 429 -> 502 -> 503 cascades for some requests.

Attachments from customer: sample_input.json (200 query vectors) and a side-by-side CSV showing two runs with different top-k.

Immediate customer ask:
- Explain cause and provide mitigation to stop quality regressions and tail latency while we investigate a fix.
2025-02-18 -- Priya Nair (Support): Acknowledged. Assigned to infra/serving. Requested sample_input.json from customer and asked for a few failing request_ids and timestamps.
2025-02-18 -- LexiSearch (Customer): Uploaded sample_input.json and two CSV exports showing order inversion for query ids: q-1302, q-1429, q-1890. Noted issue started after the encoder worker rollout on 2025-02-16.
2025-02-19 -- Miguel Ortega (SRE): Reproduced inversion in our staging with customer's sample when using mixed encoder versions. Observed embed vectors differ by a sign-flip across a subset of dimensions for same doc id depending on ingest worker. Opening hypothesis: a normalization/rotation toggle mismatch introduced during rollout.
2025-02-19 -- Miguel Ortega (SRE): Added trace link https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/trc-20250218-9a7b and PR reference https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4289 for a candidate fix to the encoder's postprocess step.
2025-02-20 -- Priya Nair (Support): Notified customer of ongoing root-cause analysis and recommended temporary mitigation: pinning embed-ingest to pre-rollout encoder image (encoder-v2.7-stable) and enabling a short-circuit in reranker to bypass CPU fallback for requests showing orientation header mismatch.
2025-02-21 -- LexiSearch (Customer): Applied the pin as instructed; reports immediate improvement — order inversions stop for newly ingested documents, tail latency returns to expected ranges for new traffic. They asked for a permanent fix timeline and whether historical documents need re-ingestion.
Summary of investigation so far:
- Reproducible when the ingest pipeline mixes encoder versions that differ in an optional post-processing step: a per-encoder 'orientation' flag that applies a deterministic rotation matrix to embeddings for compatibility with downstream quantized kernels.
- During rollout, encoder-v2.8 introduced the rotation toggle defaulting to 'on', while prior versions had it 'off'. If embeddings produced with and without rotation coexist, cosine distances used by reranker produce order inversions because effective angular positions of vectors shift.
- The orientation mismatch also prevents cache hits (cache key includes orientation hash) causing more cache misses -> more synchronous rerank calls -> batching to fall back to CPU path -> increased p95.
- Trace logs show a higher incidence of small-batch CPU fallbacks for affected requests.
- No evidence of bit-flip or serialization endian issues; numerical checksums differ predictably according to rotation pattern.

Hypotheses:
1) Configuration drift during rollout left some encoder pods with orientation=false and others with orientation=true.
2) The embed-ingest pipeline did not enforce a schema header for orientation until recently; downstream services tolerate but don't normalize when mixing variants.
3) Cache keys lacking a stable orientation tag allowed mixed vectors to be stored and served interchangeably.
Immediate: finish PR to make encoder orientation explicit in the header and have embed-ingest normalize at write-time (PR 4289).
Short term mitigation: recommend customers pin encoder version or enable automatic re-ingest normalization at embed-ingest. Documented workaround applied for LexiSearch.
Longer term: add a pipeline-level validation step that rejects ingest batches that contain mixed-orientation vectors; add e2e test around orientation compatibility and add orientation to cache key formatting.
Follow-up tasks: INT ticket to sweep customers on dedicated clusters for mixed encoder versions; data-migration playbook for re-ingestion of historical docs if customer requests (estimate: tooling + validation ~2 weeks).
Quality regression (inverted top-k) for ~3% of queries and tail latency increase to p95~280ms on affected requests; customer applied temporary pin and reported immediate improvement for new traffic.

title: Session token rotation interferes with pin coherence during incremental canary causing cross-variant fallbacks
body:
Session token rotation interferes with pin coherence during incremental canary causing cross-variant fallbacks

Issue summary:
During an incremental canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 in us-west, the customer (BrightAssist AI) reported a rise in cross-variant fallback responses where traffic pinned to the new canary model intermittently routed to an older model. This coincided with our recent session-token rotation job running during the same maintenance window.

Impact:
- ~2% of requests from a subset of pinned sessions returned responses from the fallback model (open-llama-7b-q4_0) instead of the pinned canary.
- Customer reports degraded QA metrics for conversation continuity and higher token costs.
- Incident impacted a single dedicated region (us-west) and affected several long-running user sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (BrightAssist AI) on prod us-west
- Serving runtime: v3.8.1
- Edge/session proxy: session-proxy v1.14
- Canary rollout: incremental (10% -> 25%) over 2026-03-10 02:00-04:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 with session-affinity preserved.
2) Trigger session-token rotation job (automated security task that rotates session tokens/leases).
3) Long-running sessions that received a pinned token experienced token refresh mid-stream.
4) Some edge nodes rejected rotated token headers causing a re-authorization path that did not carry the pin metadata.
5) Requests without pin metadata were routed by policy to the fallback (older) model under burst constraints.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 200 responses that contained outputs inconsistent with the canary variant (style/stop-words matched older model).
- No 5xx errors; routing decision led to expected but unwanted variant responses.
- Session logs show header rewrite/drop on specific edge-proxy instances.

Expected behavior:
- Session-token rotation should preserve pin-coherence: rotated tokens must retain or re-associate the session-level pin metadata so requests remain pinned to the intended model variant.

Attachments/Logs:
- tail of session-proxy logs (errors showing header validation mismatches) attached in ticket thread.
- Route coordinator traces showing decision tree for sample session IDs.
- Customer provided transcripts highlighting semantic divergence.

2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial report and customer transcript received. Marking P1 due to production QA impact. Notifying SRE on-call.
2026-03-10 - SRE on-call (Arjun Patel): Reproduced header drop on edge-proxy instance ep-12. Suspect token rotation handshake timing race. Captured pcap and traces.
2026-03-11 - Routing eng (Lars Becker): Confirmed some requests lost pin metadata after token refresh; edge-proxy returned 200 but omitted x-session-pin header before proxy->coordinator hop. Investigating why proxy didn't reattach pin after reauth.
2026-03-12 - Session proxy eng (Nina Alvarez): Found a bug in session-proxy v1.14 where rotated-token code path mistakenly clears temporary metadata when auth returns 204 (no-body). Preparing hotfix branch.
2026-03-12 - Customer (BrightAssist AI - ops): Confirmed symptom window matches their internal maintenance window. They've applied a temporary mitigation (pause canary expansion) and requested ETA for fix.
2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Escalated to PM for coordination on patch rollout and asked customer if they can accept a staged patch on their dedicated nodes tonight.
2026-03-13 - Engineering (Lars Becker): Hotfix PR opened and smoke tests green in staging. Planning a targeted restart of session-proxy fleet in us-west for 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC. Scheduled rollback if regressions observed.
Hypothesis 1: session-token rotation handshake returns a 204 (no-content) path that clears ephemeral headers; session-proxy code treats 204 as success and does not rehydrate pin metadata.
Hypothesis 2: route-coordinator relies on x-session-pin header strictly from edge; if header absent, it applies fallback policies even when a server-side session store contains pin data. Some requests short-circuited coordinator lookup due to cache TTL mismatch.
Evidence: packet traces show auth response sequence where rotated token accepted but edge-proxy emitted downstream request without x-session-pin for ~15s window on ep-12 and ep-17. Route coordinator logs show fallback path invoked for those requests.
Repro steps validated in staging by invoking rotation job concurrently with simulated canary traffic; saw identical header loss on session-proxy image with v1.14 but not on v1.13.
Scope estimate: ~2-3% of active pinned sessions in rollout cohort experienced at least one fallback call in the observed window. No data loss or secret exposure observed.
Risk assessment: fix is low-risk code change to session-proxy rehydrate path but requires coordinated restart of edge nodes to pick up fix in dedicated customer environment.
Workaround (customer applied): Pause canary expansion and instruct client to reconnect affected sessions to force rebind; this immediately reduced cross-variant fallbacks to <0.1%.
Fix deployed: session-proxy hotfix v1.14.1 released that preserves and reattaches x-session-pin after token rotation when auth returns 204. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/session-proxy/pull/331
Rollout plan: staged restart of us-west session-proxy instances in waves of 5% to limit interruption. Completed 2026-03-13 23:15 UTC. Smoke tests and customer validation passed.
Verification: Post-deploy traces show no header loss during rotation; monitored pinned-variant hit-rate for cohort improved from ~98% to >99.9% within 30 minutes.
Follow-ups: (1) Add an end-to-end test for token rotation + pin preservation in our canary harness. (2) Update runbook to avoid running token rotation jobs during canary expansions for dedicated customers until automated canary-friendly rotation is implemented. (3) Add observability metric for x-session-pin drops at edge-proxy.
Communication: Notified customer of fix and closure steps; recommended resuming canary expansion after confirmation window. Ticket to be closed after 48h of stable metrics.

title: Client-side priority rewrite causes incomplete streamed XML and missing closing tag on resume
body:
Client-side priority rewrite causes incomplete streamed XML and missing closing tag on resume

Issue summary: Customer's SSE streaming sessions intermittently resume with an incomplete XML payload; the final closing tag (</document>) is missing after reconnect. Impact: downstream XML parsers in customer's ingestion pipeline fail with well-formedness errors, causing message drops and a production alert. Scope: observed on several live sessions for FinBridge in us-east; appears reproducible with their client (custom browser worker) behind an enterprise proxy that rewrites priority headers.

Observed behavior: After a short network disconnect (client reconnect with resume), the server emits the resumed chunks but the last chunk boundary is truncated such that the XML closing tag is split across two TCP frames and the resumed stream omits the trailing bytes of the close tag. Expected behavior: resume should deliver the full XML stream, including all closing tags and terminators.

Notes: Customer provided captured SSE stream and client-side trace (attached in logs field). They report the issue increases when the corporate proxy performs a 302-based rewrite or strips/rewrites the Priority header, and when the client uses a custom priority-rewrite middleware.

1) Use FinBridge test account and open a streaming SSE session via their in-house client behind a corporate proxy that rewrites 'Priority' headers.
2) Begin a long XML streaming response from redwood-13b-v1 that ends with a </document> closing tag.
3) Simulate a short network disconnect (client 1–3s offline) and allow the client to reconnect with resume semantics.
4) Observe the resumed SSE payload in the client – the final closing tag is missing or split and parser fails.
5) Repeat with the proxy bypassed — behavior does not reproduce (indicates proxy-induced boundary change).
2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging with a synthetic proxy that rewrites priority header; observed chunk boundary shifted by a single byte in ~62% of attempts.
Hypothesis: Proxy rewrite inserts or removes bytes in HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 conversion path causing chunk-splitting to occur inside an XML closing tag at resume boundary.
Alternative hypothesis: Client priority middleware reorders frames which, combined with our resume offset calculation, leads to off-by-one in resumed byte range.
Confirmed: When proxy preserves raw downstream chunk boundaries (pass-through), resume returns correct document. When proxy injects a 'Via' header and strips 'Priority' header, failure rate increases.
Trace IDs: 01F8Y2X0-abc (staging reproduce), 01F8Y9Z7-def (customer capture).
Related work: PR #2154 in serving-runtime adds stricter resume-offset validation (see related_github_prs).
[2026-03-09T14:22:03Z] sse-session-id=abc123 chunk-idx=42 size=1024
[2026-03-09T14:22:06Z] connection-reset client-ip=198.51.100.25
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] sse-resume session=abc123 resumed-from-offset=40960 emitted-last-bytes=...<docu
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] sse-final emitted-last-bytes=...ment>  <-- MISSING in customer capture
Trace: see attached 'finbridge_sse_capture_20260309.txt' from customer (they attached full hex diff).
2026-03-10 09:18 - Support (Ava Martinez): Opened with customer-provided capture. Customer reports parser exceptions and data loss. Marked P1 due to production impact.
2026-03-10 11:02 - Eng (Daniel Cho): I can repro in staging when running a proxy that rewrites Priority. Looks like resume offset calculation assumes chunk boundaries are stable across proxy; adding instrumentation to validate actual byte ranges.
2026-03-11 08:34 - Customer (FinBridge SRE): We observed this after adding an edge rewrite for A/B testing. We can temporarily bypass the rewrite for critical streams; please advise a workaround.
2026-03-11 10:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Suggested workaround to customer: enable proxy 'preserve-chunk-boundaries' flag or disable priority header rewrite for streaming endpoints. Customer confirmed bypass reduces failure rate.
2026-03-12 14:20 - Eng (Daniel Cho): Deployed staging build with additional checks in resume path to ensure we don't drop trailing bytes when offset is near a chunk boundary. Need to run load tests before rolling to prod.
2026-03-13 09:45 - Support (Ava Martinez): Customer asking for timeline to prod fix and whether this affects dedicated/private deployments — Eng will confirm.
Slack reference: #support-streaming (thread ts: 1612345678.000200)
Pending - workaround acknowledged by customer (disable proxy priority rewrite for streaming endpoints). Eng has a staging fix under test.
Temporary workaround: Customer to bypass proxy rewrite for streaming endpoints or enable 'preserve-chunk-boundaries' if available.
Planned fix: Adjust resume-offset computation in serving-runtime to validate trailing bytes against an emitted checksum when close to chunk boundary; add server-side defensive padding if mismatch detected.
Rollout plan: merge PR after perf validation, canary to 5% of prod traffic in us-east, monitor stream well-formedness metrics and error-rate dashboard (stream/parser/invalid-xml).
Follow-ups: Create internal runbook for customers behind aggressive proxies and add a console warning when proxy rewrite patterns are detected on streaming sessions.

title: Funnel conversion widget shows zero counts after retention compaction window
body:
Funnel conversion widget shows zero counts after retention compaction window

Issue summary:
Customer NimbusHealth reports that the 'User conversion' funnel panel on their org dashboard intermittently shows all zero counts for multi-hour ranges immediately after nightly retention compaction runs. This affects billing-tracked conversion metrics and has caused missing alerts for conversion-rate drops.

Impact:
- Several teams at NimbusHealth rely on the funnel card to measure daily onboarding conversion; values show 0s for windows that previously had non-zero traffic.
- Alerting tied to the funnel (conversion_rate < 3%) did not fire because the dataset collapsed to zeros rather than being marked as partial/unknown.
- Customer is enterprise tier and expressed operational impact to their analytics deliverables.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east region (org: nimbushealth-prod, console org id: org_8349)
- Affected dashboard: "Acquisition -> Onboarding Funnel" (panel id 42)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open the funnel dashboard for org_8349 during UTC window immediately after nightly retention compaction (approx 03:30-04:30 UTC).
2) Select time range: Last 24h and apply event filters for "signup_completed" -> "account_verified" steps.
3) Observe counts displayed in funnel and check raw query via "View underlying query".
4) Compare same panel before compaction (e.g., previous day) and after compaction.

Observed behavior:
- Funnel card displays 0 for each step for some time after compaction.
- Raw underlying query returns empty rows in console despite ingestion metrics showing events present in storage and downstream billing counts.
- Alerts suppressed; no entries in alert history for the expected triggers.

Expected behavior:
- Funnel should show non-zero counts matching raw event store within SLO (up to a few minutes of lag).
- Alerts should evaluate against either the raw count or be marked as partial/failed and notify on degradation.

Recent changes/notes from customer:
- Customer confirmed they did a manual backfill for week-of-2026-03-07 which completed by 02:00 UTC on 2026-03-10.
- They saw the zeroing immediately following the nightly retention compaction that ran at 03:15 UTC.

Logs & evidence provided by customer:
- Screenshot of funnel (attached in ticket): funnel_zero_2026-03-10.png
- Query trace id returned when customer clicked "View underlying query": qid-7a9f3c22
- Ingestion metric snippet: "events_ingested.org_8349.signup_completed = 18,472 for 2026-03-09" (they provided CSV export).
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1678549200000

Temporary workaround reported:
- Customer exported raw events and recomputed funnel externally; also toggling dashboard time-range off/on caused the card to re-run and surface counts intermittently.

Investigation summary (support):
- Support triaged and validated gaps between console query engine and the post-compaction query planner. See investigation_notes and comments.

Recommended immediate mitigation:
- Run the adhoc rehydrate job (console-backfill-run) for org_8349 for the affected hour-range to restore interactive queries while engineering investigates root cause.

Next steps:
- Eng to validate retention compaction path in the console query planner and confirm whether compaction tombstones are being interpreted as hard zeros rather than deleted/missing data.
- Add guard in alert evaluation to mark results as partial when underlying query returns empty shards after compaction.
- Publish communication to NimbusHealth with timeline and expected ETA for fix.
2026-03-10 10:20 UTC - Support (Marco): Reproduced behaviour in prod by scheduling a compaction mirror run in staging. Funnel panel went to zero for 15-20 minutes post-compact.
2026-03-10 13:05 UTC - SRE (Lena Kim): Observed that compaction writes tombstone markers and our console query planner path incorrectly merges tombstone markers with aggregate counters producing zeroed aggregates instead of skipping shards.
2026-03-11 09:40 UTC - Eng (Dmitri Volkov): Initial hypothesis: shard-merge path in aggregation engine uses COALESCE over shards; when tombstone present COALESCE yields 0. Need to change to treat tombstone as NULL and skip in sum().
2026-03-11 15:22 UTC - Eng (Dmitri): Pushed prototype fix to treat tombstone as NULL in aggregation; added unit tests for funnel aggregation across compaction boundary. PR linked in related_github_prs.
2026-03-12 02:00 UTC - Support (Marco): Ran console-backfill-run for org_8349; customer confirmed UI shows counts restored for previously zeroed ranges. Monitoring for recurrence after next compaction window.
Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Customer reported as high-impact; provided screenshot and CSV export. Asked for priority review and immediate mitigation options.
Marco Ruiz (Support, 2026-03-10): Acknowledged; scheduling triage with SRE and Eng. Temporary mitigation: export/raw recompute or run backfill (see workaround).
Lena Kim (SRE, 2026-03-10): Confirmed compaction ran at 03:15 UTC. Creating monitoring alert to detect funnel-zero spike across orgs post-compaction. Linked slack thread #support-prod.

Marco Ruiz (Support, 2026-03-12): Noted compensation request and routed to CS lead (linked issue SUP-501234). Eng estimated fix rollout in next patch window (2026-03-16).
Workaround: adhoc rehydrate/backfill restored dashboard counts. Root cause: aggregation engine treated retention tombstone markers as zeros during shard merge, collapsing aggregates. Fix: change aggregation merge to ignore tombstones (treat as null) and add alert-evaluation guard for partial results. Patch merged to staging; scheduled rollout to prod 2026-03-16. Customer notified and follow-up scheduled.

title: Approval: time-boxed aggregated session dump (redacted) for security investigation
body:
Approval: time-boxed aggregated session dump (redacted) for security investigation

Request from Security to produce an aggregated, redacted snapshot of user session metadata and non-sensitive model telemetry to support an ongoing phishing investigation. This is not a full raw export — the goal is a minimized, inspectable artifact that preserves sequence-level timing and routing characteristics but strips or tokenizes any potential PII and model outputs. Requestor: Security (Ben Carter). Context: post-alert triage for suspicious account activity impacting three enterprise customers.
Investigative need only; dataset will be used by Security and Legal to determine scope of suspected account compromise. Low risk if redaction is performed correctly; high compliance risk if raw customer outputs or unredacted PII are exposed.
aggregated session timeline (session ids + event timestamps)
route-level latency histogram for selected buckets
tokenized prompt/response fingerprints (hashes) only — no cleartext outputs
config snapshot (model version, kernel hints) for the affected time window
1) Exclude full-text model outputs. 2) Replace user identifiers and email-like tokens with deterministic pseudonyms (UID-<hash>). 3) Hash prompts/responses with SHA256 and include only the first 8 chars of the hex as a fingerprint. 4) Strip any detected PII using the PII detection rule set v3.2. 5) Manual spot-check by Compliance on a 1% sample prior to sharing. All steps recorded in the artifact manifest.
Read-only access to the generated artifact for Security + Legal for 48 hours after delivery; artifact must be deleted from temporary storage at expiry and deletion confirmed in ticket.
1. Narrow time window: 2026-03-04T14:00:00Z to 2026-03-04T18:00:00Z.
2. Run serving-runtime aggregated query job with --include-metadata --exclude-fulloutputs flags.
3. Pipe raw output through redaction pipeline (pii-scrub v3.2 + token hashing).
4. Store artifact in temporary S3 bucket with restricted ACL and server-side encryption.
5. Notify Compliance for 1% manual sample review.
6. Upon approval, grant read-only signed URL to approvers and attach manifest to ticket.
Initial alert triggered by anomaly detector: unusual ratio of streaming disconnects to token counts for three customer orgs.
Affected model variants: rwd-1-large and rwd-1-quantized (snapshot at 2026-03-04).
Preliminary metric: 3x increase in prefix retransmissions; likely caused by network retries affecting streaming join logic.
No evidence yet of exfiltration of customer outputs; need fingerprints to correlate with customer-reported samples.
Pending approval. Compliance requested minor change to redaction plan (include salt for pseudonym hashes). Action: SRE to add salt and rerun a fresh sample for Compliance sign-off.
