title: Duplicate function invocations after SDK retry when edge-proxy rotates nonce mid-session
body:
Duplicate function invocations after SDK retry when edge-proxy rotates nonce mid-session

Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate external tool/function invocations after client-side retry. BrightDocs uses Redwood Private inside a VPC with an edge proxy that performs periodic nonce rotation for HSM-backed auth. Impact: At least one customer workflow has duplicate downstream payments and two idempotent markers created. Environment: private deployment behind company-managed proxy, SDKs used: Python 1.3.x, TypeScript 1.3.x, Go 1.2.x. Observed behavior: when proxy rotates nonce mid-session the SDK retry path replays function calls because the incoming request lacks the original idempotency token; client retry triggers identical function payload which the downstream webhook accepts as new. Expected behavior: retries should be safely deduplicated or SDK should surface a clear failure so customer can avoid duplicate side effects.
1) BrightDocs runs a long-lived chat session invoking a 3rd-party payment tool via function_call on redwood-compat-7b.
2) The edge proxy rotates the HSM nonce and rewrites a header used by the Private control plane for authentication mid-session (simulated by rotating JWTs every 90s).
3) The SDK (Python/TS/Go) experiences a transient 504 on the streaming ACK and triggers its retry/backoff path for the final tool confirmation handshake.
4) Because the proxy dropped/rewrote the per-request idempotency header (x-redwood-idempotency) the server treats the retry as a fresh request and re-issues the function_call webhook to the customer's endpoint.
5) Downstream system records a second payment action; customer sees duplicate side effect.
6) Reproducible with the Python sample below using local proxy script that rotates header token every 60-120s.
[2026-03-10T18:22:47Z] SDK(Python) - warning: stream ack timeout; entering retry path (attempt 2)
[2026-03-10T18:22:47Z] Proxy - rotated-auth-nonce: nonce=17f4 -> 17f5; rewritten header x-hsm-nonce
[2026-03-10T18:22:48Z] API - received request missing x-redwood-idempotency; generated new idempotency id: a1b2c3
[2026-03-10T18:22:48Z] Webhook - POST /payments returned 200 Payment created id=pay_0X9
[2026-03-10T18:22:49Z] API - received request missing x-redwood-idempotency; generated new idempotency id: d4e5f6
[2026-03-10T18:22:49Z] Webhook - POST /payments returned 200 Payment created id=pay_0Y2
Pinned SDK to older minor that suppresses automatic retry (python 1.2.1) — reduces duplicates but loses helpful resume behavior.
Added a compensating check in downstream webhook to dedupe by merchant_transaction_id.
Configured proxy to stop rewriting x-redwood-idempotency, which fixed problem in test environment.
BrightDocs (customer): We saw duplicate charges in production at 2026-03-10T18:22:49Z. Important: our upstream merchant wouldn't refund automatically. Please advise a safe fix without disabling retries.
Support (Ava): Thanks — collecting logs and environment. Can you confirm whether your proxy rewrites any 'x-redwood-*' headers? Also please attach a redaction-safe SDK trace if available.
Customer (BrightDocs): Proxy does rotate HSM nonce and re-signs tokens; we intentionally rewrite some auth headers. We thought idempotency was maintained by SDK.
Eng (Kenji): Reproducing locally with proxy script; initial hypothesis: header rewrite removes the idempotency token observed by our backend and SDK retry generates a new token on resume leading to duplicate webhook callbacks.
SRE (Maya): Running quick check on private deployment logs - see two distinct idempotency ids created within 2s of each other for same session id. Investigating whether server should preserve previous idempotency token when a session reconnects.
Hypothesis 1: SDK passes idempotency token only once at request start; on reconnect it regenerates token if client does not persist it across connection resets.
Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy rewrites or strips the 'x-redwood-idempotency' header and also rotates a nonce used to sign a related header that the Private control plane expects; as a result our backend can't match the retry to the original request.
Reproduction: Built a minimal proxy that removes 'x-redwood-idempotency' and rotates auth header every 60s; reproduced duplicate webhook invocations with Python/TS/Go samples attached.
Quick mitigation tested: Ingesting an 'idempotency-key' from request body (fallback) allowed dedupe; not ideal for customers that rely on header preservation.
SDK change candidate: Make SDK persist the last idempotency token per-session and re-send it on reconnect attempts, rather than generating a fresh token for a retried streaming ACK. This avoids depending on proxies to preserve headers.
Server-side change candidate: Accept a replay-assertion containing original request-hash from client to dedupe if idempotency header missing. Requires SDK + runtime schema change.
Risk: Persisting per-session token has memory/scale implications for very large multiplexed connections; need TTL and eviction policy.
Python repro snippet (conceptual):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key='redacted')
# send chat + function_call, the SDK stores idempotency in session state and will reuse it on retries
response = client.chat.stream(..., reuse_session_id=True)
TS repro snippet (conceptual):
const c = new Redwood({apiKey: 'redacted'});
// current TS SDK regenerates a token on reconnect; suggested pattern: provide explicit idempotencyId
await c.chat.create({messages, function_call: {name:'charge'}, idempotencyId: merchantTxId})
Go repro notes: Go SDK current behaviour mirrors others; ephemeral idempotency token per request. Suggest adding an option 'ReuseIdempotencyOnReconnect: true'.
1) Short term: Advise BrightDocs to configure their proxy to preserve 'x-redwood-idempotency' and/or to include an idempotency token in request body (merchant_tx_id) until SDK patch ships.
2) Mid term: Ship SDK patch (Python/TS/Go) that persists last-request idempotency token per session and re-sends it for retries and reconnects. Add configuration flag to opt-in.
3) Server-side: Add heuristic dedupe when incoming request lacks idempotency header but includes same session_id+sequence and identical function payload within a short time window (configurable), and log detected dedupes for audit.
4) Postmortem with BrightDocs and customer-facing guidance in Support KB for proxies that rotate auth headers.
Workaround recommended: configure proxy to preserve 'x-redwood-idempotency' OR include explicit idempotency token in the function_call payload. Implemented customer compensating dedupe. Next release: SDK option to reuse session-scoped idempotency tokens (ETA: 2026-03-20).
2026-03-11: Provided BrightDocs with proxy config sample to whitelist 'x-redwood-idempotency' and suggested temporary downstream dedupe by merchant_transaction_id.
2026-03-12: Engineering approved SDK opt-in feature 'reuse_session_idempotency' targeted for 1.4.2. PR created referenced above.
Follow-up: Create KB article 'Private deployments behind header-rewriting proxies: idempotency guidance' and include sample proxy configs for common proxies (nginx, envoy).
If customer cannot modify proxy, propose server-side fallback after security review; flagged for roadmap discussion.

title: Request: Automated lifecycle for new internal Jira projects + linked Confluence spaces + Slack channels
body:
Request: Automated lifecycle for new internal Jira projects + linked Confluence spaces + Slack channels

Issue summary:
Request to build an automated provisioning and lifecycle policy for new internal Jira projects that also creates and wires a linked Confluence space and a Slack channel. This is intended to replace the current manual onboarding steps and ensure consistent naming, ACLs, retention, and deprovisioning across org projects.

Request:
- Create an Atlassian automation + Terraform workflow that, given a Jira project template selection and an approved request, will:
  1) Provision a Jira project with a predefined workflow and permission scheme.
  2) Create a Confluence space with the 'internal-team' space blueprint and apply page templates (onboarding, runbook, architecture).
  3) Create a Slack channel with standardized naming and an associated private admin user group.
  4) Add initial members from SCIM group(s) and configure role-based access.
  5) Tag all artifacts with project metadata (owner, lifecycle-date, sensitivity).
  6) Schedule an automated review and potential archival/deletion at 12 months unless extended.

Business impact:
- Reduce time-to-onboard for new internal projects from days to hours.
- Reduce permission drift and security misconfigurations.
- Improve discoverability and standardization of runbooks and templates.

Requirements and constraints:
- Must support SCIM-backed groups for provisioning (AAD SSO integration).
- Slack channels should be private by default; naming convention: rw-<team>-<project>-env (e.g., rw-platform-provision-prod).
- Confluence spaces should inherit read restrictions for 'all-employees' where applicable and apply confidential flags for sensitive projects.
- Jira project keys should not collide with existing keys; automation must propose a key and have an approval step for final creation.
- Audit logs for creation actions must be preserved and linked to the Jira ticket.
- Security review: any project tagged 'sensitive' must require Security approval before Slack channel creation.

Acceptance criteria:
- POST-provision the Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channel exist and are linked in the Jira issue.
- Initial member provisioning adds at least: project owner, tech lead, and platform-admin group.
- Automated retention/archival job runs and sends reminders 30 days before expiry.
- All steps are idempotent and have clear failure/execution logs visible to platform-ops.

Proposed rollout plan:
1) Build automation in a sandbox environment and test with a pilot team (Platform-Infra).
2) Validate SCIM group behavior and Slack rate-limits.
3) Run security review and update the approval matrix.
4) Pilot for 2 months, gather feedback, then enable self-service in internal request portal.

Runbooks / links:
- Project Space Standards: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/123456/Project+Space+Standards
- Onboarding Checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/789012/Team+Onboarding+Checklist

Notes for implementer:
- Prefer Terraform for the infra-as-code pieces and use Atlassian Automation or API webhooks for cross-product wiring.
- Keep an audit trail: store action IDs in the Jira ticket as comments.


Initial feasibility check completed on 2026-03-11: Slack SCIM provisioning is supported for our workspace but rate-limits for channel creation are 50/min for the app token; plan around batching and job retries.
Confluence automation supports space creation via API but applying blueprints requires an extra step; Terraform provider for Confluence covers space metadata but not templates — will combine provider + automation script.
Jira key collision handling: will propose a key using namespace 'RW' + shortname + increment, and surface suggested key in approval step.
Security gating: Security team confirmed manual approval webhook is acceptable for 'sensitive' tag until we have an automated policy engine.
Estimated effort: 3 sprints (design + pilot + iterate) including a one-week security review window.

Tom Nguyen (Assignee, 2026-03-11): I can take ownership of the automation. Next step: create a sandbox Terraform PR and a sample Atlassian automation rule. Removing direct Slack creation in the first iteration to validate SCIM groups first.
Priya Shah (Identity, 2026-03-11): Confirmed SCIM groups exist for platform-admins and engineering-teams groups. We need to whitelist the app for group provisioning.
Marcus Lee (Security, 2026-03-12): Security will require a checklist for data classification and proof-of-ownership before Slack channels for sensitive projects are created. Adding label 'security-review'.
Tom Nguyen (2026-03-12): Linked a draft infra PR for initial review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4312
Pending: implementation plan approved by Platform and Security. Next milestone: create sandbox PR and automation rule (owner: Tom Nguyen). Security to sign off on the sensitive-project gating before enabling Slack creation for those tags.

title: Per-tenant live audit stream with manifested ack protocol and export TTL assertions
body:
Per-tenant live audit stream with manifested ack protocol and export TTL assertions

Issue summary:
Customer requests a per-tenant live audit stream that includes a manifested acknowledgement protocol (per-batch manifest with checksums and offsets) and a TTL assertion for retention compliance. They want the stream delivered to a tenant-scoped S3 prefix and an option for an on-the-wire SSE-signed HTTP delivery.

Impact:
GreenWave Health is undergoing an external security audit and needs evidence that (1) events for their tenant are exported in order, (2) each delivery includes an immutable manifest with SHA-256 checksums and byte offsets, and (3) there is a verifiable TTL assertion asserting events are retained for 90 days and then flagged for deletion. Without this they cannot complete their SOC2 audit and risk delayed go-live.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Live stream endpoint that can be filtered by tenant_id and event_type.
- Manifest per file/batch with: range offsets, SHA-256 per-event, batch HMAC signed with Redwood KMS key (attestation), and monotonically increasing manifest sequence id.
- Endpoint or delivery contains TTL assertion metadata for each event (retention_until timestamp) and a signed proof that retention policy is enforced.
- Delivery modes: streaming SSE-signed HTTP push OR S3 prefix notifications (hourly rollups).
- Proof materials: manifest schema, example manifest for last 24h, verification steps, and a small sample bundle for the auditor.

Security constraints:
- PII fields should be redacted according to the already-agreed tenant pseudonymization policy unless the customer has a DPA amendment permitting full fields.
- KMS key used for HMAC signing must be customer-specific for enterprise tenants where requested.

Proposed delivery formats (customer preference):
1) Hourly gzipped NDJSON files to s3://greenwave-audit/tenant-<tenant_id>/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/ + accompanying manifest JSON and .sig HMAC file.
2) Optional real-time HTTP SSE endpoint for live tailing with per-event sequence and manifest emission every 5 minutes.

Steps to reproduce (how Support should validate):
1. Enable "tenant live export" feature flag for tenant across prod_us-east.
2. Configure test tenant using GreenWave's tenant_id: gw-0321-test and destination s3 prefix provided in attachment.
3. Generate synthetic traffic using the provided event generator for 1 hour.
4. Verify S3 files appear hourly with accompanying manifest and .sig files.
5. Run verification script (provided in attachment) to check SHA-256, batch HMAC signature validation and monotonic manifest sequence.

Logs / Evidence references:
- Provided sample event IDs: ev-20260228-9f3a, ev-20260228-9f3b, ev-20260228-9f3c
- Relevant metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/audit-export?tenant=gw-0321-test
- Recent error window: 2026-02-28T18:00:00Z - 2026-02-28T20:30:00Z (see S3 put failures in audit-collector logs)

Notes for SRE/Eng:
Customer requests a per-tenant KMS attestation; if not feasible for on-host signing, provide a documented mitigation path and timeline. Need an engineering estimate for on-wire SSE-signed delivery and manifest generation latency impact.

title: Streaming disconnects spike after customer upgraded Redwood SDK (Node) 1.11.x → 1.12.0
body:
Streaming disconnects spike after customer upgraded Redwood SDK (Node) 1.11.x → 1.12.0

Customer reports elevated rate of streaming disconnects after upgrading Redwood Node SDK from 1.11.x to 1.12.0.

Issue summary
- Symptom: Streaming responses terminate early with client-side errors, typically after 15–40s, sometimes immediately after first tokens.
- Customer impact: Increased request retries, partial responses, degraded UX for end users.
- Onset: Within ~30 minutes of deploying SDK 1.12.0 to ~50% of traffic.
- Scope: Only streaming chat completions; non-streaming requests appear normal.

Customer-reported errors
- Node: `Error: stream closed` / `ECONNRESET` / occasional `ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR` (customer uses an HTTP/2 agent)
- Customer observation: retries succeed; failures cluster during higher concurrency.

Questions / requested artifacts
- Examples of request_ids from failed streams
- SDK version(s) and Node runtime version
- Whether requests traverse any outbound proxy / egress firewall
- Confirmation of transport mode (fetch vs undici vs http2 wrapper)

Initial Support hypothesis
- Could be:
  (A) client-side regression in SDK 1.12.0 streaming parser / abort handling
  (B) gateway-side idle timeout / proxy buffering
  (C) runtime stalls causing downstream timeout and connection resets

Notes for taxonomy boundary (for Reliability Program)
- This ticket is being used as an example of classification ambiguity: symptom looks like platform streaming instability, but root cause may be client SDK behavior. If escalated to an incident, classify based on primary system at fault once confirmed; do not default to runtime unless runtime signals correlate.

Repro steps (customer)
1) Upgrade `@redwoodinference/sdk` to 1.12.0
2) Run 200 concurrent streaming chat requests (avg prompt ~1.2k tokens)
3) Observe ~3–7% of streams disconnect before completion

Support-side quick checks performed
- No concurrent spike in 5xx on zl-prod-ue1 gateway.
- No clear serving-runtime OOM / crash-loop evidence in the time window.
- Some increase in gateway "client_disconnect" counters but not in upstream errors.
2025-11-18 18:44 UTC (Owen Phillips, Support) — Acknowledged Zenlytics escalation. Asked for 10 request_ids from failed streams and confirmed rollout timeline. Noted that we see client_disconnect increases but not 5xx. Opened internal incident watch in #incidents (INC-2025-11-18-017) pending more data.
2025-11-18 19:12 UTC (Dev Patel, Support) — Pulled traces for 3 provided request_ids. Pattern: gateway shows downstream connection closed by client; upstream to runtime continues for several seconds and completes token generation (tokens emitted but client not attached). This points away from runtime failure.

Working theory: client-side read timeout / abort controller triggered, or HTTP/2 stream handling regression in SDK 1.12.0 under concurrency.
2025-11-18 19:38 UTC (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Checked cluster health for zl-prod-ue1. No correlated saturation event. Runtime error rate stable. Gateway: slight bump in `stream_reset_by_peer` / `client_disconnect` but aligns with customer deployment window. Suggest focusing on SDK/client transport. If this becomes an incident, initial classification would be Streaming → Disconnect/Reset with subtype "Client/SDK" once confirmed.
2025-11-18 20:05 UTC (Customer - Zenlytics) — Provided details: Node 20.10, using custom http2 wrapper to reuse sessions; SDK 1.12.0 introduced a new streaming helper that wraps an AbortController with a default timeout (they did not set one explicitly). They see disconnects more frequently when streams are slow (longer responses).
2025-11-18 20:19 UTC (Dev Patel, Support) — Found likely regression: SDK 1.12.0 default `streamIdleTimeoutMs=20000` applied when using the helper, causing client abort if no token arrives within 20s. For long-form outputs with brief pauses, this triggers abort -> ECONNRESET. Asked customer to override timeout to 0 (disable) or increase to 120000ms and to test.

Proposed workaround:
- Set `stream_idle_timeout_ms: 120000` (or disable)
- Ensure keep-alive/agent is not closing idle HTTP/2 streams prematurely
- Validate no proxy idle timeout < 60s
2025-11-18 22:41 UTC (Customer - Zenlytics) — Confirmed workaround: increasing stream idle timeout to 120s reduced disconnects to <0.2% (baseline). Remaining failures correlate with their own egress proxy restarts. They will fully roll forward with updated config.
2025-11-19 00:03 UTC (Owen Phillips, Support) — Updated internal incident watch: not a platform incident; primary cause is client timeout default introduced in SDK 1.12.0 and customer proxy behavior. Closing INC-2025-11-18-017 as non-incident / customer-config induced. Linking this ticket for taxonomy training examples (client vs gateway vs runtime).
2025-11-19 16:27 UTC (Sofia Ivanova, Serving Runtime) — For completeness: reviewed runtime logs for referenced request_ids; generation completed successfully, no scheduler stalls. Confirms runtime is not the culprit.

Recommendation for taxonomy guidance: if runtime continues producing tokens and only downstream disconnects rise with an SDK deployment, prefer "Client/SDK" subtype and add gateway as a contributing system only if gateway limits are hit.
2025-11-21 10:14 UTC (Dev Patel, Support) — Added customer-facing summary and asked if they want an RCA note for internal sharing. Also recommended pinning SDK 1.11.x or applying config override until SDK patch release. Created internal follow-up task in SDK backlog to change default behavior + add migration note.
2025-11-22 09:02 UTC (Customer - Zenlytics) — Requested short write-up for their internal post-incident review. No further action required from Redwood; they are stable after config change.
2025-11-22 17:30 UTC (Owen Phillips, Support) — Closed ticket after delivering summary. Marking as taxonomy example: symptoms looked like "Streaming disconnect spike" but owner/root cause is customer SDK config/behavior (client) not gateway/runtime.
Root cause: SDK 1.12.0 streaming helper applied a default idle timeout (AbortController) that aborted streams when token emission paused, producing client-side ECONNRESET/stream closed errors. Customer also had an egress proxy with occasional restarts that contributed to residual disconnects.

Fix / workaround:
- Customer increased/disabled stream idle timeout (120s) and completed rollout.
- Internal follow-up: adjust SDK defaults and add explicit migration docs (not tracked in this Jira ticket).

Taxonomy note (for Reliability Program): If escalated as an incident prior to confirmation, initial classification may be "Streaming: Disconnect/Reset"; final classification should land under "Client/SDK regression or misconfig" once trace evidence shows gateway disconnect initiated by client while runtime completes generation.
We investigated the streaming disconnects that began immediately after the Redwood SDK upgrade. Traces show the platform continued generating output while the client connection was being closed from the downstream side. The issue was caused by a new default streaming idle timeout behavior in the upgraded SDK/stream helper (combined with your proxy behavior), which could abort streams during brief pauses in token emission. Increasing the idle timeout resolved the issue and brought disconnects back to baseline. We’re updating our SDK defaults and documentation to prevent this class of regression.

title: Timeboxed, dual-control debug snapshot and redaction run for suspected payments fraud - limited prod trace access
body:
Timeboxed, dual-control debug snapshot and redaction run for suspected payments fraud - limited prod trace access

Issue summary:
A payments integrity analyst flagged a pattern of malformed payment confirmation responses that may indicate a fraud pattern affecting a small subset of enterprise customers. We need a minimal, timeboxed debug snapshot from production traces (KV-cache / response slices) for targeted customer_ids to reproduce and triage the anomaly.

Impact:
- Potential incorrect billing + increased chargeback risk for ~7 customer accounts (estimated).
- Customer-facing reports show duplicated confirmations for a small percentage of requests in us-east region.

Environment:
- prod - us-east (primary gateway cluster serving payments)
- Affected service: serving-runtime -> response post-processing / payment confirmation handler

Requested scope and constraints (must be followed):
1) Minimality: only include request/response slices for the 7 scoped customer_ids and +/- 2 minutes around each event. No full-session replays.
2) Redaction: PII (card numbers, SSNs, full names, email addresses) must be auto-redacted by the standard redaction pipeline. If redaction fails for a field, mark record and do NOT include raw payload unless dual-control approval is granted.
3) Dual-control: Access provisioning requires two approvers: Security (Elena Morris) and Payments PM (Jordan Li). Both approvals required before decrypted payloads (if any) are accessible.
4) Timebox: Access window = 48 hours from grant. All extracted artifacts must be deleted and deletion attested in this ticket.
5) KMS constraints: If any payloads must be decrypted, decryption must be performed in the ephemeral forensic host with KMS audit logging and the operation must be recorded.

Steps to reproduce (ask analytics/SRE for traces):
- Query prod trace index for event_type=payment_confirmation and status in {duplicated, success} for customer_ids [redacted list attached to CS note].
- Pull KV-cache prefix entries for affected model routing keys (if present) for those time ranges.

title: Evening thread panic in runtime causes cascading API 5xx surge for one tenant
body:
Evening thread panic in runtime causes cascading API 5xx surge for one tenant

Issue summary: Around 18:20 UTC we observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses for requests routed to the us-east serving pool for a single dedicated tenant (LexiSearch). Impact: Customer saw ~60% error rate on chat/streaming requests and ~30% on embedding uploads for 18:20-18:55 UTC. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated capacity pool pinned to customer. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a mixed workload from LexiSearch that includes long-chat generation (>2k tokens) and bulk embedding upload concurrently. 2) Observe runtime worker thread crashes and subsequent 502/503 responses from API gateway. Logs & traces: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/dashboard/s/serve/tenant-us-east Lexi thread panic trace: logs-redwood://prod/us-east/runtime/worker-7/2026-03-10T18:22:31Z (see stack frames w/ tokenizer::segmenter::process). Slack thread: #support-lexisearch (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345/p164)
1) Use LexiSearch account to send a simultaneous streaming chat request (long prompt + function calls) and a bulk embedding upload of ~12k items.
2) Observe increased prefetch activity and repeated KV cache invalidations in serving-runtime logs.
3) Monitor API Gateway 5xx rate and runtime worker restarts during the burst.
Memory and GPU driver checks: NVML logs show transient GPU driver reset coincident with worker SIGABRT; GPU memory usage not at peak but post-reset fragmentation observed.
Stack traces point to tokenizer::segmenter::process -> tokenize_utf8_sequence -> std::vector resize in patched tokenizer library (new behavior introduced in runtime-hotpatch).
Prefetch/KV cache behaviour: Long streaming sessions caused frequent KV writes; combined with bulk embeddings, this created lock contention on kvcache shards causing coroutine queue growth and increased thread concurrency in runtime worker.
Amplification path: runtime thread panic leads to worker process crash -> Kubernetes restarts worker -> API gateway keeps retrying connections which temporarily increases connection churn and accept queue backlog -> additional 5xx from api-gateway while runtime pool recovers.
Correlation: error spike window matches customer activity (confirmed by customer logs and request-ids). No similar signals for other tenants in the same pool.
A recent runtime hotpatch updated the tokenizer library with an aggressive internal buffer resize which can trigger a stack corruption when combined with high concurrency on kvcache prefetch locks. The stack corruption produced thread-level panics and worker process SIGABRTs. Worker crash/restart churn amplified load at the API gateway (retries and accept queue saturation), producing the observed 5xx surge for the affected tenant.
1) Rolled back the runtime hotpatch to the previous stable tokenizer build (deployment rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789). 2) Applied temporary per-tenant ingress throttle for LexiSearch to prevent immediate re-flood during restarts. 3) Increased api-gateway accept_queue and provisional connection backoff to smooth retry amplification. 4) Performed rolling restarts of affected runtime shards and monitored NVML/GPU health. Result: error rate returned to baseline by 19:22 UTC.

Add a counter metric for tokenizer-exception-rate and alert when >0.1% for 5m in any tenant pool.
Improve per-tenant prewarm throttling policy to avoid single-tenant amplification on restarts.
Review the hotpatch rollout procedure: add a 1-hour low-traffic canary window when touching tokenizer/kernel codepaths.

OBS-Task: Add dashboard panel for tokenization error traces and a dedicated alert.

title: Unexpected duplicate tool executions after client-side multiplexed retry window with partial acks
body:
Unexpected duplicate tool executions after client-side multiplexed retry window with partial acks

Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports that when using the Go SDK with multiplexed streaming sessions they observe duplicate external tool executions (webhook posts) in a narrow race where the client triggers a retry during the server-side retry window. Impact:
- Duplicate downstream side effects (payment webhook charged twice) in ~0.8% of long-running sessions for one major flow.
- Billing discrepancies and customer-facing incorrect behavior.
Environment:
- SDK: redwood-go v0.12.3 (custom wrapper)
- Service: Hosted Redwood Dedicated pool (us-east-1)
- Model: redwood-13b-v1 pinned to v2026-02-26
- Traffic pattern: multiplexed client with two concurrent logical streams per connection, median request time 18s, tail 90s
Observed behavior:
1) Client sends request A invoking external tool (payment POST) and receives partial ack for call queued but connection is swapped (connection migration) at ~17s.
2) Client times out locally, then triggers an immediate retry on the multiplexed session.
3) Server retries the in-flight tool call (because it had queued it) AND the client retry causes the tool to be enqueued again for the retried request resulting in two webhook posts.
Expected behavior:
- Server-side deduplication or explicit tool-confirmation should prevent duplicate external tool invocation in this race.
Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start redwood-go client with multiplexing enabled and two logical streams per TCP connection.
2) Use a handler that triggers a synchronous external webhook call during model generation.
3) Simulate transient connection swap (tcp reset) at ~15-20s on in-flight stream A.
4) Immediately retry the request on the same multiplexed session.
5) Observe two webhook calls for a single logical action.
Logs/trace snippets (redacted):
- correlation-id: bc-prod-9f3d
- server request id: srv-20260312-5031
- webhook upstream: https://payments.brightcart.com/charge -> 2x POST bodies with identical payloads timestamped 18.042s and 18.129s
- client side: "stream: moved, retrying request" followed by "retry-sent: idempotency-token=blank"

Temporary workaround requested by customer: guidance on short-term mitigations (headers, retry backoff, SDK flags).
See description steps; customer provided a minimal repro that toggles multiplex=true and forces a connection swap. They used an internal script to send SIGPIPE to the socket after 15s.
server-log-excerpt: [2026-03-12T15:14:10Z] srv-20260312-5031 streamA queued tool POST -> outbound webhook payment id X123; [2026-03-12T15:14:27Z] connection migration detected; [2026-03-12T15:14:27Z] client retried logical streamA -> queued tool POST -> outbound webhook payment id X123 (second)
2026-03-12 - BrightCart-Support: We saw two charges for order 98765. Both webhook bodies identical. This wasn't reproducible on non-multiplexed config.
2026-03-12 - Support (Ava Patel): Thanks for the report — tagging Runtime and SDK teams. Can you share connection reset sequence and SDK version? Any idempotency token being sent?
2026-03-12 - BrightCart-Support: Using redwood-go v0.12.3, our wrapper strips idempotency headers for tool calls to reduce payload size (we didn't realize they'd be needed). We attached server logs. Repro is included.
2026-03-12 - Support (Luis Moreno): Reproduced locally with repro. Observed same double-enqueue when client retries immediately after reset and idempotency header absent. Raising to Runtime eng for dedup policy review.
2026-03-13 - Runtime Eng (Maya Chen): Observed that queued tool entries persist across connection handoff; dedupe map keyed by per-request ephemeral nonce was blank when client retried. Proposing server-side strong dedupe on (session-id, tool-hash) for a short TTL.
2026-03-13 - SDK Eng (Rajiv Kapoor): SDK change candidate: ensure SDK includes idempotency-token header for each tool request by default and preserve it across retries. Preparing PR for default behavior and docs update.
2026-03-13 - Support (Luis Moreno): Sent interim guidance to customer: enable `disable_multiplex=false` or add client-side deliberate 200ms jitter before immediate retry; both reduce duplicates pending fix.
Runtime logs show queued-tool entries survive connection swap because queue is per-worker, not per-connection.
Deduplication currently relies on client-supplied idempotency token; if missing, server treats each enqueue as unique.
Multiplexed sessions allow retries to reuse logical stream identifiers; client immediate retries currently do not re-use/forward original token in this customer's wrapper.
Hypothesis: two independent code paths enqueued the same payload: the original in-flight path and the retry path after client reconnect. Without token, server cannot collapse them.
Repro steps run in staging reproduces at ~0.7% of requests when artificial swap injected; higher with aggressive client retry logic.
Potential edge case: cleanup TTL for queued-tool dedupe map configured to 30s; race window may be shorter than cleanup frequency.
Workaround provided to customer on 2026-03-13: a) enable per-tool idempotency tokens in their wrapper; b) add 150-300ms backoff before immediate retry; c) disable multiplexing as a short-term mitigation.
Engineering action items: (1) SDK: default to attaching idempotency-token header for tool calls and preserve it across retries (PR prepared by Rajiv K). (2) Runtime: implement server-side short-term dedupe by (session-id || request-hash) with a 60s TTL to collapse duplicate enqueues when token absent (proposal by Maya C). (3) Docs: add best-practice guidance for long-running tool calls under multiplexing with examples for Go/TS/Python (tracked in GH issue).
Planned rollout: SDK change staged in next minor release (v0.12.4) after review; runtime dedupe gated behind config flag for dedicated pools and will be rolled out to us-east-1 in canary first.
Follow-up: After SDK patch deployed, ask BrightCart to re-run repro and confirm no duplicates. If duplicates persist, collect full traces and reopen.

title: Runbook elevation session orphaned after IdP audience rotation between edge proxies
body:
Runbook elevation session orphaned after IdP audience rotation between edge proxies

Issue summary: Multiple oncall users report being unable to complete temporary runbook elevation flows. After approving elevation in the identity provider (Okta), the support console shows the runbook approval as pending and the user's temporary session is not attached to the elevated role. Impact: Oncall engineers cannot execute emergency runbooks for ~15% of elevation attempts in us-west region; blocking critical incident mitigation. Timeline: 2026-03-12 08:03 UTC first report from #oncall, 2026-03-12 08:10 SRE triage, 2026-03-12 09:00 reproduced in-house. Observed behaviour: SAML assertion from IdP has a rotated audience claim (auth-edge-2) while the identity-proxy expects auth-edge-1; the session-binding cookie is set for the proxy that does not match the runbook service's session aggregator, leaving an orphaned ephemeral token.

Important context: We rolled an IdP certificate rotation and passive audience update earlier in the morning (related change: PR #12345). Edge proxies are deployed in pairs; routing during the rotation caused some assertions to be signed with the new audience before the proxy routing table was fully updated.
1) Trigger JIT elevation flow from support console as normal user
2) Approve elevation in Okta via the approval UI
3) Observe SAML assertion in network trace: audience claim set to auth-edge-2 while proxy aggregator uses auth-edge-1
4) Support console remains at 'Pending', runbook action buttons disabled, user does not receive elevated role claims

title: Provision auditable external-vendor onboarding workflow: Slack guest channels, Confluence evidence bridge, and timebound approvals
body:
Provision auditable external-vendor onboarding workflow: Slack guest channels, Confluence evidence bridge, and timebound approvals

Issue summary: Request to provision a reusable, auditable onboarding workflow for third-party vendors and contractors that combines timebound Slack guest channels, automated transcript capture to Confluence (evidence bridge), and a lightweight Jira approval microflow.

Impact: Currently vendor onboarding is ad-hoc: teams create guest channels and store notes in project spaces with inconsistent retention and no single evidence trail for audits. This increases risk during compliance reviews and makes forensic reconstruction of access/activity difficult.

Request: Build and deploy an opinionated template and automation that any pod can request via a Jira form. The automation should: 1) create a tenant-scoped Confluence space (audit namespace) populated with a vendor onboarding checklist; 2) provision a Slack guest channel with timebound membership (TTL) and a small guest bot that posts onboarding checklist items; 3) capture the full Slack transcript at deprovision time and attach it to the Confluence evidence page; 4) create a Jira approval task for Security and the Requesting Team with configurable SLAs; 5) emit structured metadata (owner, vendor name, access window, artifacts links) back to the original Jira issue.

Requirements and constraints: - Evidence artifacts must be immutable (Confluence page with view-only history) and linked to the Jira request. - Access TTL should be adjustable via the Jira form but default to 14 days. - Approvals flow must require Security sign-off for vendors with outbound network access. - All actions must be logged and traceable (who provisioned, timestamps). - Sensitive PII must not be stored in Confluence; automation must scrub any detected email/SSN patterns in transcripts before storing, and flag for manual review.

Proposed flow (high level): 1) Requester opens a templated Jira request with vendor metadata and requested duration. 2) Automation creates a Confluence evidence page from template and a Slack guest channel (private) via service account. 3) Automation creates a Jira subtask assigned to Security and notifies the on-call via #security-approvals. 4) Upon Security approval, automation adds guests (email invites) to Slack and posts onboarding checklist. 5) During access window, requesters can extend via the Jira issue; extensions spawn a brief approval. 6) At TTL expiry or manual close, automation exports Slack transcript, scrubs PII patterns, attaches the export to the Confluence evidence page, and archives the Slack channel. 7) Automation closes the Jira request with structured metadata and retention tags.

Acceptance criteria: - Template Jira request available to all pods in the Internal Tools category. - Automation successfully creates Confluence page and Slack channel in 95% of test runs. - Transcript capture to Confluence preserves message timestamps and poster handles and is scrubbed for PII. - Security approval step is enforced for high-risk vendors. - Logs include provisioning events and final artifact links.

Security considerations: - Use tenant-scoped service principals and least-privilege Slack bot token; rotate tokens regularly. - Confluence evidence pages should be created under a central audit space with restricted edit permissions. - Automation must surface any potential PII matches to Security for manual review.

Test plan: - QA team will provision three test vendor flows: low, medium, high risk. - Verify TTL enforcement, transcript capture, scrub behavior, and approval gating. - Pen test and access review for service account tokens.

Rollout plan: - Pilot with two non-sensitive pods for two weeks. - Iterate on scrub heuristics and timeouts. - After pilot, enable self-serve for all pods and publish runbook.

Owner team: Internal Tools - Admin Automation.

Estimated completion: 2026-03-24

title: Control-plane SRV/DNS lookups return NXDOMAIN due to customer connmark mangle rewrite on private deploy
body:
Control-plane SRV/DNS lookups return NXDOMAIN due to customer connmark mangle rewrite on private deploy

Issue summary: After an on-prem gateway firewall update at Kepler Analytics, Redwood control-plane SRV DNS queries for serving node discovery intermittently return NXDOMAIN. Impact: control-plane reports unhealthy for several serving nodes, causing model pulls to fail and client requests to fallback to lower-capacity regions.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed gateway), prod us-east-1 region, multiple AZs. Timeline: 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC — customer upgraded iptables connmark mangle chain; 08:26 UTC — control plane alarms for service discovery failures; 08:35 UTC — customer opened support ticket.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From customer gateway, run tcpdump on egress interface targeting destination control-plane SRV record resolution (UDP/TCP 53).
2) Observe incoming DNS responses with source IP rewritten and response RCODE=0 but answer section stripped, or RCODE=3 NXDOMAIN responses returned to control-plane.
3) Reproduce by creating synthetic SRV lookup workload from serving node in customer's VPC (nslookup -query=SRV ...).

Observed behavior: DNS responses are being rewritten by netfilter mangle CONNMARK and NAT order changes; control-plane sees response matching a different 5-tuple and drops the UDP response or treats it as NXDOMAIN during SRV parsing. Symptoms include: control-plane SRV backoff, repeated cache miss, serving node fallback.

Expected behavior: Normal SRV resolution succeeds; no path-altering connmark should modify DNS 5-tuple or fragments used by control-plane for service discovery.

Logs and traces (excerpts):
- tcpdump (serving node): "22:08:26.123456 IP 10.0.5.22.53 > 10.10.8.12.54321: 1 q: _redwood-control._tcp.example.com PTR?" followed by truncated answer.
- kernel conntrack: "nf_conntrack: table full?" not observed but connmark values present: 0x200/0xFFF modified by mangle chain.
- control-plane agent log: "srv_lookup: parse_error: unexpected empty-answer (rcode=0)" and later "srv_lookup: fallback to az-b".

Customer-provided iptables-save snapshot (sanitized):
*raw
:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A PREROUTING -p udp --dport 53 -j MARK --set-xmark 0x200/0xffffffff
COMMIT

Hypothesis: The customer's mangle/CONNMARK rules mark DNS packets and a downstream NAT rule uses that mark to change source port/address for egress. Because of NAT/mangle ordering and ephemeral port changes, control-plane's UDP socket expects the original 5-tuple and either discards the reply or the reply gets rewritten into a form that the user-space DNS parsing treats as NXDOMAIN/empty answer.

Customer impact: Some serving nodes in us-east experienced control-plane disconnects leading to degraded throughput and increased tail latency for a subset of model calls. Total affected nodes: ~6 of 24 in cluster. Duration: ~2 hours until workaround applied.
Support triage (Maya P.) 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Collected tcpdump and iptables-save. Verified correlation with gateway change. Noted mangle mark applied to UDP/53. SRE (Liam O.) 2026-03-10 10:10 UTC: Reproduced in staging by injecting connmark and NAT rewrite; observed control-plane SRV resolution failures identical to prod traces. Ran netfilter debug and echoed connmark values. Confirmed that when connmark-based SNAT alters source port, control-plane UDP socket read returns truncated/invalid payload resulting in 'empty-answer' parse path.

Mitigation testing: Cleared connmark on DNS flows via iptables rule (iptables -t mangle -I PREROUTING 1 -p udp --dport 53 -j CONNMARK --restore-mark --set-mark 0) -> control-plane SRV lookups started succeeding in test environment. Also validated that changing NAT to operate before mangle prevented the translation mismatch.

Related artifacts: pcap files uploaded to support bucket (s3://redwood-support/supp-731820/pcaps/). Kernel debug output and iptables snapshot attached in ticket.
Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Initial report received from Kepler Analytics. They rolled a gateway change at 08:12 UTC and started seeing control-plane failures. Requested tcpdump + iptables-save.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10 10:18 UTC: Reproduced locally using connmark+mangle. Suspect NAT ordering issue. Created quick test harness to emulate marking+snat behavior.
Kepler Analytics (Ops) 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC: We can apply a temporary iptables rule to clear marks on DNS flows. Please confirm the exact command and risk.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10 11:22 UTC: Recommended temporary workaround: iptables -t mangle -I PREROUTING 1 -p udp --dport 53 -j CONNMARK --restore-mark --set-mark 0 ; and ensure SNAT uses original conntrack tuple for DNS. Risk is low; change limited to DNS flows.
Kepler Analytics (Ops) 2026-03-10 11:38 UTC: Applied workaround and control-plane SRV lookups recovered by 11:41 UTC. They report traffic normalized and tail-latency reduced.
Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 15:02 UTC: Followed up to confirm customer implemented permanent fix. Kepler changed gateway rule to exempt UDP/53 from mangle marking and adjusted NAT ordering. Monitoring shows no recurrence.
Customer firewall update introduced connmark-based mangle rules that altered DNS packet 5-tuples prior to NAT in a way that broke control-plane SRV response correlation, resulting in perceived NXDOMAIN/empty-answer behavior.
Temporary workaround: Applied CONNMARK clear rule on PREROUTING limited to udp dport 53 to restore normal replies. Permanent fix: Kepler Ops removed DNS flows from mangle-marking and reordered NAT so SNAT occurs before mangle/connmark usage, ensuring control-plane sees consistent 5-tuples. Confirmed recovery and removal of support monitoring after 48h of clean metrics.
Customer runbook update: document exclusion of DNS ports from connmark mangle rules
SRE: add anomaly detection for high SRV NXDOMAIN rates per region
Docs: update private-deploy networking checklist to call out connmark/mangle interactions
No code change required on Redwood side; worked with customer network team for configuration change.
Escalation: Notified platform-networking lead (Angela Ruiz) during incident window.

title: SSE session offset drift after VPN path migration causes duplicate mid-paragraph fragments and missing end marker on reconnect
body:
SSE session offset drift after VPN path migration causes duplicate mid-paragraph fragments and missing end marker on reconnect

Issue summary: Customer reports repeated partial paragraph fragments and missing final end-marker when resuming SSE streams after a corporate VPN (split-tunnel) path migration. Impact: Multiple generation outputs are duplicated mid-paragraph and sometimes the final JSON/terminal marker is not received by the client, causing downstream parsers to hang. Occurs intermittently during mobile/workstation VPN re-route or NAT rebinding events. First reported by FinGrid on 2026-03-09 14:20 UTC.
1) Start a long-running SSE generation request from FinGrid client behind corporate split-tunnel VPN.
2) Trigger network path change (disconnect/reconnect VPN or move machine to external network) while stream is active.
3) Client reconnects and attempts to resume the SSE session using existing session token/cookie and resume offset header.
4) Observe duplicated mid-paragraph fragments and/or missing closing event (no 'end' marker).
client-log: conn=abcd1234, resume_offset=23174, observed_duplicate_fragment='...the transaction will be processed' repeated
edge-proxy: session_id=fg-9987, NAT_rebind=true, client_ip=10.1.5.23->54.210.12.8, resume_offset=23174 forwarded
serving-runtime: resume_validation: expected_offset=23180, incoming_offset=23174, kv_cache_lookup=miss -> partial replay applied
auth: sso-cookie-rotate at 2026-03-09T14:21:03Z for user=finops@fingrid.com
(Support) 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Acknowledged receipt. We need network traces from the customer and the client-side SSE raw stream to confirm the offset negotiation behavior.
(Customer) 2026-03-10 - FinGrid Ops (J. Morgan): Attached pcap and client raw events. Happens ~15% of reconnects during VPN re-routes. Parser downstream fails on ~40% of affected requests.
(SRE) 2026-03-11 - Miguel Alvarez: Reproduced locally by simulating NAT rebind and resume header mismatch. Observed server applied delta-replay that overlapped by 6 tokens, causing duplicated text. Missing end marker appears when edge LB drops final keepalive event during handoff.
(Support) 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Temporary mitigation suggested - client should fully close and re-open a new stream when moving networks. Customer confirms acceptable as short-term workaround.
(Eng) 2026-03-13 - Priya Desai: Patch ready that adds a tolerance compare on resume offsets and forces explicit reconciliation of KV cache by client id. Deploying to canary this evening.
Hypothesis 1: NAT port rebind combined with SSO cookie rotation results in the client being associated with a different edge session id; resume offset forwarded to a different serving worker whose KV cache is offset by a few tokens -> duplicate fragments.
Hypothesis 2: Edge LB handoff drop can remove the final 'end' keepalive/control event while the client assumes stream continues, leaving client awaiting terminal marker.
Repro steps validated in staging with netem causing path migration and auth cookie refresh - duplicate fragments reproduced consistently when resume_offset < worker_expected_offset.
KV-cache mismatch trace: serving-runtime returned 'partial-replay' path that concatenated overlapping tokens instead of de-duplicating overlap region.
Observed correlation with longer-lived streams (>45s) and enterprises using split-tunnel VPNs.
Mitigation (short-term): Advise customers to close and re-open stream on network change. Support provided a client SDK snippet that falls back to full reconnect when NAT or IP change detected.
Fix (deployed 2026-03-13): Canary edge patch adds resume-offset tolerance logic: if incoming_offset <= expected_offset && overlap <= 12 tokens, trim overlap on server side rather than replaying. Also added explicit final-event ack forwarding during LB handoff.
Follow-up: Roll out patch to all edge regions on 2026-03-14 with monitoring dashboard for 'resume_overlap' metric. Create runbook entry describing detection and manual mitigation steps.
Customer follow-up: FinGrid validated canary and sees reduction of duplicates from ~15% to <1% on test cohort. They will schedule wider validation next week.

title: Ephemeral allocator latency from sparse tenant spinups causing transient P99 throughput regression
body:
Ephemeral allocator latency from sparse tenant spinups causing transient P99 throughput regression

Issue summary:
Customer Acme Cloud observed a sudden and repeatable p99 throughput regression on their dedicated pool during midday windows. The dips correlate with waves of short-lived tenant spinups (many 5–30s streams) after a marketing campaign. Impact: sustained ~30% drop in batch throughput and elevated queueing for ~3-6 minutes per wave.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference latency spikes and degraded SLAs for batch-heavy endpoints
- Autoscaler temporarily failed to instrument capacity (delayed upscales) leading to request queueing and budgeted fallback model routing

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (Acme Cloud reserve), prod, us-west-2
- Mix of models (13B, 7B) with batching enabled and prefix-KV cache warmups

Observation summary:
Metrics show short bursts of many short streams that cause the allocator to take ~200-700ms stalls when assigning slots; these stalls accumulate, causing batchers to miss assembly windows and p99 throughput falls. NVME/io and GPU memory not saturated; traces point to allocator RPC latency and a spin-lock path in the GPU-allocator daemon that scales poorly for high churn of ephemeral connections.
Simulate 1,200 short-lived streams (5-30s) across 100 tenants over 60 seconds targeting dedicated pool slot-prefetch route
Observe allocator pod logs and batcher assembly p99 in Grafana (dashboard: dedicated/pool/slot-alloc)
Reproduce locally on staging with same concurrency and confirm slot-assignment latency spike
11:40 - Initial triage: ruled out NVIDIA driver or GPU OOM; GPU metrics steady, memory headroom present.
12:05 - Hypothesis A: autoscaler metrics pipeline lag causes delayed node adds. Counter-evidence: nodes were added but slot allocator still stalling.
12:30 - Hypothesis B: allocator contention under connection churn. Recreated in staging with synthetic short streams; observed identical slot_assign RPC latency spikes.
12:55 - Found allocator thread stack trace showing a lock held during connection tear-down code path (prefetch cancel path). Suspect contention between prefetch cancellation and new assignment operations.
13:15 - Discovered increased goroutine counts in allocator pods correlated with each wave; GC/pause times negligible but mutex contention high.
13:45 - Quick mitigation tested: bumping allocator pod replicas from 3 -> 6 reduced per-pod in-flight RPC and brought p99 throughput back to baseline under same load in staging.
14:10 - Further hypothesis: short-lived streams cause many simultaneous prefetch cancellations which invoke a cleanup routine that takes a lock over shared slot-index. Need code-level fix to narrow lock scope.
Links: Grafana (dedicated/pool/slot-alloc): https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/slot-alloc, Slack thread: #support-acme (https://slack.com/archives/C0123456)
Related investigation: see SUP-271400 for prefetch-related throughput anomalies (similar cancellation path implicated).
2026-03-13T11:34:12Z allocator[pid=1294]: slot_assign_start tenant=acct-ACME shard=3 request_id=...
2026-03-13T11:34:12Z allocator[pid=1294]: rpc_latency=0.62s peer=allocator-2 (count=14 in-flight)
2026-03-13T11:34:13Z batcher[pid=2201]: assemble_missed window=50ms reason=slot-delay p99=0.67s
Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-13: Customer reported first occurrence at 11:30 PDT after email campaign. They are seeing p99 increases and multiple model fallbacks. Asking for urgent triage.
Riley Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Triage started. Running synthetic load to reproduce; initial signs point to allocator RPC queuing. Putting alloc pods into debug mode to capture stacks.
Mateo Alvarez (Infra Eng) - 2026-03-13: Confirmed high mutex wait times in allocator at peak. Recommending temporary scale of allocator replicas as mitigation while we prepare a patch.
Riley Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Scaled allocator replicas 3->6 in prod dedicated pool for Acme (change id: infra/scale/ACL-881). Observed throughput recovery within two waves. Customer notified of workaround.
Priya Raman (Allocator Owner) - 2026-03-14: Root cause narrowed to prefetch cancel path holding global slot-index lock. Preparing PR to replace coarse lock with per-shard lock; will run canary on staging.
Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-14: Customer acknowledges temporary improvement but requests ETA on permanent fix and asks for retro on how to avoid future recurrence during campaigns.
Workaround applied: scaled allocator replicas from 3 to 6 for the affected dedicated pool (action id infra/scale/ACL-881). This reduced per-pod in-flight RPC and mitigated p99 throughput regressions for the observed waves. Root cause: allocator global lock contention in prefetch cancel code path under high churn of short-lived streams. Permanent fix: replace coarse global lock with per-shard locking and refactor cleanup to be non-blocking; patch PR opened and under code review (github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/912).
Deploy PR with per-shard locks to canary staging and run synthetic churn test (owner: Priya Raman, due: 2026-03-18)
Add autoscale rule to proactively add allocator capacity when short-stream connection churn > 500/s (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due: 2026-03-20)
Postmortem draft in Confluence and customer-facing RCA to be prepared (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-19)
Add targeted alerting for allocator mutex contention and per-pod goroutine growth (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-16)
Customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-15 10:00 PDT (calendar invite sent)

title: Intermittent console 504 / aborted uploads: gRPC-web upload stream resets behind customer ADC that coalesces HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
body:
Intermittent console 504 / aborted uploads: gRPC-web upload stream resets behind customer ADC that coalesces HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames

Customers report 504s from Redwood Console when uploading large prompt bundles (~30–120MB). Failures only occur for users routing through their corporate ADC (F5/Big-IP) that applies TCP optimizations. Browser shows gRPC-web stream reset / PROTOCOL_ERROR; server-side logs show aborted streams and SETTINGS frame sequence anomalies.
Issue summary: Intermittent upload failures and 504s observed in Redwood Console for a Private deployment. Failures reproduce only when the user's traffic flows through their on-prem ADC which performs HTTP/2/TCP optimizations. Impact: uploads fail to complete, leading to customer inability to persist prompt datasets and occasional console timeouts; affects a subset of users behind the ADC, not all tenants.
Multiple engineering users at Nimbus Security cannot upload prompt bundles via Console; some retry loops create duplicate upload attempts and token churn. Estimated 10–20% of uploads from within the corporate network fail during nightly ingestion batches.
Private deployment (customer-managed VPC, VPCE to Redwood control plane). Customer frontends traffic through an on-prem F5 BIG-IP ADC which terminates TLS and proxies upstream to the VPCE. ADC configured with HTTP/2 multiplexing, TCP coalescing, and an application profile that rewrites some SETTINGS behavior to minimize handshake RTTs.
1) Login to Redwood Console from a client inside Nimbus Security network.
2) Start a large prompt bundle upload (~30–120MB) via the Console 'Dataset > Upload' flow (uses gRPC-web over HTTP/2).
3) Observe upload progress; in failing cases upload stalls and Console eventually shows a 504 or 'Upload failed: stream reset'.
4) Reproduce is consistent when client is on the corp network and routing through ADC; bypassing the ADC (direct internet or mobile tether) completes upload successfully.
5) Packet captures and ADC access logs were captured by the customer and attached below.
gRPC-web stream resets mid-upload, Console logs show 'STREAM_RESET' or 'PROTOCOL_ERROR'. Server logs report aborted streams, and HTTP/2 trace shows SETTINGS frames arriving out of expected order or with coalesced payloads. ADC logs show an optimization labeled 'http2-settings-coalesce' and TCP coalescing across small writes.
Uploads should complete without stream resets; HTTP/2 SETTINGS and WINDOW_UPDATE frames should arrive intact and in-order so the gRPC runtime can maintain the stream. Console should return success and persist the dataset.
Customer-provided tcpdump (snippet): frame 12345: TLS record: Handshake
    frame 12346: HTTP/2 SETTINGS (initial)
    frame 12348: HTTP/2 SETTINGS (ack) coalesced-with WINDOW_UPDATE
    frame 12350: DATA (partial) -> stream reset
ADC syslog excerpt: Mar 10 10:12:34 bigip1 INFO http2:settings-coalesce enabled profile=low-latency; coalesced_frames=12
Console client error (browser console): gRPC-Web: transport error; code=2; message=Stream reset (code=PROTOCOL_ERROR)
Server side trace id: trace-redwood-98231 (attached request ids across aborted uploads)
Customer-provided ADC config excerpt (redacted): http2 profile with 'coalesce-settings' and 'tcp-latency-opt' enabled
2026-03-10 15:00 - Ethan Park: Triaging; reproduced a failing upload when routing through customer's VPN endpoint (confirmed success from mobile tether).
2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE: Captured server-side HTTP/2 frame trace. Observed SETTINGS frames grouped and a WINDOW_UPDATE inserted before SETTINGS_ACK which triggers our gRPC runtime to treat the stream as out-of-order leading to PROTOCOL_ERROR.
2026-03-10 17:45 - Eng: Reviewed gRPC-web client behavior; client library expects SETTINGS/ACK handshake before application DATA on a new stream. ADC coalescing merges control frames and packets such that ordering is not preserved from server perspective.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Support: Requested customer to temporarily disable 'http2 settings coalesce' and 'tcp-latency-opt' on ADC; they agreed to test during a maintenance window.
2026-03-11 14:05 - Customer: Re-tested with optimizations disabled; upload success rate returned to baseline. ADC vendor notes indicate an optional patch that alters SETTINGS handling for legacy backend stacks.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Eng: Determined a safe client-side retry/backoff change can make uploads more robust to short control-frame reordering, but fix is non-trivial and may mask real protocol violations.
2026-03-10 - Maya S: Acknowledged receipt and requested tcpdump + ADC config. Asked for maintenance window to test config changes.
2026-03-11 - Maya S: Coordinated maintenance window 2026-03-11 13:00–15:00 ET with customer network team.
2026-03-11 - Customer (Nimbus): Disabled 'http2-settings-coalesce' during window and reported successful uploads. Customer will engage ADC vendor for a permanent patch.
2026-03-12 - Ethan P: Provided recommended mitigations and a temporary console-side workaround (retry on PROTOCOL_ERROR for uploads up to 2x with exponential backoff).
On-prem ADC is rewriting/coalescing HTTP/2 control frames (SETTINGS/ACK/WINDOW_UPDATE) and delivering them to the backend in a combined TCP segment. The gRPC-web client and our HTTP/2 stack interpret the reordered/coalesced frames as a protocol error, leading to stream resets. Bypassing ADC shows success, disabling coalescing in ADC resolves the issue.
1) Ask customer to disable 'http2-settings-coalesce' and any TCP coalescing/latency optimizations on their ADC for paths to the VPCE.
2) If disabling is not possible, recommend bypassing ADC for uploads (split upload endpoint via direct egress subnet) during their migration window.
3) Console-side: implement a guarded retry for uploads that fail with PROTOCOL_ERROR (limited retries to avoid duplication).
- Engineering to evaluate robust handling of unexpected control-frame ordering in the HTTP/2 stack; prototype safe retry/backoff logic for gRPC-web uploads (Q2 work item).
- Docs: Add ADC/ADC-profile guidance to Private deploy runbook (confluence page) describing HTTP/2 profiles known to break gRPC-web.
- Support: Add a diagnostic check to onboarding checklist that flags 'http2-settings-coalesce' or similar ADC optimizations.
- Follow-up with customer: Confirm ADC vendor patch schedule and re-open if patch doesn't remediate.
- Add unit test in runtime to simulate SETTINGS coalescing to observe client behavior.
In Progress - temporary mitigation verified. Customer disabled ADC coalescing and reported upload success during maintenance window. Engineering to scope a resilient client-side mitigation and add runbook guidance. Pending verification after customer's vendor patch.
1) Eng to produce a small RFC for safe upload retry behavior and run it by security/rate-limiting teams (owner: Lara Chen, due 2026-03-19).
2) Support to update onboarding checklist and confluence guidance (owner: Maya Singh, due 2026-03-16).
3) Customer to confirm ADC vendor patch and provide test date; Support to revalidate.
4) Keep ticket open until customer's patched ADC validated in prod for 48h of normal ingestion cycles.

title: EmberSearch (Dedicated): Dedicated pool upgrades need phased rollout with objective gates + fast rollback
body:
EmberSearch (Dedicated): Dedicated pool upgrades need phased rollout with objective gates + fast rollback

Account: EmberSearch (Dedicated)
Primary contacts: (via TAM) Head of Platform Eng + oncall rotation

Issue summary
Customer is requesting a safer, deterministic process for Dedicated pool upgrades (model version/runtime build/routing policy changes) using phased/staged rollouts with measurable gates and quick rollback. They explicitly do not want “big bang” pool flips.

Why this is urgent / escalation context
- EmberSearch runs embeddings + reranking traffic with strict latency SLOs and spiky batch workloads.
- They experienced customer-visible impact during the last 2 Dedicated pool upgrades.
- They have internal change management requirements (platform sign-off) and want a documented, auditable process.

Impact history (customer-reported)
1) 2024-12-11 (us-east): pool upgrade caused p99 latency to jump ~2.5x for ~25–35 minutes after cutover; intermittent 5xx; rollback required.
2) 2025-01-17 (multi-region): partial upgrade (us-east first, eu-west later) caused uneven routing and elevated 429s; they saw request drops during peak traffic. Customer’s take: “We couldn’t tell if this was capacity, routing, or the new build; we had no gating data and no safe ‘pause’ button.”

Customer request (what they want)
They are asking Redwood to provide (or document as an interim) a staged rollout workflow for a single Dedicated pool:
- Default stages: 1% → 10% → 50% → 100% (or replica partitions for small pools)
- Minimum time in stage: configurable (they suggested 30–60 minutes)
- Gate evaluation before promotion, with clear pass/fail reasoning
- Ability to HOLD (pause) a rollout and keep traffic pinned to the last good stage
- Fast abort/rollback that reverts routing immediately (with clarity on what happens to in-flight streams)
- Audit trail of actions (who promoted/overrode/aborted, reason, timestamps)

Desired gating metrics (customer-proposed)
Customer specifically asked for objective gates, visible in Console or exportable:
1) Error rate: 5xx + timeouts (HTTP and upstream), broken out by region and stage
2) Throttling: 429 rate and queue-depth / saturation indicators (they suspect last issue was capacity starvation)
3) Latency: p95 + p99 end-to-end, and (if possible) server-side tokenization/compute breakdown
4) GPU health: unhealthy nodes, ECC errors, throttling, GPU resets
5) OOM / memory pressure: OOM kill count, KV cache eviction pressure (if applicable)
6) Headroom: utilization/saturation gate to ensure the canary partition isn’t under-provisioned
7) (Nice-to-have) Quality regression checks: simple eval/prompt set or embedding drift sanity checks, at least for major version upgrades

Environment details
- Dedicated pool: ES-embed-prod (multi-region us-east + eu-west)
- Traffic pattern: spiky batch (indexing) + steady online traffic
- Peak QPS: customer reports 2–4x within 5 minutes during their indexing windows

Asks from Redwood (support request)
- Provide a near-term, operator-led staged upgrade procedure we can run for their next upgrade (even if manual gating).
- Provide a timeline/commitment for first-class “staged rollouts for Dedicated pools” so they can plan.
- Identify whether we can support replica-based stages when the pool is small (to avoid capacity fragmentation).

Internal notes / triage
This request aligns with the ongoing Dedicated staged rollouts project (rollout plans + stage gates + promote/abort/hold + audit logging + Console timeline). Customer is a strong candidate for design partner / beta.

Next scheduled customer touchpoint
- 2025-02-06: technical deep dive requested (TAM + SRE + Product) to walk through proposed stages, gate signals, and rollback semantics.
2025-01-29 09:12 PT - Liam O'Rourke (TAM): Logging per EmberSearch escalation. They want staged upgrades with gating + rollback. Last upgrade was painful and they’re requesting commitments before next quarterly upgrade window.
2025-01-29 10:03 PT - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please pull concrete timestamps from the 2025-01-17 event. If it’s the same pattern as the early beta 429 issue, likely capacity partitioning/routing interaction. We should avoid manual “split pool in half” procedures without clear headroom rules.
2025-01-29 10:41 PT - Lauren Bishop (PM, Dedicated): This matches what we’re building (Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools). I can join customer call and position MVP: manual gates first, then automated gate evaluation + Console evidence panel.
2025-01-29 12:18 PT - Allison Grant (Observability): If we commit to gating, we need stage-tagged metrics with strict cardinality controls. We can provide a limited set of standard queries for latency/error/429/saturation and show them in Console as evidence.
2025-01-30 08:57 PT - Mina Haddad (Routing): Multi-region pools complicate partial upgrades. We should be explicit: stage applies per-region partition but promotion should be coordinated. Also define behavior if a region is impaired mid-stage (hold vs abort).
2025-01-31 14:22 PT - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Gate proposals should be tied to their SLO and error budget burn. We should also include a ‘no promote during incident/high burn’ rule. Missing metrics should fail-closed with manual override, otherwise we’ll ship a footgun.
2025-02-03 11:06 PT - Liam O'Rourke (TAM): Customer provided desired thresholds (informal): 5xx < 0.2%, p99 < 900ms, 429 < 0.5% during canary; wants 30m windows and ability to extend. They’re okay with Redwood-defined defaults as long as they can see what we’re evaluating and why we blocked a promote.
2025-02-06 13:35 PT - Lauren Bishop (PM, Dedicated): Completed technical deep dive with customer. We aligned on default stages (1/10/50/100) and documented HOLD + ABORT semantics. Action: we’ll enroll EmberSearch in limited beta once feature flag is available; interim workaround is operator-run canary using a separate shadow pool only for batch indexing traffic (not ideal).
2025-02-07 09:28 PT - Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Beta enablement will be behind feature flag; we can target a controlled enablement for 1–2 accounts after migrations. Please file an internal enablement request when ready (INT ticket).
2025-02-10 15:04 PT - Lauren Bishop (PM, Dedicated): Creating Product escalation notes: customer needs gate evidence visible in Console (not just internal dashboards) and audit trail export. Also requesting replica-based stages for small pools to avoid 429s from partition starvation.
2025-02-11 10:26 PT - Liam O'Rourke (TAM): Filed internal request to enable staged rollouts beta once available (linked INT-1933). Customer agrees to be design partner; wants a written runbook and a ‘go/no-go’ checklist for each promotion.
2025-02-12 16:50 PT - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Added EmberSearch to candidate list for beta with SRE monitoring plan. Recommendation: start with manual gates + strict hold/abort; do not allow auto-promote for first rollout. Ensure headroom validation (min replicas) to avoid a repeat of the 429 issue.
Resolved as product/enablement path: Confirmed alignment with Dedicated staged rollouts project. Customer accepted interim operator-led canary workaround for next upgrade window and agreed to join limited beta. Internal enablement tracking moved to INT-1933; follow-on capacity starvation investigation tracked separately (see SUP-28522 for early beta 429 behavior reference).

title: Verify vendor payee name vs bank metadata before scheduled payout (NordPoint Shipping GmbH)
body:
Verify vendor payee name vs bank metadata before scheduled payout (NordPoint Shipping GmbH)

Issue summary: A scheduled payout for vendor 'NordPoint Shipping GmbH' was flagged by the bank on payout day due to a payee name mismatch and IBAN formatting concerns. Treasury put the transaction on hold to avoid rejection. Impact: vendor payment delayed, potential late-fee exposure and vendor escalation to Partnerships. This ticket coordinates AP, Treasury, and Vendor Ops to validate identity and release the payment.
1) Vendor submitted invoice INV-2026-334 via vendor portal on 2026-03-05 with payee 'NordPoint Shipping' (no legal suffix).
2) AP approved invoice and created a scheduled payrun for 2026-03-12 through NetSuite/Payments service.
3) Treasury submitted ACH/SEPA instruction to bank for execution; bank returned a reject/hold citing 'payee name does not match beneficiary records' and flagged IBAN formatting (extra non-ASCII characters).
4) Treasury placed payrun on hold, notified AP and Vendor Ops; vendor opened an escalation thread in #vendor-ops on Slack.

Vendor portal submission metadata: vendor_profile_id=VND-9082; payee_display='NordPoint Shipping'; attached_business_registry='Hand-signed PDF, company name: NordPoint Shipping GmbH'
Finance/Payments review (Markus): Vendor profile payee_display lacks legal suffix 'GmbH' while registry doc includes it. NetSuite vendor record payee_name='NordPoint Shipping' (legacy entry from 2024 onboarding).
Treasury checked the SWIFT/IBAN lookup: IBAN provided 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00' contains a non-standard invisible character when copy-pasted from the PDF (U+200B). Bank parser flagged formatting and normalized copy failed.

Risk assessment: If released without name alignment, bank may reject leading to chargebacks and manual correction windows; keeping on hold is recommended until name/IBAN are confirmed.

Add alert to operations dashboard to flag 'payrun holds' with high frequency over a 24-hour window (owner: SRE/Observability, runbook link added below)

title: Provision incident-playbook Slack channel templates and automate Confluence runbook sync for cross-org infra alerts
body:
Provision incident-playbook Slack channel templates and automate Confluence runbook sync for cross-org infra alerts

Background:
- On-call teams across infra, serving-runtime, and platform have ad-hoc Slack channels for incidents. There is no standardized channel template or signal that links a channel to an authoritative Confluence incident playbook.
- This causes inconsistent post-incident documentation, missed runbook updates, and difficulties for cross-org escalation (paging, postmortems, runbook ownership).
- Goal: create a templated Slack channel provision flow plus automations that wire channel creation to a Confluence runbook skeleton and a Jira issue template when an incident channel is created via the ops portal or an automation workflow.
We request internal-support to implement the following: 
1) Slack: Add a new channel creation template named 'incident-playbook' that pre-populates: pinned runbook link placeholder, onboarding message with playbook checklist, channel topic (Incident: <short-desc> | Sev <n>), and a bot that posts a reminder to populate postmortem link after incident closure.
2) Confluence: Create a new page template 'Infra Incident Playbook - skeleton' under space /confluence/spaces/ops-runbooks with required sections (summary, impact, mitigation steps, rollback, owner, runbook version). Grant edit rights to +infra-oncall and +platform-oncall groups.
3) Automation: Build a sync so that when a channel is created using the incident-playbook template, a Confluence skeleton page is created and the page URL is posted to the channel. Additionally create a linked Jira issue (project: INT-ops-maintenance) populated with a 'Postmortem' template.
4) Retention/Audit: Ensure all created incident channels are flagged with a retention tag and their creation events are logged to the audit channel #ops-audit. Provide an option to auto-archive channels after 90 days unless the channel owner requests extension.
5) Documentation: Add a short runbook for oncall engineers describing the flow and how to manually trigger the sync (edge case handling).
- Slack channel template 'incident-playbook' exists and is available in the channel creation modal for users with +oncall role.
- Creating a channel with that template creates a Confluence page skeleton and posts the link in channel within 60s.
- A Jira 'Postmortem' issue is auto-created and linked in the channel.
- Permissions on the Confluence runbook are set to allow oncall editing and ops-reviewers to comment.

title: Privilege-escrow: temporary service-account elevation for cross-log account-mapping audit
body:
Privilege-escrow: temporary service-account elevation for cross-log account-mapping audit

Issue summary: Request time-limited privilege escrow for a dedicated SRE service account to perform an account-mapping audit across production request traces, kv-cache metadata, and billing ingestion pipelines.

Impact: There is a suspected mismatch between invoiced token counts and a customer reconciliation report (Acme Analytics, enterprise tier). The data required to validate the reconciliation is spread across multiple systems and requires a join on hashed request identifiers that are not accessible to regular SRE roles for privacy reasons.

Justification: A minimal, auditable, time-restricted elevation is required to produce an aggregated reconciliation artefact (hash joins and aggregated counts only — no raw payloads). This will allow Finance and Support to confirm whether an invoice overage is a billing bug or a customer-side discrepancy.

Scope & constraints:
- Access target: production request metadata indices, KV-cache metadata (no raw payloads), and billing ingestion logs for 2026-02-15 to 2026-03-01 (two-week window).
- Data minimization: export must contain only hashed_request_id, timestamp, model_id, token_counts, and ingestion_batch_id. No prompt/response text, no user identifiers.
- Duration: 8 business hours of elevated access, starting after approval and following a completed runbook checklist.
- Audit controls: all actions performed under the escrowed service account must be logged to the secure audit stream (immutable), and an on-call Security reviewer must observe via live screen share for the initial query run.

Requested deliverables:
1) Aggregated CSV mapping hashed_request_id -> token_count, model_id, ingestion_batch_id for window.
2) Short reconciliation summary (one paragraph) describing whether totals align with invoiced units and any anomalies found.

Attachments: link to customer ticket SUP-9921 (billing inquiry), snapshot of customer-reported totals, and billing ingestion dashboard links.
