title: Dedicated autoscaling oscillation causing latency spikes (Northstar Payments)
body:
Dedicated autoscaling oscillation causing latency spikes (Northstar Payments)

Issue summary:
Northstar Payments reports periodic p95/p99 latency spikes on their Dedicated deployment. Early signal suggests repeated scale-up/scale-down events (“autoscaling churn”) causing request queuing and cold-start penalties.

Impact:
- Customer-visible latency spikes (chat + embeddings) during business hours.
- No full outage; error rate remained low but elevated timeouts in client (customer-side 30s timeout).
- Customer concern: reliability regression compared to prior week.

Customer context:
- Tier: Dedicated
- Primary workloads: chat completions + embeddings
- Notable constraints: customer has strict p99 latency target in peak windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: northstar-payments / us-east
- Runtime: 1.18.x (per customer note)
- Autoscaling mode: request-driven (target utilization)

Symptoms (as reported):
- p95 jumps from ~700ms to 4–8s for ~5–10 minute intervals.
- Spikes correlate with frequent instance count changes.

Initial triage checklist (Support):
- Confirm region, model(s), approximate time windows, and request IDs.
- Pull dedicated dashboards: request queue depth, replica count, GPU utilization, cold start time, and scheduler events.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-02-05 15:22: Customer email + console screenshot showing replica count “sawtooth”.
- 2026-02-05 15:31: SUP opened, P1 set; Slack bridge created (#support bridge, then moved to #incidents for visibility).
- 2026-02-05 16:05: SRE engaged to validate scaling events and rule out host-level contention.

Diagnostics / notes:
- Dedicated replica count oscillating between 4 and 10 on ~6–9 min cadence.
- Queue depth spikes immediately after scale-down; subsequent scale-up lags by ~2–3 minutes.
- Noisy neighbor unlikely (dedicated isolation intact); symptoms align with aggressive scale-down + workload burstiness.

Mitigation applied (temporary):
- Increased min replicas to reduce cold-start thrash.
- Increased scale-down cooldown to avoid rapid contraction.
- Adjusted target utilization to reduce oscillation sensitivity.

Follow-ups:
- Link to ENG-4829 (guardrails for autoscaling stability) for a productized fix.
- Publish/refresh known-issues workaround article for Dedicated autoscaling oscillation with Support copy/paste steps and “when to escalate” criteria.
2026-02-05 15:34 UTC — Dev Patel (Support)
Set priority P1 / Sev2 based on customer impact (latency spikes causing timeouts but not a full outage). Requesting: affected endpoints, request IDs from last spike, and whether customer changed traffic patterns or configs.

Created Slack bridge per playbook and invited on-call + Dedicated on-call.
Links:
- Linear: ENG-4829 (autoscaling stability guardrail)
- Known-issue draft: workaround-dedicated-autoscaling-oscillation

Provided time window 14:40–15:15 UTC and sample request IDs (shared privately in email; not pasted here). Notes no changes on their side; traffic bursty due to downstream batch jobs.

Also shared screenshot: replicas 4→10→4 repeatedly; p99 correlated.
2026-02-05 16:07 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Confirmed from dashboards: replica count oscillation with cooldown set low. Cold start time ~90–120s per new replica is enough to hurt tail latency during bursts.

Suggested immediate mitigation:
1) raise min_replicas to cover baseline peak
2) increase scale_down_cooldown to >= 15–20m
3) consider slightly lower target_utilization to keep more headroom

No infra alarms; nodes healthy; no indication of GPU faults.

Applied temporary config changes with Dedicated ops approval:
- min_replicas: 4 → 6
- scale_down_cooldown: 5m → 20m

Monitoring next 60–90 minutes for reduced sawtooth and improved tail latency.

Latency improved: p99 back to ~1.2–1.8s. Replica count stable at 6–8; fewer scale events. Queue depth spikes reduced.

Flag: keep an eye on cost implications; raising floor increases steady-state spend. Recommend follow-up with customer on acceptable baseline capacity vs SLO target.
2026-02-05 17:42 UTC — Ethan Park (Platform)
Acknowledged this pattern is recurring across a few Dedicated accounts with bursty traffic. ENG-4829 is the right track: add guardrails + better defaults.

for the ENG-4829 acceptance criteria.

Queued for SRE + Dedicated Eng review before publishing broadly.

title: Provision dedicated GPU benchmark runner capacity for Runtime LTS perf gates (avoid blocking CI)
body:
Provision dedicated GPU benchmark runner capacity for Runtime LTS perf gates (avoid blocking CI)

Request
- We need dedicated GPU runner capacity for perf-canary benchmarks used as *release gates* for Runtime LTS patch releases.
- Current state: perf jobs are contending with general CI and ad-hoc benchmark runs, causing queue times and occasional partial coverage during patch week.

Why this matters
- LTS patches are blocked on perf gate results (p50/p95 latency + throughput across canonical workloads). Any runner starvation delays releases and increases risk of releasing without full coverage.
- We also need to avoid impacting regular developer CI and nightly runs.

Scope
- Provision/allocate a separate runner pool (or reserved quota) for perf-canary “release-branch / LTS gate” workflows.
- Ensure capacity exists for concurrent runs during patch week (RC validation + reruns for flakes) without starving mainline.

Requirements (from Runtime LTS workstream)
- GPU SKUs: H100 (primary), A100 (secondary) at minimum.
- Concurrency target: 6 parallel benchmark jobs (H100) + 2 parallel (A100) during patch week; outside patch week, allow scale down to 2+1.
- Runtime: each job ~45–70 minutes wall time; expect 2–3 full gate cycles per RC (initial run + rerun(s)).
- Determinism: pin driver/container image; avoid noisy neighbors (dedicated nodes preferred).

Acceptance criteria
- New runner pool available to perf-canary with labels (e.g., runner_group=lts-perf-gate).
- perf-canary workflows updated to target that pool for release/* and runtime-*-lts branches.
- Documented scheduling policy + escalation path if capacity is exhausted.

Owners / stakeholders
- Requestor: Sahana Iyer (CI/build)
- Release Eng: Connor O’Brien
- Runtime perf: Marcus Reed / Jonas Weber
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (assignee), Rafael Mendes (backup)

References
- Slack: #eng-sre / “lts-perf-gate-thresholds” and #eng-infra / runner capacity discussion
- Related: INT-3302 for release-branch CI permissions/secrets; ENG-4825 for perf gate integration into LTS release.

- tagged RC runs

title: Sustained 5xxs after route weight change: tainted prefetch cache + priority-queue starvation
body:
Sustained 5xxs after route weight change: tainted prefetch cache + priority-queue starvation

Issue summary: After a customer-directed route weight adjustment this morning, Atlas reported a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the API (primarily 502/503). Impact: ~18% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx over a 22-minute window, causing user-facing failures in chat and embedding uploads. Environment: Dedicated tenant in prod (us-east) using pinned instances and prefetch enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Apply route weight change (route weight shifted from default pool -> new pool) 2) Resume normal traffic ramp for tenant 3) Observe elevated 5xxs and increased runtime restart counts Observed behavior: API gateway returns 502/503; serving runtimes show repeated model-prefetch evictions and KV cache miss storms. Runtime logs contain frequent "prefetch-lock-timeout" and "connection lease expired" messages. Expected behavior: Route weight change should redirect traffic without increasing 5xx floor; prefetch cache eviction should be graceful without triggering runtime crash/restarts. Initial hypothesis: Misrouted traffic landed on a small set of warm runtimes while a prefetch-eviction race left those runtimes with tainted kvcache states; combined with ingress prioritizer dropping lower-priority requests, this led to priority-queue starvation and upstream connection churn causing 5xx amplification.
13:02 UTC - Alert: tenant Atlas saw error-rate jump from baseline 0.6% -> 18%. Notified via #support and #incidents.
13:05 UTC - api-gateway metrics show surge in upstream 502s; 95th latency for successful requests increased from 220ms -> 1.4s.
13:08 UTC - serving-runtime team observed repeated "prefetch-lock-timeout" and kvcache eviction spikes on three nodes (node ids: s-ea-12, s-ea-15, s-ea-23).
13:12 UTC - ingress prioritizer logs show several priority-shed events for tenant traffic coincident with route weight change (link: slack://channel#incidents/clip-xyz).
13:18 UTC - Identified that connection leases to the runtime pool expired aggressively due to a stale client keepalive policy during the traffic handoff.
13:24 UTC - Correlated runtime restarts with a prefetch eviction bug where tainted entries triggered heavy KV lock contention (see runtime PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582).
Support (Ethan Myers) 13:10: Thanks for reporting, Atlas. We're triaging — can you confirm if you changed route weights or did this via the Console rollouts?

title: Cross-region burst caused tenant token overdraft during queued routing — request for backoff and routing configuration guidance
body:
Cross-region burst caused tenant token overdraft during queued routing — request for backoff and routing configuration guidance

Customer observed a sustained wave of 429 responses for a dedicated tenant during a cross-region ingest spike. Patterns suggest token accounting drift when requests are routed to a cold region pool and queued for fallback routing; customer requests clear guidance on backoff parameters and smart-routing hints to avoid overdraft during multi-region failover.
Issue summary:
NimbleSearch (dedicated tenant) reported a production incident where a large client-side batch job triggered elevated 429s across two regions. The workflow concurrently opens short-lived streaming sessions in us-east and eu-west. When the primary region experienced transient capacity pressure, requests were routed to eu-west which returned slower warmups and many requests were queued. Token refill accounting and cross-region routing combined to create an overdraft-like pattern where token counters dropped below 0 and 429s were observed across both regions for ~18 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer saw ~12% request failure rate (429) for peak customers over a 18 minute window.
- Business impact: search indexing pipelines delayed; two high-priority customers reported timeouts and triggered support escalation.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Pools: reserved GPU pool in us-east-1, overflow pool in eu-west-1 (cold nodes)
- API usage: mixed streaming short sessions and synchronous batch requests; many ephemeral keys used by ingest workers

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start 200 parallel short streaming sessions in us-east with ephemeral keys and small per-session token footprint.
2) Simultaneously start 50 batch generation requests pinned to the same tenant across both regions.
3) Force a simulated capacity pressure on us-east by adding dummy long-running GPU work.
4) Observe routed requests moving to eu-west and an increase in request queue length and token accounting anomalies.

Observed behavior:
- Rapid spike in queue length on edge-proxy and routing layer, followed by 429s with rate-limit headers showing near-zero refill windows.
- Token counters for tenant showed negative oscillation in internal dump (timestamped counters) before stabilization.
- Latency for fallback requests was high (p90 > 2.3s) while token exhaustion persisted.

Expected behavior:
- Graceful failover with smooth traffic shaping so tenant does not see tenant-level token overdraft; queueing should favor backoff and re-enqueue rather than immediate token burn.

Preliminary logs/metrics provided by customer:
- Edge-proxy logs: repeated 429 responses with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset in ~1s increments.
- Router traces: requests dropped into eu-west queue with worker warmup durations of 1.8–2.6s.
- Tenant counters: periodic token refill variance showing refill bursts misaligned between regions.

Immediate mitigations attempted by customer:
- Added client-side exponential backoff and jitter on retries (reduced apparent 429s by ~60%).
- Temporarily reduced concurrency from ingest workers.

Request from customer:
- Guidance on server-side rate-limit backoff settings and recommended route-weighting to reduce overdraft during cross-region bursts.
(Support) 2026-03-10: Triage by on-call. Key observations: routing fallbacks move traffic to cold pools, token refill windows are per-region and use per-route accounting which can momentarily double-count or misalign when a single tenant has concurrent tokens across regions.

(SRE) 2026-03-11: Collected historical refill logs; found a 3s clock skew on eu-west refill scheduler for this tenant's routing shard leading to refill windows offset. Investigated router codepath that credits token buckets on handoff but does not atomically reconcile when queues are active across regions.

(Hypothesis) Token overdraft was caused by: (1) short-lived streaming sessions creating many ephemeral buckets; (2) fallback routing handing requests to cold pool and queuing while refill timers in that region were lagging; (3) client retries without sufficient jitter causing rapid repeated consumption once refill window fired.

(Temporary actions) Applied a region-level soft cap on concurrent short-lived sessions for the tenant and suggested client-side additional jitter. Scheduled a follow-up to add a reconciliation pass in the router handoff code to avoid transient double-accounting.
Workaround applied: temporary route-weight adjustment to prefer us-east warm pool and a soft concurrency cap for streaming sessions for NimbleSearch. Client implemented exponential backoff with randomized jitter (recommended).

Short-term engineering plan: adjust edge-proxy to enforce per-tenant global concurrency semaphore before region handoff to prevent parallel token buckets from being created.

Medium-term plan: add atomic handoff reconciliation that subtracts tokens from the origin bucket when a routed request is accepted by the fallback region to avoid duplication during queue drain. Also add telemetry to detect refill skew between regions and trigger an automatic temporary hold for new short-lived sessions.

Customer asked for recommended config values: support recommended starting points:
- Client-side: base retry delay 200ms, max backoff 5s, jitter 0.25–0.6
- Server-side: route-weight bias 0.8 to primary region for first 60s after detected capacity pressure; short-session per-tenant soft cap = 150 concurrent sessions; pre-warm threshold for cold pool = queue_length > 30.

Engineer owners: Router: Miguel Torres; Edge-proxy: Priya Rao; SRE: Mateo Ruiz.

Targeted rollout: patch router handoff in canary next 48–72 hours, monitor 429 rate and queue length, then promote to all regions if stable.

1) Deploy router handoff patch to canary (Miguel) 48–72h. 2) Monitor dashboards for 24–72h and collect traces for any 429 resurgence. 3) If stable, roll to other regions and update public best-practices doc for cross-region backoff. 4) Postmortem draft if any unexpected 429 recurrence.

title: Embedding namespace collision + trailing-dim padding causes rerank score inversion and intermittent timeouts
body:
Embedding namespace collision + trailing-dim padding causes rerank score inversion and intermittent timeouts

Customer reports that a recent bulk re-ingest caused large shifts in reranker top-k order and intermittent 503/timeout errors from the reranking endpoint. Symptoms started immediately after KnowMeAI uploaded a new embedding batch (approx 120k vectors) and ran nightly rerank jobs. They observe: score inversions (previous top results dropped to bottom) and ~3-8% of rerank requests returning 503/timeouts for queries that previously succeeded.
Production reranking for KnowMeAI is degraded: search quality regressions (wrong top-k order) affecting UX and intermittent request failures causing job retries. This affects approximately 18% of their weekly queries since the ingest. Customer is on Dedicated tier and is using reserved capacity in us-east-1.
1) Using the customer's dataset, call embeddings.upload with namespace 'user-profiles' and include vectors created by SDK v1.4.2 (they supplied file).
2) Run the rerank endpoint ratelimit of 50 qps against reranker-tiny-v1 with top_k=10 and pass the 'namespace' header set to 'user-profiles'.
3) Observe top-k order differences compared to baseline dataset embedded with SDK v1.3.x.
4) Run 1k synthetic queries and note ~3-8% 503/timeouts and increased p95 latency for rerank requests to 750-1200ms.
5) Inspect embedding dimensions returned from embeddings.list for recently ingested batch and compare against model expected dimension (512).
2026-03-09T22:14:02Z WARN embeddings-service: ingest: namespace 'user-profiles' batch=120345 dims_detected=[512,520] -> mixed-dim detected, routing to fallback-path
2026-03-09T22:14:03Z ERROR serving-runtime: reranker request id=xyz123 queue=long fallback=true reason='mixed-dim-handling' latency=1023ms status=503
2026-03-09T22:14:03Z ERROR reranker: score-compute: numerical-exception: NaN encountered for cos-sim vector pair, input-dims (512 vs 520)
Request sample headers: Authorization=REDACTED, Content-Type=application/json, X-Embedding-Namespace=user-profiles, X-Client-SDK=redwood-python/1.4.2
Stacktrace excerpt: serving-runtime/core/fallback_handler.py: line 210 -> routing decision: FALLBACK_CPU_QUANT_PATH due to dims mismatch
2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Opened ticket after initial customer report. Asked for sample embedding batch and client version. Requested customer's rerank job config and recent request IDs.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (Evan Liu, KnowMeAI): Provided a sample of 1000 vectors (attached) and their ingestion script. Noted they upgraded to redwood-python 1.4.2 during nightly pipeline. Asked for urgent mitigation as search is customer-facing.
2026-03-10 12:40 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Reproduced mixed-dim detection on staging with customer's sample. Confirmed embeddings-service allowed mixed dims in same namespace and tagged batch for fallback path. Pushed initial hypothesis to ticket.
2026-03-11 08:22 - Eng (Priya Menon): Investigating SDK change in 1.4.2; saw a change in numpy serialization that could append two trailing zeros when dtype=float32->bytes in some numpy builds. Proposed quick reject-on-ingest + informative error to stop silent fallback.
2026-03-12 15:30 - Support (Aisha Patel): Shared temporary workaround: advise customer to re-ingest after normalizing dims locally (trim/pad to 512) or pin SDK to 1.3.x until fix; customer accepted re-ingest as short-term plan.
Hypothesis 1: SDK v1.4.2 changed serialization leading to padding of 8 floats (~32 bytes) at end of some vectors, yielding 520 effective dims for a subset of vectors.
Hypothesis 2: Embeddings-service previously accepted heterogeneous vector shapes within same namespace and lazily routed to fallback CPU quant path, which is significantly slower and occasionally OOMs under reserved capacity, causing 503/timeouts.
Reproduction: Replaying customer's 1k vector file on staging produced identical mixed dims and triggered fallback route. Running cosine compute on mismatched shapes produced NaNs and score inversion in reranker outputs.
Telemetry: Between 2026-03-09 21:00 and 2026-03-10 03:00, the customer's rerank p95 latency increased from 420ms to 980ms and error rate spiked to 6% for queries routed to that namespace. CPU fallback replicas warmed up and experienced increased GC and occasional OOM-death cycles.
Root cause (preliminary): Combination of SDK serialization edge-case (client-side) + permissive ingest policy (server-side) allowed mixed-dimension vectors into the same namespace. The reranker assumes uniform dims; mismatch triggers fallback and numeric instability leading to score flip.
Risk: Other customers that upgraded to SDK v1.4.2 and use namespace-level mixing are at risk until ingest validation is enforced.
Confirmed related issue: SUP-91455 (embedding-cache-invalidation-delay) appears in some runs where cache keys didn't clear after re-ingest; added to linked_issues for follow-up.
Action 1 (hotfix): embeddings-service: validate per-batch vector dims on ingest and reject batch with 400 + clear message indicating expected dims and sample offending vector ids. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/842 (merged to main).
Action 2 (service change): Add strict enforcement behind a feature flag to reject mixed-dim vectors on dedicated/private clusters. Flag enabled for KnowMeAI's tenant on 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC.
Action 3 (SDK): Eng created an SDK ticket to patch serialization in redwood-python 1.4.3 to avoid trailing-zero padding; PR filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/304
Action 4 (customer workaround): Instructed KnowMeAI to re-ingest their batch after trimming vectors to 512 dims using 'python -m redwood.tools.normalize_vectors --dim 512' OR pin to SDK v1.3.x. Customer chose re-ingest; completed on 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC.
Action 5 (rollout): After re-ingest and feature-flag enforcement, rerank error rate dropped back to <0.5% and p95 latency returned to baseline ~430ms by 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC. Customer confirmed quality restored.
Temporary mitigation: Added a monitoring alert for mixed-dim ingestion events and a dashboard showing per-namespace dim histogram.
Status: Hotfix deployed and tenant flag set; monitoring in place. Waiting on SDK release and broader rollout.
1) Release redwood-python 1.4.3 with serialization fix and notify customers via /status and SDK release notes (owner: SDK team, due 2026-03-18).
2) Update embeddings ingestion runbook to fail fast on mixed-dim batches and include remediation steps (owner: Eng Ops, due 2026-03-15).
3) Add unit/integration tests that simulate padded vectors from various numpy builds (owner: Embeddings team).
4) Evaluate whether auto-trim/pad is acceptable as an ingestion option (product decision; create RFC).
5) Outreach: email affected Dedicated customers who upgraded to 1.4.x with instructions and links to normalization tool (owner: Customer Success).

title: Approval request for cryptographic-hash-only trace extract for regulated payment dispute
body:
Approval request for cryptographic-hash-only trace extract for regulated payment dispute

ISSUE SUMMARY: Support requests temporary, minimized extract of inference traces for a regulated payment dispute. The export must contain only cryptographic hashes (SHA-256 hex) of request/response blobs plus minimal metadata (timestamp, model_id, route_id, obfuscated_client_id). No plaintext prompts, completions, KV cache contents, or raw customer identifiers may be included.

IMPACT: Legal and Payments teams need a verifiable hexdigest to correlate an external payment reference with an internal processing trace. Customer privacy and compliance require zero plaintext exposure.

ENVIRONMENT: prod - us-east (hosted + dedicated edge routing active during window).

REQUEST DETAILS:
- Provide a timebound (48 hour access window) export scoped to 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z..2026-03-01T06:00:00Z for the specified payment transaction IDs list (provided to Security out-of-band).
- Export format: CSV or newline-delimited JSON where each row contains: sha256_hex(request_blob), sha256_hex(response_blob), event_timestamp, model_id, route_id, obfuscated_client_id (one-way salted hash).
- Salt policy: per-customer ephemeral salt derived from KMS-protected secret; salts are never to be stored in plaintext; provide proof of rotation and KMS audit events.
- Delivery: KMS-wrapped file in ephemeral S3 bucket with 7-day auto-delete and restricted cross-account access; copy to Legal bucket only after two-person approval recorded in audit logs.

JUSTIFICATION: Finance is contesting a charge and needs non-reversible correlation evidence that does not expose PII. A hash-only extract satisfies evidence requirements while preserving customer privacy.

DATA MINIMIZATION & RISK MITIGATION:
- No full request/response or token-level data will be exported.
- Hash algorithm: SHA-256 with per-customer salt; include the hashing algorithm and salt derivation method in the audit record.
- Include an attestation manifest describing what was excluded and verification steps used.

ACCESS CONTROLS REQUESTED:
- Two-person control for unlocking KMS-wrapped salts (security + legal approvers).
- Timebound IAM role scoped to this export job only.
- Full audit trail (who, when, KMS decrypt logs, S3 access).

TIMELINE: Need approval within 72 hours if possible; export job estimated runtime ~15 minutes once query approved.

DELIVERABLES WANTED:
- Signed approval from Security and Legal recorded in this ticket.
- Link to ephemeral S3 object and KMS audit events when export completes.

title: OIDC introspection cache returning stale scope set prevents admin impersonation in private deployment
body:
OIDC introspection cache returning stale scope set prevents admin impersonation in private deployment

Issue summary:
Customer reports they cannot perform admin impersonation (Admin -> Impersonate User) intermittently after their IdP rotated the client secret for the OIDC client. The Redwood private control plane returns 403 on admin-impersonation API calls for a subset of admins for approximately 10-20 minutes after rotation.

Impact:
- Several Nimbus Health admins unable to impersonate user sessions when troubleshooting production incidents.
- Affects private deployment in us-west region only.
- Intermittent; normal admin functions otherwise working.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane)
- Region: us-west-2
- Auth provider: Azure AD (OIDC) with token introspection enabled
- Token introspection endpoint cached by control plane (TTL configurable)

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Admin in Nimbus Health attempts to impersonate a user via the admin console.
2) Admin receives 403 with body: {"error":"forbidden","message":"insufficient_scopes"}
3) After ~10-20 minutes calls resume succeeding without change on the customer side.

Observed logs and traces:
- Control plane auth log snippet: "introspection: cached response found, scopes="["read:users"]" returned, original token scopes="["read:users","impersonate:admin"]"
- Edge proxy trace shows successful TLS to IdP during rotation window, no network failures.
- Customer-side IdP audit shows token refresh and client secret rollover at 2026-03-13T09:12:02Z.
- Redis cache metrics show a spike in introspection cache hits aligned to rotation window.

Immediate hypothesis:
- Introspection responses cached with scope sets derived from older token introspection results. During client secret rotation, IdP returned introspection results with a reduced scope set for transient tokens. The control plane cached that reduced scope set and honored it for the TTL, causing subsequent calls to be judged as missing the impersonation scope until the cache entry expired or a new introspection request overwritten it.

Potential root causes to validate:
- Incorrect cache keying: cache keyed only by access_token issuer but not by token signature/issued_at leading to reuse across rotated secrets.
- Missing cache-busting on client credential change notification from IdP.
- Introspection response parsing that normalizes scopes (dedup/ordering) but drops whitespace-separated tokens in certain assertion forms.

Attachments:
- Redacted control-plane auth logs (attached in ticket).
- Customer IdP rotation audit (provided by customer).

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced internally using a test private deployment with simulated secret rotation. When rotating client secret quickly in succession, the control plane continued to serve an introspection cache entry keyed only on client_id+issuer for the TTL (60s in test), returning stale scope sets.
- Cache key in code: "introspection:issuer:{issuer}:client:{client_id}" — confirmed does not consider token_jti or token_signature.
- Redis TTL set to 600s in customer's config (longer than recommended). That explains 10-20 minute impact window.
- Reviewed recent deploys: a partial refactor of auth service in PR github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/324 modified cache behaviour to increase hit ratios; it removed token-specific hashing unintentionally.
- Confirmed linked issue SUP-30121 references JWKS cache problems; similar symptom but different mechanism (jwks vs introspection cache).

Next steps suggested:
1) Patch: restore token-specific cache keying to include token_iat or token_signature hash (hotfix in auth-service).
2) Mitigation: reduce introspection cache TTL in customer config to 30s and provide guidance to customers to set lower TTL during secret rotations.
3) Add guard: when receiving a successful introspection immediately after a client credential rotation event, bypass cache for a short window.
4) Customer-facing: provide runbook steps to Nimbus Health for next secret rotation to avoid repeat impact (rotate in maintenance window, set TTL low beforehand).
Support (Aisha Kapoor) 2026-03-13: Thanks for the report — we've triaged this as a P1 and are investigating. Please share IdP rotation timestamp and any correlation IDs from the failed 403s.

Customer (Nimbus Health - Daniel Ortiz) 2026-03-13: Provided rotation timestamp and some failed request IDs. Confirm TTL in their override config is 600s.

Auth Eng (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-13: Reproduced locally with a private sandbox. Found the cache key omission; preparing a hotfix branch.

Support (Aisha Kapoor) 2026-03-14: Hotfix branch created and smoke-tested in staging. Rolling patch to affected private tenant at customer's approval.

Resolution notes:
- Deployed hotfix to control plane for Nimbus Health that updates introspection cache key to include a 256-bit hash of the access_token signature + token_iat. This prevents reuse of introspection results across tokens and secret rotations.
- Reduced default introspection cache TTL from 600s to 30s in the patch; documented configuration knob and recommended values for customers performing secret rotations.
- Communicated runbook to Nimbus Health: (1) reduce introspection TTL before rotation, (2) rotate client secret during maintenance window, (3) confirm privileged tokens reissued post-rotation.
- Follow-up tasks: add a detection alert when a high percentage of admin-impersonation requests return insufficient_scopes and correlate with IdP rotation events; tracked as INT-4121 for internal follow-up.

Status: patch applied to customer private control plane, customer validated impersonation flows resumed. Ticket marked for monitoring for 48 hours before closure.

title: Model fingerprint split-brain caused session-affinity drift, duplicated completions and token billing surge — post-incident follow-up
body:
Model fingerprint split-brain caused session-affinity drift, duplicated completions and token billing surge — post-incident follow-up

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-11 09:08 UTC we observed a high-rate surge of 5xx errors and duplicated streaming completions for a subset of CobaltCare traffic routed through eu-west. The initial symptom was duplicate final chunks in streaming responses and token counts roughly 2x expected in customer billing reports. The problem coincided with a canary rollout of a quantized variant of redwood-gpt-13b.

Impact:
- Customer visible: duplicated completions for ~2.1% of requests from CobaltCare during the incident window (09:08–10:27 UTC).
- Billing: elevated token counts reported to CobaltCare and potential double-charges for affected requests.
- SLOs: latency SLOs breached for affected routes; streaming session failures escalated to the on-call SRE team.

Timeline (key events):
- 09:02 UTC: Canary for redwood-gpt-13b-quantized (canary-id: canary-2026-03011-q13b) began serving 2% traffic in eu-west.
- 09:08 UTC: First customer complaint (CobaltCare CS) about duplicated outputs and unexpected token usage.
- 09:12 UTC: Alert: increased 5xx rate and streaming reconnects on route /v1/generate for eu-west.
- 09:18 UTC: On-call Eng (David Kim) triaged; traffic patterns showed simultaneous routing to quantized and standard variants for same session IDs.
- 09:40 UTC: Emergency rollback of the canary to 0% for eu-west.
- 09:52 UTC: Interim mitigation: disabled cross-variant routing reconciliation and forced session-affinity to last-known-model.
- 10:27 UTC: 5xx rate normalized and duplicate completions ceased.
- 11:00 UTC: Billing snapshot captured for audit; customers notified and credits issued pending final reconciliation.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1. Deploy a canary variant with differing model fingerprint metadata (binary/manifest hash mismatch) to routing table.
2. Send a streaming request that opens a session, then trigger a routing rebalance (load spike or autoscaler event) causing router to consult model matching rules.
3. Observe session being split: read-path served from one variant while continuation tokens served from another. Reconstructed streaming output shows repeated termination and reattachment resulting in duplicated end-of-sequence chunks.

Investigation notes / logs referenced:
- Router logs (link): slack://channel/#incidents (thread: canary-splitbrain-2026-03-11) and cloudwatch: /redwood/router/eu-west/2026-03-11
- Serving runtime trace: traces at github.com/redwood-inference/traces/2026/11-09-canary-split.txt (internal).
- Billing snapshot: s3://billing-snapshots/2026-03-11/CobaltCare-eu-west-dup-tokens.csv
- Keyed observation: KV-cache TTL mismatches and per-session model_id tags diverged between router and runtime.

Root cause hypothesis and confirmation:
- Root cause: A model fingerprinting regression in the canary pipeline generated a model manifest hash that was semantically equivalent to the canonical model but did not match the router's strict fingerprint check. During routing reconciliation, this caused the routing layer to treat the canary as a distinct incompatible variant, triggering split-path routing for sessions that had in-flight KV state bound to the canonical variant. The serving runtime accepted continuation requests on the canary variant which had different tokenization/stream framing behavior, producing duplicated terminal chunks and higher token accounting.
- Confirmation steps: correlating request_ids across router and runtime logs showed identical session IDs resolved to two different model_ids within a 2s window. Replaying a sample session with the canary reproduced duplicated completion.

Mitigation and resolution:
- Immediate: Rolled canary back to 0% in eu-west (09:40 UTC), forced routing table reconciliation, and pinned active sessions to their pre-rollout model_id to drain gracefully.
- Short-term: Applied a runtime patch to reject continuation tokens when model_id mismatch detected (PR #1456). This was hotfixed and deployed to eu-west (10:05 UTC).
- Customer remediation: Issued temporary billing credits to CobaltCare and started a line-item audit for affected requests.

Post-incident action items (owner / ETA):
- Add pre-flight model-fingerprint validation in the canary pipeline to prevent manifest-hash drift (owner: Sofia Martinez / ETA: 2026-03-25).
- Tighter router gating: refuse cross-variant session handoff if tokenization/stream framing flags differ (owner: David Kim / ETA: 2026-03-18).
- Billing reconciliation job to identify and refund affected tokens for all impacted customers (owner: Elena Ruiz - Billing / ETA: 2026-03-20).
- Create an automated test that replays sessions across canary/primary variants to detect split-brain effects in CI (owner: Eng QA / ETA: 2026-03-22).
- Update runbook: detection playbook for model-fingerprint split-brain with concrete dashboard thresholds and playbook steps (owner: SRE runbooks / ETA: 2026-03-19).

Resolution notes:
- Root cause patch merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456
- Canary validation checks introduced into CI pipeline for model manifests (deferred to 2026-03-25 rollout).
- Customer credits issued and confirmed; CobaltCare accepted the proposed remediation and will continue on dedicated capacity with new pre-flight validation enabled by default.

Follow-ups for customer communications:
- Drafted post-incident summary and timeline for CobaltCare CS review (Aisha Patel).
- Scheduled a 1:1 technical review with CobaltCare platform team on 2026-03-16 to review mitigations and to audit billing adjustments.

title: Autoscaler opened node requests but requests queued — reduced throughput in dedicated GPU pool
body:
Autoscaler opened node requests but requests queued — reduced throughput in dedicated GPU pool

Issue summary: Customer reports sustained request queueing and token throughput drop for their Dedicated pool starting 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC. Autoscaler issued scale-out requests but new nodes did not become usable; requests were queued causing elevated P50/P95 generation latency and occasional 429s. Impact: affecting one enterprise customer's production workflows (real-time summarization), increased tail-latency and some dropped streams. Observed symptoms point to GPU attach/driver issues plus a noisy tenant causing degraded PCIe throughput on a subset of nodes. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations, and follow-up remediation tasks.
1) Customer submits sustained concurrent generation load matching their historical peak: ~120 concurrent sessions targeting redwood-open-7b-v2.
2) Autoscaler evaluates NodeGroup A and requests 3 additional nodes (GPU-backed) to meet queue targets.
3) New node provisioning starts but kubelet reports node Ready false; serving runtime shows GPUs not registered.
4) Requests remain in queue; latency increases and 429 throttles appear between 02:15-02:50 UTC.

Hypothesis 1: Provisioning AMI mismatch (GPU driver) prevented new nodes from registering GPUs. Evidence: kubelet error shows driver mismatch; two failed node attaches.
Hypothesis 2: Noisy neighbor on pool caused PCIe saturations lowering effective throughput of co-located nodes. Evidence: host-level monitoring shows sustained high PCIe Tx/Rx and large NVLINK usage from tenant container PID 8421.
Cloud provider quotas checked: GPU quota available in region. Not a soft quota exhaustion event.
Autoscaler logs: scale-out requests completed but nodes not Ready; autoscaler backoff engaged after 2 failed attempts. Thresholds too aggressive for transient provisioning instability.
Customer traffic profile: bursty with many short-lived streams; batching config not optimal for this workload leading to higher kernel invocation overhead.
Observed 429s were from front-tier queueing, not explicit rate-limit policy; caused by lack of Ready capacity and request queue cap enforcement.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC: replaced faulty AMI on node group and reprovisioned 3 nodes with correct GPU drivers; cordoned and drained two impacted nodes.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-10 04:15 UTC: moved noisy tenant-3142 to overflow capacity and limited their allowed concurrent streams (temporary quota) to reduce PCIe contention.
Customer-facing workaround: temporarily increased fallback to redwood-open-1.3b-quant for non-critical streams and enabled prefix caching to reduce token work.
Root cause: AMI rollback during recent infra maintenance introduced older GPU driver on new instances, combined with a noisy tenant co-located on the same dedicated pool causing degraded node throughput.
Permanent fixes planned: 1) pin AMI build in auto-provisioner and add driver check in node health probe; 2) implement PCIe contention alerting for node-level telemetry; 3) adjust autoscaler backoff to retry with shorter backoff for node-provisioner class failures; 4) implement tenant isolation policy for dedicated pools to prevent noisy co-tenancy in single node group.
Follow-ups created: INT-4021 (infra: AMI pin and driver probe), INT-4022 (telemetry: PCIe saturation alerting), SUP-7860 (customer: postmortem follow-up and quota adjustment request from StreamScribe).

title: Unexpected 5xx spike tied to rate-bloom and runtime thread starvation during tenant concurrency ramp
body:
Unexpected 5xx spike tied to rate-bloom and runtime thread starvation during tenant concurrency ramp

Issue summary:
Customer Epsilon Labs reported a sudden elevation in 5xx errors (502/503) observed around 2026-03-14T03:17:00Z on their dedicated cluster in us-east-1. Errors primarily surfaced on their high-concurrency chat route (tenant-scoped).

Impact:
- ~15% increased 5xx rate on the tenant's routed API keys between 03:17 - 04:10 UTC.
- Client-facing timeouts and aborted streaming sessions; several large batches returned 502.
- Customer reports degraded SLAs for peak batch window; billing-sensitive workload.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (fleet: ded-us-east-42) servicing Epsilon Labs.
- Serving runtime: gpu-runtime v2.7.3, api-gateway v1.14.
- Autoscaler policy: conservative warmup with aggressive prefetch.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer ramped a concurrency job at 03:15 UTC (gradual, but sustained increase over minutes).
2) Around 03:17 UTC apigw accept_queue length started growing for tenant route.
3) Apigw began returning 502 on first-byte-timeouts; serving runtime threads moved to near-100% sys CPU.
4) Runtime started emitting worker hang warnings and occasional SIGABRT restarts on the node handling the tenant.
5) Healthcheck-driven rebalancer amplified handoffs, creating a feedback loop and sustained 5xx floor.

Logs / key excerpts (sanitized):
- [03:16:58Z] apigw[route:tenant-xyz] accept_queue_len=8124 backlog_ms=412
- [03:17:05Z] runtime[node:ded-us-east-42-03] threadpool_util=98% threads_blocked=342 "worker-hang"
- [03:17:18Z] runtime[node:ded-us-east-42-03] ERROR: prefetch-cancelled -> KV lock thrash
- [03:18:03Z] apigw[proxy] returning 502 first_byte_timeout
- [03:21:44Z] kernel: OOM-killer triggered (but recovered), nvml: gpu driver soft reset logged

Immediate mitigation attempted by Support:
- Scoped temporary rate cap of 60% on the tenant burst queue at 03:25 UTC.
- Rerouted a fraction (20%) of traffic to a cold spare region (us-west-2) at 03:30 UTC to reduce pressure on faulty node.
- Eng notified for priority investigation.

Notes on what is NOT observed:
- No evidence of network packet loss between apigw and runtime.
- No recent deployment/variant swap for the tenant in the 24h preceding the incident.

Request for SRE/Runtime team:
- Confirm root cause of thread starvation and whether token-bucket/rate-limiter miscalculation caused accept_queue bloom.
- Recommend immediate remediation steps to prevent reoccurrence for dedicated tenants during burst ramps.

[Support - 2026-03-14T03:28Z] Aisha Patel: Temporarily applied tenant-level burst cap and opened this ticket. Customer sees partial relief but error floor persists. Notified SRE by page.
[SRE - 2026-03-14T03:34Z] Kai Morgan: Observed accept_queue spike correlating with tokenbucket refill jitter; several runtime threads in D state waiting on kvcache mutex. Investigating thread-stack dumps.
[Customer - 2026-03-14T03:40Z] Epsilon contact (Lina Zhao): We observed many aborted websocket sessions and increased client retries. Appreciate ETA on mitigation; this impacts nightly jobs.
[Eng - 2026-03-14T03:55Z] Marco Sanchez: Collecting core dumps and attaching runtime telemetry. Suspect a rate-limiter arithmetic edge-case when concurrent refill events overlap with healthcheck-induced prefetches.
[SRE - 2026-03-14T04:05Z] Kai Morgan: Reroute and rate cap reduced tail error, but one runtime node shows repeated watchdog restarts; isolating node and draining in progress.
[Support - 2026-03-14T04:20Z] Aisha Patel: Customer notified of temporary mitigations (rate cap + partial reroute). Customer accepted workaround; asked for timeline for permanent fix.
Hypothesis A: Token-bucket "rate-bloom" where concurrent refill and borrow operations under high concurrency produce transient over-allocation and a sudden accept_queue flood.
Hypothesis B: KVCACHE lock convoy plus prefetch cancellation causing runtime threads to block (observed large blocked-thread counts in stack dumps).
Evidence: accept_queue_len > 8000 metrics at spike; runtime thread dumps show majority waiting on kvcache::write_mutex; kernel log includes nvml driver soft-reset shortly after the spike.
Cross-checks: No recent config rollouts for apigw; autoscaler did not scale up nodes fast enough due to conservative warmup. Cold spare region accepted traffic with expected latency and minimal 5xx.
Related artifacts: stack-dump links uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/sup-808808/), apigw traces linked in PR  https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/20421 (internal), and Grafana dashboard panels: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/incident/sup-808808-acceptqueue
Mitigation implemented: 03:25 UTC tenant burst cap applied, 03:30 UTC ~20% traffic rerouted to us-west-2, 04:10 UTC problematic runtime node drained and replaced.
Permanent fix planned: patch token-bucket implementation to serialize concurrent refill/borrow operations and add safety floor to accept_queue accounting (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/20457).
Follow-up actions: Autoscaler warmup policy will be tuned for dedicated customers with warmup threshold lowered; add canary tests for high-concurrency refill paths; postmortem to be scheduled with SRE/Runtime/Products within 3 business days.
Customer communication: Notified Epsilon Labs of temporary mitigation and next steps; scheduled a post-incident review for 2026-03-16 17:00 UTC.

title: MapleBridge ordering: duplicate completions from retried requests due to idempotency-key collision — post-incident escalation
body:
MapleBridge ordering: duplicate completions from retried requests due to idempotency-key collision — post-incident escalation

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 14:10 UTC MapleBridge reported seeing duplicate order confirmations returned to their downstream systems. Duplicate responses correlated with customer retries; root cause traced to idempotency-key collisions introduced by a routing change during the 2026-03-10 canary deploy.
Impact: Customer reports duplicated orders (2–3x) for a subset of API calls during a 40-minute window. Financial exposure and elevated support overhead; customer placed incident hotline call and requested rollback. No data exfiltration suspected.
Timeline: 2026-03-10 14:08 UTC — first 5xx spike observed on MapleBridge tenant metrics. 14:10 — customer support inbound escalation. 14:25 — SRE identified unusual idempotency key reuse pattern. 14:40 — rollback of routing change began. 14:55 — duplicate responses stopped. 15:10 — monitoring shows normal traffic.
Environment: Production (us-east), Hosted Redwood API, customer enterprise account on dedicated routing policy 'rb-evenshard'.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Send identical request payloads in quick succession without idempotency header. 2) Send same request with X-Idempotency-Key set to short random (8 chars) during canary routing enabled. 3) Observe duplicate completions when routing table flaps under burst load.
Observed behavior: Requests that should have been deduplicated were assigned the same internal dedupe token due to a hash truncation change in routing layer; retries were treated as new requests leading to 2–3 completions returned upstream.
Expected behavior: Identical idempotency keys and request fingerprints should be deduplicated and return single completion.
Logs excerpt: 'router:assign_token() truncated_hash=0x1f3a len=8 tenant=maplebridge route=rb-evenshard', 'kv-dedupe: hit=false key=maplebridge/req/0x1f3a', 'completions: emit completion_id=cmp_abc123 request_id=req_abc123'
Billing exposure: Preliminary estimate 1.8x token billing on ~3k affected requests; finance notified for potential credit.
Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-10T14:12Z: Opened ticket after customer's hotline call describing duplicate order confirmations. Customer provided sample request_ids and timestamps.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-10T14:30Z: Observed dedupe misses on tenant 'maplebridge' during routing update. Correlates with new truncation logic from PR #4921.
Priya Shah (Eng) 2026-03-10T14:45Z: Rolling back routing trunk-local hash truncation in canary; patch queued to disable naive truncation behavior.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-10T15:02Z: Rollback completed across canary nodes. Post-rollback checks show dedupe hit rate recovered to baseline.
Marcus Li (Customer Success) 2026-03-10T15:30Z: Informed customer of rollback and interim mitigation. Customer requested formal post-incident write-up; escalated to enterprise SLA owner.
Hypothesis: recent change to router hash generator truncated digest to 8 bytes to reduce key length for memstore; collisions increased under tenant fanout patterns.
Reproduced locally by enabling 'trunc_hash_to_8' toggle and replaying MapleBridge traffic samples; duplicate completions reproduced in 95% of trials where retries occurred within 120ms.
KV-dedupe layer expects full 32-byte fingerprint; truncation resulted in earlier eviction and logical collisions when combined with route affinity.
Monitoring gaps: no dedupe collision alerts on console; add metric for dedupe_hit_rate per-tenant and per-routing-policy.
Rolled back the truncation change in routing canary (PR reverted).
Enabled emergency tenant-level dedupe-protection: keep full fingerprint for tenants flagged as 'sensitive' until fix is deployed.
Issued interim billing credit to MapleBridge for affected window (billing team coordinated).
Deployed hotfix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4928) that restores full fingerprint length when generating dedupe keys and adds a unit test covering retries.

ENG-TRACK-921: Add unit/integration tests for hash truncation and memstore collisions (owner: Priya Shah) — due 2026-03-18
OPS-TRACK-514: Run full tenant audit for other customers using rb-evenshard routing policy (owner: SRE team) — due 2026-03-17
CS-TRACK-87: Customer-facing post-incident report with timeline and credits (owner: Marcus Li) — due 2026-03-12

title: Hidden soft-throttle windows produce bursts of 429s; client retry amplification presents as endpoint hangs/slow inference
body:
Hidden soft-throttle windows produce bursts of 429s; client retry amplification presents as endpoint hangs/slow inference

Issue summary: Customer reports sporadic multi-second inference stalls for streaming requests; trace shows a short burst of 429 responses from the gateway followed by a surge of client retries. Impact: production traffic from Clipster Media in us-east experiences apparent timeouts; user-facing video caption jobs fail intermittently and queue up. Initial observation: the pattern is short (5-15s) windows of enforced soft-throttle that are not surfaced clearly to customers, combined with aggressive client retry logic that amplifies the load and looks like a serving-side latency regression.
2026-03-12T11:10Z - Customer support ticket opened by CS after multiple customer escalations
2026-03-12T11:25Z - Support reproduced 429 bursts from customer's traffic pattern in prod logs
2026-03-12T11:45Z - Routed to SRE for rate-limiter/observability deep-dive
2026-03-12T12:30Z - Temporary mitigation advised to customer: reduce client concurrency and apply exponential backoff with jitter
2026-03-12T12:55Z - SRE identified short-lived rate-window enforcement in the gateway (soft quota) coincident with Clipster traffic spikes
1) Use Clipster production API key against prod us-east endpoint with same concurrency (16 connections) and request rate (~120 rps)
2) Issue streaming generate requests with typical prompt sizes (avg 120 tokens) repeatedly for 5+ minutes
3) Observe gateway logs for 429s followed by client retry bursts; measure tail latency and error rates
4) Re-run with client backoff (base=200ms, cap=2s, jitter) - fewer amplified errors observed
Intermittent multi-second perceived hangs during inference requests
Short bursts (5-15s) of 429 responses from api-gateway with X-RateLimit-Remaining indicating soft enforcement
Customer SDK retries immediately (no jitter) causing retry amplification and additional 429s
Endpoints appear slow because retries queue up and increase end-to-end latencies
Rate limits should be signaled consistently with clear Retry-After headers
Client SDKs should back off to avoid amplification; platform should provide clearer soft-throttle telemetry
Transient quota enforcement should not produce visible multi-second hangs for well-behaved clients
[2026-03-12T11:22:03Z] gateway: client_key=clipster-prod status=429 msg=soft-throttle-window remain=0 window_ms=12000
[2026-03-12T11:22:03Z] client-sdk: req_id=abc123 retry=1 error=429 immediate_retry

[2026-03-12T11:22:10Z] serving-runtime: p99_latency=520ms tokens=avg120 concurrent=30
Hypothesis A: Soft throttle windows are sized to burst tolerance but not exposed via Retry-After; clients aggressive retry patterns convert a temporary throttle to sustained overload
Hypothesis B: Dedicated pool booking mis-evaluated burst credits for Clipster causing short enforcement windows when near commit boundaries
SRE checked gateway rate-limiter timeline: enforcement spikes align with customer traffic spikes and coincide with internal burst-window recalculation (scheduler job at :00/:30)
Observed that the customer's SDK version 0.9.2 does immediate retries without jitter in streaming mode; recommending upgrade to 0.9.4 where backoff is default
Checked Dedicated capacity metrics: no GPU OOMs, no node restarts. Serving runtime p95/p99 latency stable outside throttle windows. Suggests throttle is at gateway/quota layer rather than runtime regression.
1) Short term: Advised Clipster to apply exponential backoff with jitter and reduce concurrency to 8 connections (applied 12:30 UTC)
2) Platform: add Retry-After header and clearer X-Soft-Throttle flag on 429 responses (workaround PR drafted)
3) Ops: disable scheduled burst-credit recalculation during peak window for affected dedicated pools while we investigate
4) Support: monitor error rate with an ad-hoc dashboard and daily sync until resolved
Create a small rate-limiter tweak PR to emit Retry-After and X-Soft-Throttle metadata (owner: infra/rate-limiter)
Backport updated client SDK default backoff to 0.9.4 and push patch release notes targeted to Dedicated customers
Add a Canary check that simulates client retries to ensure soft-throttle windows don't amplify under typical SDK patterns
Postmortem after stabilization with recommendations for soft-throttle telemetry and API-level guidance
SRE validated that 429s are coming from gateway soft-throttle windows and not from serving runtime. Temporary customer mitigation applied. Engineering PR to add clearer headers and telemetry is in draft. Continuing to monitor Clipster traffic for recurrence.
Triage ongoing: temporary mitigations in place. Will mark Resolved after PRs merged, SDK guidance published, and 72 hours of stable error-rate metrics.

title: Discrepant throttle headers when concurrency window saturated by short-lived ephemeral agents
body:
Discrepant throttle headers when concurrency window saturated by short-lived ephemeral agents

Issue summary:
BrightRoute reports repeated 429 responses for short-lived streaming sessions despite throttle headers indicating ample remaining tokens and no tenant token exhaustion. The customer is seeing degraded UX for third-party agents that create ephemeral API keys for each micro-interaction.

Impact:
- Customer-facing call agents intermittently receive HTTP 429 while initiating streams (impacting 5-10% of sessions during peak).
- Business-critical workflow (real-time booking confirmations) experiences visible latency/failures.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east), Dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated pool rp-ded-4
- Customer uses a pool of ephemeral keys: keys minted per agent session via their auth service (TTL ~30s)
- Streaming API over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections (many short-lived streams on single connection)
Create 200 ephemeral keys with TTL 20-40s (simulate agent pool behavior)
Open 100 concurrent streaming sessions over 5 client hosts (HTTP/2 multiplexing) each sending small prompts and immediately closing after response (~2-3s per session)
Observe 429 responses returned on stream start for a subset of requests while checking response headers
Capture response headers (noting X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Window, X-Redwood-Concurrency-Remaining or similar)
Some stream start requests return 429 with body: 'rate limit exceeded'. Response headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 1200, X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000, X-Redwood-Concurrency-Remaining: 0. Header counts imply token quota is available but concurrency capacity is zero. 429s occur in bursts and correlate with rapid spawn of ephemeral keys.
When header X-RateLimit-Remaining > 0 the request should not be 429 unless concurrency or other explicit gate is exhausted; headers should clearly reflect which gate (token quota vs concurrency slots) caused the 429.
[2026-03-12T15:03:21Z] ingress-proxy: request start key=ephem-rcv-12; conn_id=abc123; http2_stream=45
[2026-03-12T15:03:21Z] rate-limiter: tenant=brightroute; tokens_remaining=1200; concurrency_slots_remaining=0; window=60s
HTTP/2 429
X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 1200
X-RateLimit-Reset: 160
X-Redwood-Concurrency-Remaining: 0
Body: {"error":"rate limit exceeded"}
2026-03-12 15:20 — Asha Patel (Support): Opening ticket at customer request. Customer supplied load script and header captures. They are confident tokens aren't exhausted; suspect concurrency gating or mis-accounting for ephemeral keys.
2026-03-12 15:45 — Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced locally with a small harness. Confirmed concurrency_slots drop to zero and cause 429 even though the token bucket has credits. Hypothesis: per-tenant concurrency window being shared across ephemeral keys and connection pooling causing slot leaks on abrupt stream close.
2026-03-12 16:10 — BrightRoute (Customer): Provided additional traces showing ephemeral keys rotated every 25s and ~20 short-lived agent processes spawning in parallel. Asked for short-term mitigation (we need a quick config change if possible).
2026-03-12 18:02 — Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Applied a temporary rule to relax concurrency enforcement for streams with header X-Ephemeral-Agent: true on a targeted route as a test. Saw 60% reduction in 429s in customer test window. Not a product fix — requires engineering review for safety and fairness.
2026-03-13 09:30 — Product (Liu Chen): Requested data on how often connection resets lead to slot leaks and whether a soft timeout for slot reclamation is already present. Asked infra to surface metrics for slot hold times and abrupt-close counts.
Reproduced with internal load harness that mimics ephemeral key rotation and short streams over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections.
Rate limiter enforces two gates: token bucket (per-tenant tokens) and concurrency slots/window (max active streams per-tenant). Headers report both but 429 currently only returns generic message; we should return gate-specific code in headers/body.
Concurrency slots are held until stream close event or until lease TTL expires. Abrupt client disconnects sometimes do not immediately release slots due to edge-proxy timeout configuration (idle timeout 30s).
Ephemeral keys increase cardinality of active sessions which increases probability of short-lived streams colliding and exhausting concurrency slot gates even when token buckets have capacity.
Temporary relaxation of concurrency gate for flagged agent traffic reduced immediate 429s but may open DOS/abuse vector if abused by tenant traffic patterns.
Short term: Customer can batch short agent interactions to reuse streaming sessions where possible (reuse connection-level streams), or increase per-tenant concurrency via support-config change for their dedicated pool (requires approval).
Short term: Add header X-Ephemeral-Agent: true from client to identify trusted ephemeral agent traffic; we can apply a limited experimental exemption on dedicated pool for BrightRoute during testing (already trialed).
Medium term: Suggest client-side exponential backoff with jitter on 429s for ephemeral agents to reduce microburst collision.
Long term: Engineering to implement explicit 429 reason header (e.g., X-Redwood-429-Reason: concurrency-window) and faster slot reclamation on abrupt disconnects (reduce edge-proxy idle timeout or add active socket close handling).
SRE to capture metrics: slot_hold_time histogram, abrupt_close_rate per tenant for last 7 days (assigned Miguel) — due 2026-03-15
Eng (rate-limiter) to spec and implement gate-specific 429 headers and ephemeral-key-aware configs — ticket INT-33421 (linked) — owner: Priya Rao
