title: Legacy supplier entity change caused invoice holds due to attachment filename truncation and PO-line allocation mismatch
body:
Legacy supplier entity change caused invoice holds due to attachment filename truncation and PO-line allocation mismatch

Issue summary: Several vendor invoices from supplier 'TriLake Systems' are stuck in AP hold. The invoice processor flagged them as potential duplicates and routed them to manual review. Finance reports these invoices correspond to open POs but are not auto-matching due to a mismatch between the PO's legal entity and the invoice 'payee' metadata after a supplier legal-entity consolidation last month. Additionally, OCR-extracted attachment filenames are being truncated to 64 chars by an upstream S3 metadata job which causes the duplicate-detection key to differ from the incoming invoice payload.

Impact: 8 invoices (total ~USD 42,900) are on hold and will miss the payment run if not cleared. Affected items are mid-month vendor payments with potential vendor relations impact.

Environment: Production invoice ingestion pipeline, us-east-1 region. Affected workflow: invoice-parse -> duplicate-check -> PO-match -> AP-hold.

Observed behaviour: The invoice parser extracts payee identifier that still includes legacy suffix (TriLake LLC) but POs are allocated to the merged entity (TriLake Systems Inc). The duplicate-check uses attachment filename+checksum as one of the dedupe keys; when the filename is truncated (by s3-metadata service) the key changes and the system marks invoice as 'new' but then fails three-way PO-match due to entity mismatch and goes into HOLD_DUPLICATE_REVIEW.
1) Upload sample invoice 'TriLake-INV-2026-0310-very-long-filename-that-exceeds-system-limit.pdf' to the AP S3 bucket in prod-us-east-1.
2) Let invoice-parser process (invoice-parser v1.12).
3) Observe generated invoice metadata in Dynamo table invoices-prod.
4) Check duplicate-check logs for dedupe key generation and note filename truncation.
5) Check PO-match service output and see mismatch between invoice.payee_entity and po.legal_entity.
invoice-parser logs (2026-03-10T14:12:23Z): INFO parsed filename=TriLake-INV-2026-0310-very-long-filename-that-exceeds-system-limit.pdf; s3-metadata normalized_filename=TriLake-INV-2026-0310-very-long-filename-that-exceeds-syste...; dedupe_key=sha256:ab12...
duplicate-check (2026-03-10T14:12:24Z): WARN dedupe_key mismatch for incoming payload vs s3-object metadata
po-match (2026-03-10T14:12:26Z): ERROR entity_mismatch: invoice.payee=TriLake LLC, po.legal_entity=TriLake Systems Inc
AP UI: HOLD_DUPLICATE_REVIEW created by rule po_entity_mismatch
Hypotheses: 1) s3-metadata service truncates filename to 64 chars in metadata causing dedupe key drift. 2) Supplier consolidation updated POs to the new legal entity but legacy invoices still present old payee naming. 3) Invoice parser does not canonicalize payee names against supplier-entity alias table.

Actions taken so far: - Pulled sample object and confirmed s3 metadata 'normalized_filename' is truncated by lambda s3-metadata v0.9. - Queried supplier master data: supplier_id 7012 shows aliases ('TriLake LLC', 'TriLake Systems', 'TriLake Systems Inc'). supplier master has not been fully populated into the invoice-parser alias cache. - Temporarily added a manual alias mapping into invoice-parser cache and reprocessed a sample; PO match succeeded.

Open questions: - Should dedupe keys include checksum only and not filename? - Who owns s3-metadata lambda that truncates filenames? (tagged team: infra-storage)
Workarounds and next steps: 1) Short-term workaround: Finance has manually approved 8 invoices for the current run (payment scheduled). Approval ticket recorded in AP UI. 2) Hotfix: invoice-parser will be updated to prefer content checksum + vendor_tax_id + invoice_number as primary dedupe keys (PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/invoice-parser/pull/312). 3) Medium-term: infra-storage to remove filename truncation in s3-metadata lambda and preserve original filename in metadata; change request filed. 4) Data: sync supplier alias table and add canonicalization rules for legacy entity names; ops task created to backfill supplier aliases for supplier_id 7012 and other recently merged vendors.

Planned rollout: PR for parser change to be merged after tests (target 2026-03-13), infra change scheduled with CI gate for 2026-03-18. Finance will monitor next two payment runs for recurrence.
Ava Thompson (Support): Initial triage complete. Confirmed invoices on hold, extracted sample object and logs attached to ticket. Escalating to AP engineering and infra-storage.
Diego Martinez (AP Eng): I reproduced the failure locally. Invoice parser needs alias canonicalization. Created quick mapping to unblock one sample; will submit parser PR to change dedupe key order so we don't rely on filename. See PR link in related_github_prs.
Maya Patel (Infra-Storage): s3-metadata lambda truncation is an intentional historical limit (64 chars) set in 2019. I'll open an RFC to remove the truncation and keep original_filename metadata. ETA for change 2026-03-18 after infra review.
Liam O'Connor (Finance): We've approved the 8 invoices manually and scheduled the payment. Please flag if any more from TriLake appear in the next ingest batch.
Diego Martinez (AP Eng): Hotfix merged to staging. Will run a backfill job for invoices in HOLD_DUPLICATE_REVIEW that match supplier_id 7012 and TriLake alias list once infra approves metadata change.

title: Egress policy priority override rewrites SNI -> intermittent control-plane TLS auth failures on private deploy
body:
Egress policy priority override rewrites SNI -> intermittent control-plane TLS auth failures on private deploy

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent control-plane authentication failures from nodes in their private deployment. Failures manifest as short-lived TLS connection errors when the agent tries to authenticate to the Redwood control plane; subsequently the agent retries and eventually succeeds, but model-serving streaming sessions can drop during the window.

Impact:
- ~8% of control-plane connection attempts from the customer's serving fleet fail TLS auth intermittently over the past 36 hours, causing short reconnect flaps and a small but visible increase in 5xxs and stream resets for live traffic.
- No customer-visible data loss, but increased latencies and transient failures for streaming inference.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) with VPC peering to Redwood control plane region.
- Egress flows pass through customer-managed NGFW (vendor: FortiGate) and an egress NAT appliance that applies policy-based SNAT and header normalization.
- Agents: redwood-node-agent v1.4.6.
- Control plane endpoint: control.redwood-internal.net (VPCE + regional endpoints).

Steps to reproduce / diagnostics performed:
1) On a representative serving node we ran: 
   - curl --http2 -v https://control.redwood-internal.net/health -> intermittent TLS handshake failure with certificate subject mismatch logged.
   - openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-internal.net:443 -servername control.redwood-internal.net -> observed certificate for "internal-egress-gw.corp" on failing attempts.
   - tcpdump (port 443) captured ClientHello with SNI=control.redwood-internal.net, but Server Hello from egress device with cert CN=internal-egress-gw.corp.
2) Control-plane logs show TLS alert "handshake_failure" and agent auth failure entries around the same timestamps.
3) Packet capture shows occasional on-path TLS proxy rewriting the SNI in upstream flow (apparently due to a policy rule that normalizes host headers for HTTP virtual-hosting).

Observed logs (excerpt):
[agent] 2026-02-27T22:18:12Z TLS handshake failed: tls: remote error: handshake failure (alert 40)
[control] 2026-02-27T22:18:12Z auth: token exchange failed: certificate subject mismatch for host control.redwood-internal.net
tcpdump snippet: 
  ClientHello SNI: control.redwood-internal.net
  Server certificate CN: internal-egress-gw.corp

Initial hypothesis:
- Egress appliance is performing TLS interception or SNI rewrite for a subset of flows. A policy precedence change (recent firewall rule push) causes control-plane traffic to be routed through the appliance's host-based rewrite path, which rewrites or substitutes certs leading to client-side validation failures.

Why this is different from common split-horizon issues:
- DNS resolution is correct; SNI delivered by client is correct. The mismatch occurs after egress, where an appliance rewrites TLS metadata or terminates TLS for inspection and re-initiates TLS upstream with its own cert and SNI. The customer's egress policy recently added a "host normalization" rule that is applied before the VPC-peering exception, so control-plane traffic is sometimes treated as general HTTP traffic and gets rewritten.
2026-02-28T08:12: Support (Aisha Khan): Initial intake from BrightLedger SRE — intermittent TLS auth failures, attached packet captures and curl reproducer. Asked for a tcpdump and the output of 'openssl s_client -servername'.
2026-02-28T10:03: BrightLedger SRE (Jordan Meyers): Uploaded tcpdump (sensitive redacted). Noted that failing flows go via firewall instance fw-egress-02 with policy set 'global-host-normalize' applied at higher priority than 'redwood-vpce-exempt'.
2026-02-28T13:45: Networking Eng (Daniel Ortega): Confirmed with customer that firewall policy change was staged 2026-02-26 23:50 UTC. Requested firewall rule export and asked customer to test temporarily bypassing fw-egress-02 for control traffic.
2026-02-28T15:30: Customer (Jordan Meyers): Temporarily added route to steer control traffic around fw-egress-02 -> observed no TLS failures for 90 minutes of load testing. Reverted route after test.
Deep-dive performed by SRE and Networking:
- Verified policy precedence: 'global-host-normalize' is evaluated before the peering-exempt ACL due to a policy priority misconfiguration.
- Evidence: firewall logs show inbound flow to control.redwood-internal.net matched rule id 9012 (host-normalize) which explicitly rewrites Host header and performs TLS termination for HTTP inspection. Upstream re-SSL uses appliance cert CN=internal-egress-gw.corp and SNI internal-egress-gw.corp.
- Packet captures from the bypass test show clean handshake with control.redwood-internal.net cert when appliance is out of path.
- Correlated timestamps with control-plane auth logs showing certificate_subject_mismatch and auth retries.
- Risk analysis: long-lived grpc streams are fragile to mid-stream reconnects; even short control-plane auth flaps can trigger client library backoff and stream resets.
- Temporary mitigation tested: routing control-plane IPs through a dedicated NAT instance that does not run the host-normalize policy eliminated failures during test window.
- Engineering note: agent v1.4.6 will attempt up to 3 quick retries with exponential backoff; we observed a window where retries still resulted in stream resets.
Workarounds and remediation steps taken: 
1) Customer permanently lowered policy priority for 'global-host-normalize' and added an explicit higher-priority exception rule 'redwood-controlplane-exempt' that preserves SNI and bypasses TLS inspection for control.redwood-internal.net. Firewall rule change PR: https://github.com/brightledger/infra-config/pull/342
2) Customer updated SNAT mapping to preserve source IP for VPCE flows to avoid additional appliance hairpinning.
3) Redwood shipped agent patch v1.4.7 (cherry-picked) that improves TLS retry behavior and logs clearer SNI/cert mismatch diagnostics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/agents/pull/559). Patch applied as a rolling update to BrightLedger's nodes.
4) Post-rollback validation: 72-hour monitoring shows TLS auth failures dropped to 0.04% (from ~8%). Mean streaming error rate returned to baseline.

Follow-ups / action items: 
- Networking: add a runbook step in private-deploy onboarding to verify egress policy precedence and to advise adding 'controlplane-exempt' rules during initial firewall staging. (Owner: Daniel Ortega)
- DX/Docs: update private-deploy checklist to include an SNI-preservation verification step and sample iptables/tc commands to validate path. (Owner: Priya Shah)
- Customer success: schedule a short post-mortem call with BrightLedger to review firewall change controls and confirm monitoring thresholds. (Owner: Aisha Khan)

Final status: Issue mitigated and in monitoring. Customer applied firewall rule change and Redwood agent patch; no new TLS auth regressions observed in the follow-up window. Awaiting confirmation call with customer to close the ticket.

title: Sustained 5xx elevation caused by half-closed HTTP/2 sockets + cgroup CPU starvation on dedicated VPC
body:
Sustained 5xx elevation caused by half-closed HTTP/2 sockets + cgroup CPU starvation on dedicated VPC

Issue summary:
Customer Nimbus Health reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for their dedicated VPC tenant during steady traffic (mix of short chat and embedding requests). Errors manifested as API gateway 502/503/504s and frequent serving-runtime restarts for backends pinned to the customer's dedicated pool.

Impact:
- Customer-facing requests returned 5xx at ~8-12% of requests for a 90-minute window, causing multiple downstream app failures and an incident page alert.
- Affected both streaming and non-streaming routes.
- No billing discrepancy reported. Priority set to P1 due to customer SLA and critical workflows.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2026-03-09 14:05 UTC: Nimbus Health support pinged #support reporting elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects.
- 2026-03-09 14:12 UTC: Initial triage by CS; escalated to SRE and Dedicated-Team.
- 2026-03-09 14:30–15:55 UTC: Correlated spikes with large number of half-closed HTTP/2 streams from a specific app version in the customer's fleet.
- 2026-03-09 15:20 UTC: Observed repeated serving-runtime restarts on 3 dedicated GPU nodes.
- 2026-03-09 17:00 UTC: Mitigations applied (aggressively closed stale keepalives, temporary route weight reduction).
- 2026-03-09 18:50 UTC: 5xx rate returned to baseline; resolved and monitoring continued.

Steps to reproduce (investigation guidance):
1) Replay customer traffic on a staging cluster using the same HTTP/2 client behavior (long-lived streams with intermittent half-close).
2) Run a scripted fanout using short chat requests + embedding calls and artificially delay client RST/FIN to emulate half-closed sockets.
3) Observe apigw socket counts, epoll wake rates, and runtime fd counts while increasing concurrency to the customer baseline.

Investigation notes / evidence:
- API gateway metrics: accept-queue depth rose modestly but connection count with state "half-closed" spiked 7x for the tenant between 14:10–15:30 UTC.
- netstat and socket diagnostics on edge proxies showed many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT and FIN_WAIT2 tied to the tenant's source IPs.
- Serving-runtime logs showed repeated EMFILE and "too many open files" traces immediately prior to SIGTERM restarts on GPU nodes (see logs_snippets below).
- cgroups metrics (cpu.stat) for the dedicated pool showed very high throttling (nr_throttled increased) concurrent with a drop in runnable threads in the runtime process; CPU steal/pressure caused slow handling of epoll events.
- NVML/kernel logs: no GPU OOMs, but several guarded watchdog timeouts caused by mainloop starvation; dmesg showed some user-space watchdog kills where runtime failed liveness check.
- Heap and file descriptor analysis: runtime leaked FDs under heavy half-closed stream conditions (multiplexed HTTP/2), exacerbated by delayed client RST which prevented close() paths from running promptly.
- We observed interaction: half-closed sockets increased internal epoll wake storms, main thread started spinning on select/epoll with high syscall rate; when cgroup CPU throttling kicked in (due to noisy neighbor within dedicated pool), the runtime could not catch up processing close() and cleanup, leaving FDs accumulating until EMFILE and process restart.

Root cause (summary):
A chain of factors created the 5xx wave: (1) the customer's app version opened many multiplexed HTTP/2 streams and left sessions half-closed; (2) apigw and serving runtime code paths did not aggressively reclaim half-closed sockets under high FD pressure; (3) a late-occurring cgroup CPU throttle in the dedicated GPU pool slowed runtime cleanup, causing a runaway FD accumulation and subsequent EMFILE-induced restarts. The combination (half-closed socket accumulation + CPU throttling) produced the sustained elevated 5xx.

Mitigation & resolution applied:
- Short-term (within incident window):
  - Applied tenant-specific keepalive timeout reduction and enabled aggressive half-close reclamation on the apigw for Nimbus Health (reduces CLOSE_WAIT lifetime).
  - Temporarily reduced route weight to the dedicated pool to lower concurrency and give runtime headroom.
  - Restarted affected runtime processes sequentially to drain FD backlog and re-establish healthy state.
- Long-term (follow-up actions implemented):
  - Serving-runtime change merged to main branch to better detect and forcibly close stale half-closed streams after N seconds and to proactively release FD resources during high accept rates (PR referenced below).
  - Infrastructure tweak: adjust cgroup CPU cap/limits for dedicated pools and add a guard that raises an alert when nr_throttled rises above threshold for >30s.
  - CS/AM item: ask Nimbus Health to roll forward to client v2.3.1 which fixes a known HTTP/2 stream shutdown bug (they confirmed planning a rollout).

Current status and monitoring:
- Post-fix monitoring shows 5xx dropped back to baseline within 2 hours of mitigations and no further runtime restarts recorded for that tenant. We left a dedicated alert for the tenant that triggers at 3% 5xx for >5m.

Notes and evidence links:
- Grafana: /d/edge/tenant-traffic?orgId=1&var-tenant=Nimbus+Health (apigw conn states, 14:00–19:00 UTC)
- Runtime logs (obfuscated): https://internal-logs/redwood/nimbus/2026-03-09/runtime-rotated.log.gz
- Kernel logs from node-03: https://internal-logs/redwood/nimbus/2026-03-09/dmesg-node-03.txt

Follow-up items (owners):
- Serving runtime team: backport FD-reclamation change to the 2025.10 LTS branch and add unit tests (owner: Diego Morales).
- Infra/SRE: add cgroup-throttle alert and revise dedicated pool guardrails (owner: SRE team).
- CS: confirm customer rollout of client v2.3.1 and validate in staging after their upgrade (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Postmortem: publish short incident note in Confluence with timeline and RCA, link to fixes (owner: Incident Lead).
Deploy a serving runtime and apigw on a dedicated pool sized ~3 nodes
Use an HTTP/2 client that opens 100s of multiplexed streams per connection and intentionally delays RST/FIN (simulate client bug)
Ramp to customer-concurrency baseline (approx 150 concurrent streams), include embedding + chat mix
Observe apigw socket states (CLOSE_WAIT, FIN_WAIT2), runtime FD counts, and nr_throttled in cgroups
Trigger CPU burst on same cgroup (simulate noisy neighbor) to reproduce throttle and observe EMFILE/restarts
[2026-03-09T15:18:22Z] runtime ERROR: accept() succeeded but next close path failed: EMFILE (too many open files)
[2026-03-09T15:18:22Z] runtime WARN: fd_count=10240, fd_limit=10240, pending_cleanup=312
[node-03 dmesg 15:19] watchdog: task runtime_main: killed as it stalled for >30s
[apigw 15:14] conn_state: half-closed count for tenant Nimbus Health rose from 12->86 in 6m
2026-03-09 14:20 Aisha Patel (CS): Customer reports ~9% 5xx. Provided request ids and sample traces.
2026-03-09 14:33 Diego Morales (SRE): Observed elevated CLOSE_WAIT sockets tied to Nimbus source CIDR; escalating to infra and runtime teams.
2026-03-09 15:05 Infra Pager: cgroup throttling event for dedicated-pool-7. Investigating noisy neighbor.
2026-03-09 16:40 Diego Morales (SRE): Applied keepalive timeout reduction and route weight change. Seeing immediate drop in half-closed sockets.
2026-03-09 18:30 Aisha Patel (CS): Customer confirms stability after rolling client's fixed version to 20% of their fleet; will complete rollout by EOD.
2026-03-11 09:10 Diego Morales (SRE): Backport PR merged (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/401) and cgroup alert added to infra playbook. Marking incident resolved.
Mitigations (aggressive keepalive/half-close reclamation and route weight reduction) removed immediate pressure. Root-cause fix deployed to serving-runtime (FD reclamation) and infra alerting added; customer upgraded client. Incident closed after 48h of stable telemetry.

title: Elevated time-to-first-token for short-chat payloads after runtime 2.3.1 + model repin
body:
Elevated time-to-first-token for short-chat payloads after runtime 2.3.1 + model repin

Issue summary:
Elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) observed for short chat prompts (<32 tokens) from LuminaApps on the Hosted API after the runtime 2.3.1 deploy and model repin performed 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.

Impact:
- A subset of customer chat sessions see 1.0–3.5s additional delay to first token.
- Affects primarily small prompts and bursty traffic patterns; medium/long prompts show normal tail latency.
- Customer reports degraded UX for chat snippets used in search/autocomplete flows.

Environment:
- Hosted API (prod) in us-east-1, customer using dedicated pool with session-affinity.
- Runtime: 2.3.1 (rolled 2026-03-09), Model repin to redwood-2.0 (quantized variant) at same window.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send short chat completion request (system + single-turn user prompt ~8–16 tokens) via Hosted API with session affinity header.
2) Observe websocket/HTTP streaming start time and time-to-first-token metric.
3) Repeat at scale (50–200 qps) to reproduce bursty behavior.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- api-gw logs: upstream_connect_time spike correlated with 504s early, but most requests return 200 with delayed first-token.
- edge-proxy: TLS handshake durations stable; occasional renegotiation entries for connections with affinity to pool-a.
- serving-runtime: increased per-request setup time before KV cache warm path (~800ms per affected request).
- session-manager: affinity mapping shows 18% of user sessions sent to a new runtime shard (shard-7) after repin.

Temporary workaround attempted by Support:
- Forced customer traffic to a stable pool via temporary routing override (re-routed to pool-b). Observed immediate reduction in TTFB for affected sessions.
- Scoped rate-limit on pool-a to reduce burst pressure; partial improvement.

Notes: This is not a full outage and does not generate widespread 5xxs. Reproducible via short prompts + session affinity and burst pattern.
